# The review register

This register is the evidence behind optmat's data and models. It records every
transcribed value, every correction of a printed value, every choice made in fitting and
every question left open, with what was checked, against what, and when. Code, data
records and documentation cite its entries by number (`TC-92`); the manual page *The
review register* explains how to read it and how entries are added.

Each entry is numbered `TC-n` (originally "to check"). Numbers become permanent on
`main`; branch-only numbers are provisional until integration. Established entries
are never renumbered or removed; later entries correct or supersede earlier ones and
say so. Entries follow the order in which the work was done, so an entry's code and
data locations are those of its day where it describes the data format, and the present
ones where it names a module or a file.

The curation was done by J. C. Travers working with AI agents. Most records were
transcribed and checked by an agent at extraction and reviewed by a second curator, an
agent or J. C. Travers; the decisions on data, fits and conventions are his. "At
extraction" and "a second curator" below refer to this division of the work.

Status: `open`, `verified (date)`, `corrected (date)`, `decided (date)`.

## TC-1: real-gas densities from the equation of state's compressibility factor

- **Where:** `optmat.gas.eos.number_density`, `optmat.gas.eos.compressibility`.
- **Claim:** the real-gas density is formed as `p / (Z k_B T)` with CoolProp's `Z`,
  not from its mass density, because several CoolProp equations carry older gas
  constants (argon and nitrogen: R = 8.31451 J/(mol K)) that put their mass densities
  5.7e-6 from the CODATA ideal gas at vanishing pressure (measured 2026-09-24 at 10 Pa,
  273.15 K: Ar 0.9999944, N2 0.9999943, H2 0.9999988, He 1.0000003).
- **Consequence for solprop:** `solprop.physdata.equation_of_state` uses the mass
  density, so its argon and nitrogen densities carry this 5.7e-6 offset (for the solprop
  integration).
- **Status:** open.

## TC-2: Edlen 1966 standard-air dispersion formula

- **Where:** `optmat.conditions.standard_air_refractivity`.
- **Claim:** `1e8 (n - 1) = 8342.13 + 2406030 / (130 - s^2) + 15997 / (38.9 - s^2)`,
  `s` the vacuum wavenumber in um^-1, for dry air with 0.03 % CO2 at 15 degrees C and
  101 325 Pa (B. Edlen, Metrologia 2, 71 (1966)). Transcribed from memory: the paper is
  not in the curators' library (cited by Smith 1976 and Zhang 2008). It is used only to
  convert standard-air wavelengths (Leonard 1974 Table II, Cuthbertson) to vacuum, where a
  1e-7 error in n - 1 moves a wavelength by 1e-7 relative and a refractivity by ~1e-9.
- **Status:** verified (2026-09-24, source `edlen_1966`): the package's formula is
  Edlen's Eq. (1) exactly, coefficients, variable and reference state.

## TC-3: Huber & Tondello (1974), helium 92-190 nm

- **Where:** `data/sources/huber_1974.toml`, `tools/extract/huber_1974.py`.
- **Transcribed:** Table I (tbl_6b16f76840f9), 11 rows: the experimental column
  (primary) and the theoretical column (Victor et al., reproduced), x1e-5, vacuum
  Angstrom, 0 degrees C and 760 Torr ("NPT"; the reduction method is not stated, so
  `density = "unknown"`).
- **Uncertainty:** "the probable error in the best-fit curve is smaller than +-3 %"
  (p. 391), read as a probable error of 3 % (1.48 x 3 % one sigma). The table lists the
  smoothed best-fit curve, not the individual measurements.
- **Status:** open.

## TC-4: Bideau-Mehu et al. (1981), Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe 140-254 nm

- **Where:** `data/sources/bideau_mehu_1981.toml`, `tools/extract/bideau_mehu_1981.py`.
- **Structural fixes:** the captions in the curators' extraction are wrong for three
  tables (checked on the images): tbl_804a29eb8dd3 = Table 2 neon, tbl_7062fe0f03a9
  (captioned "Table 5 Xenon") = Table 4 krypton, tbl_7ab7e916e7b3 = Table 5 xenon. The
  raised dots marking other authors' extrapolated values, lost in the extracted CSVs,
  were read from the images and those cells are not extracted; Chashchina & Shreider's
  xenon values below 155 nm are also dropped as extrapolations because the text says
  they stopped measuring at 155 nm.
- **Uncertainty:** 0.5 % for Ne, Ar, Kr and 0.3 % for Xe (1 % at 149.5 and 148.3 nm),
  level not stated; the paper gives "about 0.5 % for neon to 0.3 % for xenon", so Ar and
  Kr were given 0.5 %, the bound of the stated range. To confirm: this reading.
- **Reduction:** 0 degrees C, 760 Torr, real gas (van der Waals for Ne, Kr, Xe;
  Hilsenrath for Ar).
- **Erratum:** fit_Ne at 253.7 nm, printed 69.60, corrected 68.60 (the formula gives
  68.60 and reproduces every other row).
- **Formulas:** Ne corrected (B1 182.90 -> 1.8290, lambda^-1 -> lambda^-2); Xe corrected
  (C2 50.578 -> 59.578); Ar reproduces its column; **Kr does not** (0.1-0.7 % low, no
  single coefficient explains it; left as printed). The upper ends of the formulas'
  ranges (546.1, 567.7, 623.4, 670.8 nm) are the longest wavelengths of the literature
  data the authors joined, taken from refractiveindex.info's entries: to check.
- **Heddle column:** Ref. 19's argon values (332.0, 336.0 at 184.9, 180.7 nm) are not
  Heddle et al.'s published 325 and 328 x 1e-6 at 1850 and 1805 A.
- **Status:** open.

## TC-5: Ermolov et al. (2015) helium formula and its reference state

- **Where:** `data/sources/ermolov_2015.toml`.
- **Transcribed:** Table I coefficients from the table image (the header row was lost in
  extraction): B = 2.16463e-5, 2.10561e-7, 4.75093e-5; C = -6.8077e-4, 5.13251e-3,
  3.18621e-3; Eq. (3), rho relative to 1 bar at 273 K (read as 273.15 K).
- **Finding:** referred to 1 bar as printed, the formula lies 1.3 % above Mansfield &
  Peck, Borzsonyi and every refractiveindex.info helium entry from the UV to the near
  infrared; referred to 1 atm it agrees with them (gallery, helium page). solprop's
  reading (1 atm) matches the data; the paper's stated state does not. To confirm
  (with an author of the paper): which state the fit was made at.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-25): follow the data, the formula is a 1 atm fit (an
  author of the paper cannot recall the fit's state; the 1 bar in the paper is presumably
  an error). solprop's reading stands.

## TC-8 mansfield_peck_1969 (identity unverified)

- Transcribed: Table I tbl_aae92dff687e (extracted cells, no CSV; image checked): 13
  fitted He points (`experiment`, x1e-9, vacuum A, 1 atm 0 C, real gas via White's
  virial Z) and the two parenthesised, footnote-a points 9660.434 and 15300.153 A
  (`experiment_excluded`). Deviation column not extracted.
- Table II tbl_330bf663e80e (image): 20 oscillator strengths (reproduced; row ids name
  the upper state; the CSV merges series labels into the sum rows).
- Tables III (Koch 1913, Cuthbertson 1932 at 5462.258 A), IV (Korwin, present calc,
  Musulin-Epstein, Karplus-Kolker, Migneron-Levinger at 5500 A), VI (six static
  polarizabilities, x1e-24 cm3): one dataset per author (images checked).
- Uncertainty: per point 0.29e-9 rms (Eq. 4 residual), systematic 0.26 % (the paper's
  "liberal" +-0.009e-5 at the green line, taken as one sigma: the level to confirm).
- Erratum: Table II 1s4p wavenumber 19.4195 -> 19.1495 (digit transposition; Rydberg
  fit to the paper's n = 5-10 gives 19.150).
- Formulas: Eqs. 1-4 (experiment) reproduce Table I (rms 0.63/0.41/0.53/0.38e-9 vs quoted
  0.57/0.42/0.36/0.29); Eq. 3 static limit gives Table VI's 6.462 exactly (so its "+" is
  right). Eq. 7 sign misprint ("-" -> "+") and Eq. 8 missing "+": corrected forms agree
  with each other (3.49784 at 5462 A) and give Table VI's 6.468; the paper's own 3.4976
  (Table IV) is 7e-5 lower, unexplained.
- Doubts: Table I's deviation column reproduces from no version of Eq. 4 (sign appears
  flipped); text says (2s,np) sum from n = 7 is 0.00122, table prints 0.00137 (left
  as printed); Table IV "0.02 %" does not follow from its numbers; Tables V, VII, VIII
  (derived F values, Becquerel constants, Verdet constants with no power of ten) not
  extracted. Source id is `mansfield_peck_1969`, not the `<first author>_<year>` rule
  (`mansfield_1969`).
- **Status:** open.

## TC-25 borzsonyi_2008 (Borzsonyi et al., Appl. Opt. 47, 4856 (2008))

- Transcribed: Table 1 (`tbl_15ed1378c327`, JSON cells only: the curators' extraction
  has no CSV for it; read through the helper `tools/extract/_json_table.py`), SGD /
  SGDD / STOD with their +- errors for N2, He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe (air skipped): 18
  one-point datasets. Compared with the table image: all cells as printed.
- State: 1000 mbar and the per-gas 'Temperature of Meas.' (19.4-20.8 C); the caption
  says '20 C'. Density = real (measured at the state, not reduced). Wavelength 800 nm
  vacuum (omega0 = 2.35 fs^-1, p. 4). Level of the +- errors not stated.
- SGD is the excess over vacuum ((n_g - 1)/c; He 146 fs/m): recorded as
  `parameters.excess_over_vacuum = true`. The vocabulary's `group_delay` does not say
  whether 1/c is included: **to be defined**.
- **Doubt, SGD set to `use = "check"`**: every SGD is 22-39 fs/m above what the
  refractivity implies (He 146.0 printed vs about 108 expected from its n - 1 known
  to 0.1 %). Probably a common additive offset; unverifiable. SGDD kept primary; STOD
  is an upper limit only (p. 5): `check`.
- Lorentz-Lorenz constants (m^3/kg) not extracted: their derivation is not given and
  2/3 (n - 1)/rho does not reproduce N2's.
- Formulas: six Sellmeier fits (Eq. 14, Table 2 `tbl_8d505c3d8e77`, image checked),
  ideal-gas (p/p0)(T0/T) scaling of n^2 - 1, p0 = 1000 mbar, T0 = 273 K (text) /
  0 C (caption). Fitted to three literature n (Leonard / Peck-Khanna / CRC) plus the
  SGDD only. Checks at 546.2258 nm (0 C, 1013.25 mbar): N2 299.15 (PK 299.14),
  He 34.88, Ne 67.24, Ar 282.46, Kr 430.71 against Leonard's Table I. At 800 nm the

## TC-43: the helium formula of Wilmouth & Sayres (2020) and He et al. (2021) is a 0 degrees C formula

- **Where:** `he_2021.toml` and `wilmouth_2020.toml`, formula `He_table1`.
- **Claim:** both papers list `(n - 1) x 10^8 = 2283 + 1.8102e13 / (1.5342e10 - nu^2)` as
  the refractivity at 288.15 K and 1013.25 hPa. It gives 3489.3e-8 at 546.2 nm, which is
  helium's refractivity at **0 degrees C** (Stone's formula: 3486.9e-8; Mansfield & Peck
  3495.0e-8); at 15 degrees C helium's is 3305.5e-8. Read at the stated 15 degrees C, the
  formula is 5.5 % high (the ratio 288.15/273.15), and a Rayleigh cross section computed
  from it about 11 % high. The formula is recorded as printed (state 1atm_15C); the
  gallery's helium page shows the offset. Whether the papers' helium cross sections carry
  the error is outside this package's scope.
- **Status:** open.

## TC-44: Mansfield & Peck (1969) lie 0.25 % above modern helium theory

- **Where:** gallery, helium page.
- **Observation:** Stone & Stejskal's molar refractivity (theory to 1e-6), Liu's ab
  initio polarizabilities, Cuthbertson 1932, Smith 1976, Victor's theory and the static
  polarizabilities agree with each other; Mansfield & Peck's absolute scale, the basis of
  most helium Sellmeier formulas (Borzsonyi fitted to Leonard, who adopted it), is
  0.25 % higher, inside its own stated systematic (+-0.009e-5 of 3.4950e-5, 0.26 %). The
  proposed fits take Mansfield & Peck's *relative* dispersion with a free scale.
- **Status:** decided and closed (2026-09-24/25): the relative dispersion with a free
  scale.

## TC-62: format gaps met

- Tables with merged cells in the curators' extraction have no CSV; every script that
  needs them has a local `grid()` reading `tables/<id>.json` (8 copies of the same 10
  lines): `_library.table` could read the JSON.
- A refractivity dataset must imply 0.5 < alpha < 400 a.u. (test): negative n - 1
  (x-ray, above a resonance: Liggett Tables IV-V, Mahon Table I, Kr at Lyman alpha)
  and Gill's Xe 172e-4 cannot be stored.
- No quantity for a phase mismatch per atom (Mahon's C, L'Huillier's Delta k).
- Oscillator strengths need a wavelength; papers that name levels only (Ferrell,
  Liggett) cannot be stored.
- Per-row use/exclusion is impossible, so single points are split into their own
  datasets (Leonard's Larsen 4108 A, Rusch 67628.5 A).
- **Status:** open.

## TC-71: refraction measures alpha + chi_0; theory and dielectric data give alpha alone

- **Where:** `optmat.gas.fitting`; raised from Lesiuk et al. 2020 and 2023.
- **Claim:** at optical and microwave frequencies n^2 = eps mu, so a refractivity measures
  the electric polarizability plus the (diamagnetic) magnetic susceptibility chi_0 of
  the atom, while an ab initio alpha(omega) and a dielectric-constant (capacitance, DCGT)
  measurement give the electric polarizability alone. Lesiuk gives chi_0 = -2.30e-4 a.u.
  for argon (-21 ppm of alpha) and -8.484(19)e-5 a.u. for neon (-32 ppm); helium's is of
  order -2e-5 a.u. (-1.5e-5 of alpha; value to be taken from Puchalski et al. 2016). The
  fits model the refractive polarizability alpha + chi_0 and add chi_0 to every
  electric-only value (theory, dielectric) before fitting; each such dataset is marked in
  its fit configuration. At the level of Borzsonyi or Bideau-Mehu (1e-3) this is
  invisible; at the level of Puchalski, Lesiuk, Gaiser and Peck & Fisher it is not.
- **Status:** open (to be implemented in the fits).

## TC-72: Kumar & Thakkar (2010) dipole sums are fitted to refractivity data already here

- **Where:** `kumar_2010.toml`.
- **Claim:** the DOSDs were constrained by refractivities from Cuthbertson 1932, Smith 1976,
  Bideau-Mehu 1981 (in this package) and Hohm, Coulon (not), so fitting their S(k)
  beside those datasets would count the same data twice. The S(k) datasets are therefore
  used as validators (`check`) in the fits, not as data (a reversible decision).
- **Status:** open.

## TC-73: argon's absolute level: Peck & Fisher +3.5e-4 and Zhang +2.6e-4 above theory and metrology

- **Where:** `data/gas/fits/Ar.toml`, `fit/Ar`.
- **Observation:** Lesiuk & Jeziorski's ab initio moments (S(-2) to 1.7e-4), the
  dielectric (DCGT) static polarizability of Gaiser & Fellmuth (2.4e-6, via Lesiuk) and
  Egan's refractometry at 632.99 nm (1.5e-5, via Lesiuk) agree with each other, and
  Birch 1991 at 633 nm lies -53 ppm from them. Against that level, Peck & Fisher's 17
  points lie a uniform +353 ppm high (their stated systematic <= 2e-4) and Zhang et al.'s
  800 nm comb value +265 ppm (stated 2.3e-5). The fit takes Peck & Fisher's shape with a
  free scale (their shape residuals are at their 4e-6 rms) and Zhang as a validator. The
  Borzsonyi-family argon formulas, fitted to Leonard's (Peck-based) level, are 0.1-0.15 %
  high in the visible; Luna's legacy Kingston fit rises several per cent above the fit
  below 150 nm.
- **Status:** confirmed (2026-09-25): Peck & Fisher's shape with a free scale, Zhang a validator.

## TC-74: argon vacuum-ultraviolet sources used as validators

- **Where:** `data/gas/fits/Ar.toml`.
- **Observation:** Gill & Heddle's Rayleigh value at 121.6 nm is 11 % above the fit, and
  Heddle et al.'s Cerenkov values -2 % (180, 185 nm) and +8 % (121 nm); Chopra & Heddle
  (Rayleigh, 121.6 nm, normalised to a calculated H2 cross section) -1.6 %; Ferrell's
  third-harmonic values +0.1 to -1.7 %. All are validators, not fitted: broad bandpass
  (Cerenkov), sign-blind and normalised (Rayleigh), or no stated per-point uncertainty
  (Ferrell). Bideau-Mehu (140-254 nm, 0.5 %) and Gordon (111-115 nm, 5 %) are fitted and
  agree within their errors. Chashchina's smoothed values (via Bideau-Mehu) lie 0.05-0.5
  % below the fit.
- **Status:** open.

## TC-89: Mansfield & Peck's helium dispersion departs from ab initio theory by 1e-4

  & Peck's 13 points lie +108, +110 and +69 ppm (480-546 nm) and -18 to -47 ppm (0.72-2.06
  um) from the model built on Puchalski et al.'s coefficients: their relative dispersion
  between 480 and 546 nm is about 2 % off theory, where theory is good to 1e-5. They are
  fitted with a 1e-4 allowance added to their 8e-6 stated precision, which leaves them
  without influence on a model fixed by theory.

## TC-90: classical helium refractometry scatters by +-0.3 % about theory

## TC-91: the helium model in the vacuum ultraviolet

- **Where:** `fit/He`.
- **Observation:** below 90 nm the model rests on Puchalski's high-order coefficients
  (S(-10) ... S(-16) are nonrelativistic, with estimated correction allowances) and the
  NIST 1s2p and 1s3p lines; its stated uncertainty is 3 ppm at 83 nm, 24 ppm at 70 nm and
  0.08 % at 61 nm. Liu's independent (infinite-mass, nonrelativistic) calculation departs
  smoothly from it, -411 ppm at long wavelength (the mass and relativistic correction)
  to -0.16 % at 65 nm and -0.8 % at 60.75 nm, the growth the shift of the resonance pole
  implies. The fitted 1s2p oscillator strength is 0.2767(8) (NIST 0.27625, AAA).
- **Status:** open.

## TC-92: neon's dispersion: experiment against ab initio theory (2.5 sigma)

- **Where:** `data/gas/fits/Ne.toml`, `fit/Ne` (reduced chi-squared 2.5).
- **Observation:** Lesiuk et al.'s S(-4) = 2.850(7) and S(-6) = 4.932(14) (with S(-2) =
  2.66080(36)) give less dispersion than every experiment-constrained source: the fit to
  the Cuthbertsons' visible shape alone wants S(-4) = 2.868; Kumar & Thakkar's DOSD
  (constrained by refractivities) has 2.875 with S(-2) = 2.669, Langhoff & Karplus 2.863;
  relative to the static term the experiments' S(-4)/S(-2) is 0.6 % above theory's.
  Bideau-Mehu's VUV values lie +1 to +2 % above the theory-constrained model at 140-152
  nm (sigma 0.5 %). For argon, theory (Lesiuk 2023) and Peck & Fisher's shape agree.
  The fit keeps every stated uncertainty and scales its band by the reduced chi-squared.
  **Question:** trust the ab initio dispersion (inflate the old
  data's errors) or the experiments (inflate the theory's dynamic terms)?
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-25): keep the ab initio backbone; the two experimental routes (refractometry above, photoabsorption below, TC-126) bracket it; the working estimate 0.3 % covers the spread.

## TC-93: helium and neon refractometry systematically high (a contamination hypothesis)

- **Observation:** against theory-anchored fits, classical values for the light gases lie
  high: helium Birch +0.32 %, Cuthbertson 1910 +0.24 %, Mansfield & Peck +0.23 %,
  Achtermann +0.20 %, Orcutt & Cole +0.34 %; neon Birch +0.14 %, Orcutt & Cole +0.33 %,
  Cuthbertson 1932 +0.32 %; for argon Birch is -0.01 %. A trace of a heavier gas raises a
  light gas's refractivity strongly (0.03 % of air in helium adds about 0.24 % to its
  n - 1), which would explain the sign and the size. A hypothesis only; it is why the
  fits take these values' shapes, not their levels.
- **Status:** open.

## TC-94: krypton and xenon rest on single static anchors and old dispersion data

- **Where:** `fit/Kr`, `fit/Xe`.
- **Observation:** the curators' library has no ab initio dispersion for Kr or Xe; their
  levels rest on dielectric static polarizabilities (Huot & Bose 1991 as reproduced by
  Kumar & Thakkar 2010, Orcutt & Cole 1967 for Kr) and Birch's 633 nm value (Kr), their
  shapes on Smith 1976 (Kr), Bideau-Mehu 1981 and the Cuthbertsons (level free). Both
  fits have reduced chi-squared below 0.7. Leonard's recommended 546 nm values lie +0.05 %
  (Kr) and +0.14 % (Xe) above the fits; Huot & Bose's Kr value is 2.8 sigma from Orcutt &
  Cole and Birch. The magnetic susceptibilities are not in the curators' library and are
  neglected (about -25 ppm of alpha). Useful additions: ab initio dispersion coefficients
  for Kr and Xe, their chi_0, Hohm & Kerl 1990 and Hohm & Thakkar 2012 (static values).
- **Status:** open.

## TC-95: the molecular fits (N2, H2, D2, O2)

- **Where:** `data/gas/fits/{N2,H2,D2,O2}.toml`.
- **N2** (reduced chi-squared 1.1): Griesmann's VUV (level free, calibrated on Abjean),
  Peck & Khanna, Birch, Stone, Achtermann, Zhang, Newell, Orcutt & Cole and Marchetti agree
  to their uncertainties; effective oscillators only (N2 has no infrared-active mode).
- **H2** (reduced chi-squared 0.8, Newell a validator): the absolute level is contested at 1e-3.
  Relative to the fit, Rychlewski's ab initio thermal average is -450 ppm and Bishop &
  Cheung's -200 ppm (the two theories differ by 0.17 %, which is the allowance given to
  theory), Peck & Huang -1000 ppm (their scale is fitted with its 3.1e-4 prior: -3.3
  sigma), Achtermann +140 ppm (reliable for Ar and N2, 10 sigma high for He), Orcutt &
  Cole +744 ppm, Newell -1370 ppm (a validator). The temperature dependence of H2's
  rotationally averaged polarizability is not modelled (theory at 293 K, data at 273-323
  K). A modern ab initio H2 alpha(omega) with its uncertainty would settle it.
- **D2**: Rychlewski's theory, and since TC-96 Shelton's D2/H2 and H2/D2 ratios; Orr's
  1936 value (+0.2 %) inherits an outdated H2 refractivity.
- **O2** (reduced chi-squared 0.2): above the Schumann-Runge bands only (195 nm); Zhang's
  800 nm value is -482 ppm (12 sigma; Kren's A-band criticism). Kumar & Thakkar's sums
  (constrained by Smith's and Stoll's refractivities) against the fit with Shelton's N2/O2
  ratio (TC-96): S(-2) -0.03 %, S(-4) +0.55 %, S(-6) -6 %, S(-8) -1 % (before the ratio:
  -0.01, -0.7, -3.1, +3.1 %); the high moments hang on the lowest pseudo-oscillator
  (155 nm, the Schumann-Runge region) and two oscillators do not fix them.
- **CH4, SF6, N2O** are not fitted: the curators' library holds no direct dispersion data
  for them beyond single visible or 633 nm values (Achtermann, Birch, Swift, Cuthbertson
  1914 for N2O) and Rayleigh-derived formulas; their infrared bands need band intensities
  (HITRAN) that are not curated. The papers that would supply them are not in the
  curators' library.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-25): put hydrogen on theory: Raj et al.'s 293 K average fitted with a 0.1 % allowance (the spread of the three calculations), the experiments' levels free or prior-limited (TC-101).

## TC-96: Shelton's phase-matching density ratios as fit observations

- **Where:** `optmat.gas.fitting._ratio`, `data/gas/fits/{Ne,N2,H2,D2,Kr,Xe,O2}.toml`,
  `optmat.gas.crosschecks`.
- **What:** each ratio `rho_gas / rho_ref = Delta alpha_ref / Delta alpha_gas`
  (`Delta alpha = alpha(2 omega) - alpha(omega)`) is fitted in the gas whose dispersion it
  constrains, with the partner held at its recommended model (fits are run in dependency
  order: He and Ar first, then Ne, N2, H2, Kr, Xe, then O2 and D2). Resulting reduced
  chi-squared: Ne 2.6 (He/Ne 1.4 and 1.6 sigma, the TC-92 tension again), N2 1.15
  (He/N2), H2 0.76, D2 0.25, Kr 0.80, Xe 0.68, O2 0.19.
- **Argon against Shelton:** Shelton's ratios are self-consistent to 0.02 %
  (He/N2 x N2/Ar = He/Ar), but the argon model (Lesiuk & Jeziorski's ab initio moments)
  gives a He/Ar ratio 0.31 % and 0.32 % below Shelton's (1.9 and 1.2 sigma). Fitted in N2,
  the 0.02 % N2/Ar ratio drags nitrogen onto that difference (reduced chi-squared 1.1 to
  1.76, Peck & Khanna's chi-squared 16 to 26), so **N2/Ar is a validator** of `fit/N2`
  (-0.11 %). To check: whether Shelton's He/Ar (or the whole argon-referenced set:
  Ar/Kr, Ar/Xe) carries a 0.3 % systematic, or the argon dispersion at 1.3 um does.
- **D2** needed 20 starting points (`[model] starts`, new): with the default six, one
  effective oscillator stayed at zero strength (chi-squared 8605). The other fits give the
  same minimum with 20 starts (He and Ar lower by 0.13 and 0.03 in chi-squared).
- **Status:** open.

## TC-101: robustness of the fits (leave one dataset out) and their near-degenerate minima

- **Where:** `tools/fit/robustness.py`, `data/gas/models/robustness/*.json`, gallery
  *Robustness*.
- **Single-dataset levels:** hydrogen's level rests on Achtermann's 633 nm value alone
  (without it the fit moves -870 ppm, 18 sigma of the stated 47 ppm, towards Peck & Hung
  and the ab initio values; TC-95), and oxygen's on Birch's (-840 ppm, 10 sigma of 79
  ppm). The stated uncertainty band reflects that one measurement, not the spread of the
  levels. Open question: widen those values' allowance (or add a level
  uncertainty to the model), or accept the metrology as it stands.
- **By design:** the backbones move their models by many sigma when dropped (helium's
  Puchalski moments 2151 sigma, neon's DCGT 20, argon's Lesiuk moments 9 and DCGT 6,
  deuterium's Rychlewski 49, xenon's Bideau-Mehu 16 near its range's short end, oxygen's
  Smith 114 at 205 nm); every other dataset moves its model by less than 4.3 sigma, most
  by less than 2.
- **Minima:** the fits' cost has near-degenerate minima (a far effective oscillator enters
  only through f/E^2). More starting points find slightly lower ones: helium chi-squared
  37.97 against 38.10 with its fourth oscillator driven to infinity (its covariance then
  singular), argon 19.60 against 19.63, neon 52.55 against 54.65 with an oscillator on
  the first resonance. They differ from the stored fits by at most 0.44 sigma of the
  model anywhere in range, so the stored fits stand; a global search (variable projection
  over the effective energies) would make the minimum unique. The robustness refits start
  from the full solution (`fit(..., start=)`) so that they measure the dataset.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-25): hydrogen's level moves to the ab initio calculations (TC-95); oxygen's is resolved by Egan 2026 (TC-147).

## TC-103: the dispersion uncertainty of the fits, statistical against empirical

- **Where:** `optmat.gas.models.fitted.FittedModel.dispersion_sigma_relative`,
  `optmat.gas.models.oscillator.OscillatorModel.dispersion_au`,
  `docs/accuracy.md` (its table checked by `tests/test_accuracy_page.py`), gallery
  *Dispersion uncertainty*, the GVD shifts added to `data/gas/models/robustness`.
- **Finding:** the covariance-propagated GVD uncertainty is a lower bound. Adding Shelton's
  ratios (TC-96) moved the 800 nm GVD of krypton by +1.0 % (8 statistical sigma), oxygen
  +0.95 % (6), deuterium +0.42 % (26) and xenon +0.35 % (3); leaving one dataset out moves
  nitrogen's and hydrogen's GVD by 0.2 % (17 and 8 sigma). A ratio-fitted gas also
  inherits its partner's uncertainty, which its covariance lacks.
- **Working estimates:** the page's "working estimate" column (He < 0.01 %, Ne 0.3 %,
  Ar 0.05 %, Kr 1 %, Xe 0.4 %, N2 and H2 0.2 %, D2 0.3 %, O2 1 % at 800 nm) is a
  judgement from both measures. At 800 nm solprop's formulas for neon,
  hydrogen and oxygen lie within these estimates of the fits, those for krypton close to
  it, the others well outside.
- **Also:** the assessment's formula table rows for Ne, Kr and Xe were stale (from before
  the ratio refits) and were recomputed.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-25): the working estimates accepted; columns at 343 and 1800 nm to be added.

  `tbl_b0cae9bc8235`) and T5 (D2, `tbl_3f331311ba2d`), the diagonal columns
  <0,0|alpha|0,0> and <1,0|alpha|1,0>, 53 rows each (52 laser wavelengths in nm and
  "Static"); main Table II (`tbl_aa58a97e916a`, JSON), the H2 293 K thermal average
  "Our", 15 rows. Inputs read (not stored): Tables T26 (`tbl_8f44df72c173` S0/O1,
  `tbl_db455a894d4d` Q1/S1) and T29 (`tbl_7c62aa367012`), the "Our" transition energies.
- **Computed, not printed**: the authors' own module
  `rovibME.py` (SHA-256 75823f2e..., files dated 24 Jan 2018, from a local copy of the
  authors' GitHub repository `H2-PolarizabilityMatrixElements`) run
  unmodified by `tools/extract/_raj_2018_program.py` in a pinned uv script environment
  (Python 3.11.16, NumPy 1.24.4, SciPy 1.10.1) because it fails under NumPy 2 and calls
  `scipy.integrate.quadrature` (removed in SciPy 1.15). Per-state <0,J|alpha|0,J>, J =
  0-10, H2 and D2, at T1's 53 wavelengths: 22 files `raj_2018__program_J*.csv`
  (`raj_2018.py --program`, about one minute). Then normal H2 / normal D2 averages at
  273.15, 293.15, 296.15 K (6 files, `extract()`).
- **Decisions**:
  1. *Normal* gas = spin species in the high-temperature ratio (H2 para:ortho 1:3, D2
     ortho:para 2:1), each Boltzmann within its own levels; so only energies within each
     parity chain are needed (T26/T29's S0 give them; no S0 connects odd and even J).
     Equilibrium at 293.15 K differs by at most 1.4e-5 a.u. for H2 (HITRAN E(J=1)).
  2. **D2 spin weights 6:3 have no directly stated numeric source for D2**: the curators'
     library has "the spin of the D nucleus is I_N = 1, so that for the D2 molecule, even
     j states are twice as populated as odd j" (an unverified copy, Chen et al. 2007
     by its file name, PDF p. 15; the same page wrongly says H2 even j are 3x odd) and
     "equals 6 for even j and 3 for odd j" for two spin-1 nuclei (Borysow et al. 2019,
     14N2, PDF p. 8). HITRAN has no D2. The 6:3 weights also reproduce Rychlewski's D2
     average (rychlewski_1983 notes). H2 1:3: Bishop & Cheung (1980) text after Eq. (23)
     and HITRAN's g'' (HITRAN API 2026-09-25, isotopologue 103).
  3. v = 0 only (v = 1 population < 5e-7 at 296.15 K from Q1(0)); J <= 10 (D2 J = 9
     holds 1.7e-5 of its species at 296.15 K, J = 10 1.3e-6).
  4. `use`: normal_293K primary (H2 and D2), the other temperatures and everything else
     check. For H2 it is a third ab initio set beside Rychlewski and Bishop.
  5. The environment for the authors' module is a tool environment (uv inline script
     metadata, pinned old NumPy/SciPy), not a project dependency.
- **Checks passed**: every computed <0,0|alpha|0,0> rounds to T1/T5's printed value
  (106 values, asserted in `extract()`); S0 agrees with S1 - Q1 and Q1 - O1 of the same
  tables to 7e-4 cm^-1 (asserted to 1e-3); the paper's own Table II average reproduced
  to 4e-5 a.u. at all 15 wavelengths; five states identical in a second, independent
  environment (Python 3.9, NumPy 1.21, SciPy 1.7.3).
- **Comparison at 293 K** (`raj_2018.py --compare`, T = 293.0 K, the program's range
  182.25-1320.7 nm only): Bishop & Cheung H2, 16 wavelengths: -0.015 % (static) to
  +0.146 % (185.46 nm), mean +0.043 %; Rychlewski H2, 14: +0.007 to +0.057 %, mean
  +0.030 %; Rychlewski D2, 14: +0.015 to +0.055 %, mean +0.031 %.
- **D2/H2 dispersion**: the ESHG phase-match density ratio D2/H2 computed from these
  averages (295.15 K; one-off program run at the 9 fundamentals and harmonics, not
  stored) is 1.0317-1.0345 against Shelton & Mizrahi's measured 1.0301-1.0319
  (shelton_1986/ratio_D2_H2): 0.0009-0.0026 high (1.3-10 times the printed errors), like Rychlewski's
  1.0310-1.0347. Fitting H2 and D2 to Raj's values would conflict with that ratio.
- **Accuracy**: "accurate to about 10^-3" (PDF p. 10), datasets carry 1e-3 a.u.
  absolute, level not stated; the package README says +/-1e-4 numerical.
- **Not extracted**: gamma, off-diagonal elements, T17, Table I; Table II's Bishop and
  Victor-Dalgarno columns (identical to bishop_1980's alpha_293K and victor_dalgarno at
  all 15 wavelengths, checked); Bridge & Buckingham 632.8 nm (reproduced; D2's alpha
  and gamma rows printed swapped: alpha "2.0254", gamma "5.4514", image checked).
  T29 D2 O1(8) Delta^a "0.893" looks misprinted (neighbours 0.025-0.109); not used.
- **Could not verify**: that the GitHub snapshot is the version the paper used (the
  paper cites the repository "accessed 18-01-2017"; the files are dated 24 Jan 2018).
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-25): the pinned regeneration environment is accepted. The D2 spin weights 6:3 are accepted on the evidence above, noted as indirectly sourced. **Resolved (2026-09-25):** murphy_1934 states the ratio directly (g_s/g_a = 1.97 +- 0.03 measured, 'the theoretical ratio of 2', spin 1, even J symmetric; TC-173), and teal_1935 confirms the alternation (TC-174); raj_2018's notes now cite them.

## TC-126: neon's extreme-ultraviolet distribution, and what it says about TC-92

- **Where:** `data/gas/euv/Ne.toml`, `optmat.gas.euv._lines` (NIST lines may now take a `total` and a
  `pseudo_line_ev`), `tests/test_euv.py`, `docs/euv.md`.
- **Construction:** NIST's 17 ground-state lines with f (sum 0.246); a pseudo-line of
  0.046 at 21.55 eV for the unlisted higher members (Chan's discrete total 0.292(15) to
  21.616 eV less the NIST sum; placed just below that midpoint, a choice to review);
  Chan's TRK-normalised continuum 21.6-250 eV; Henke's f2 above; scaled by 1.054 to
  Lesiuk's S(-2) = 2.66080.
- **Results:** S(0) = 9.72; below threshold 0.01-0.02 % from `fit/Ne` in the infrared and
  visible, -0.34 % at 120 nm. S(-4) = 2.826 and S(-6) = 4.765, 0.8 % (3.4 sigma) and 3.4 %
  below Lesiuk's ab initio values. So the photoabsorption route puts neon's dispersion
  below theory, while the refractometry puts it above (TC-92): two independent
  experimental routes on opposite sides of the theory. The sensitivity of S(-4) to the
  pseudo-line position, the 5.4 % scale and the NIST line strengths (grades A-D+) is not
  yet quantified.
- **Also (TC-125):** `lesiuk_2020/chan_1992_Ne` attributes S(-4) and S(-6) to
  Chan et al. 1992, but that paper prints no S(k); the values are presumably Lesiuk's
  own integration of Chan's data. The record is left as reproduced; to review.
- **Status:** open.

  towards the ultraviolet (Xe +0.75 % at 150 nm); GVD at 800 nm +0.49, -0.25, +0.34,

## TC-146: the CH4, SF6 and N2O fits (with the infrared bands)

- **Where:** `data/gas/fits/{CH4,SF6,N2O}.toml`, `data/gas/models/fitted`, `data/gas/defaults.toml` (the
  fits are now the recommended models), `docs/accuracy.md`.
- **CH4** (reduced chi-squared 0.23): the Cuthbertsons' 1920 and Watson & Ramaswamy's
  visible dispersion (free scales), Achtermann, Shelton's 14 ratios to nitrogen; two
  effective oscillators; HITRAN bands below 4500 cm^-1 (1.8 % of the infrared strength
  left out). Reinsch's MC-SCF theory is -12 % (his stated 1-10 %).
- **SF6** (4.15): Swift, Vukovic, Achtermann, Shelton 1985 (6) and 1990 (2) ratios.
  Watson & Ramaswamy's dispersion is a validator: chi-squared 135 for 5 points even with
  a free scale. One effective oscillator sits at its lower energy bound (0.25 hartree,
  a modelling choice) with f = 0.006, and is needed (chi-squared 509 without it).
  **The two Shelton sets prefer HITRAN's SF6 strengths times 1.036 +- 0.009** (chi-squared
  21 against 50 at 1.0); HITRAN's own two cross-section sets differ by 1 %. The strengths
  are kept at HITRAN's (an independent measurement); to decide. SF6's GVD crosses zero
  near 1.2 um (the infrared term); He et al.'s formula gives +55 % at 800 nm.
- **N2O** (3.36): the Cuthbertsons' 1914 dispersion (shape) and the 633 nm metrology
  (Birch, Egan); two effective oscillators with the TRK sum S(0) = 22 +- 2.2 as a prior
  (without it one runs to 6.9 hartree with f = 661 at the same chi-squared). The
  electronic S(-2) = 19.72 against Zeiss et al.'s DOSD 19.70. Watson & Ramaswamy's 546
  nm value (+0.09 %, 7 sigma) is a validator. The dispersion rests on one visible dataset.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-25): keep HITRAN's SF6 band strengths fixed; record the 3.6 % tension; revisit once the Rayleigh data can be fitted.

## TC-150: Rayleigh scattering as an observable, and what it shows

- **Where:** `optmat.gas.fitting._rayleigh` (quantity `rayleigh_cross_section`, `parameters.king_factor`),
  tests in `tests/test_fitting.py`; validators added to `fit/{Ar,N2,CO2,CH4,SF6,N2O}`.
- **Conversion checked:** Sneep & Ubachs's index-based cross sections equal those from
  the fits to 0.2 % for Ar and N2 (1.5-3 % for CO2, N2O, SF6, whose index formulas
  differ).
- **Against the fits** (alpha, measured over model): at 532 nm (Sneep) Ar -1.1 %, N2
  -1.8 %, CO2 -2.7 %, SF6 -1.2 % (each about 1 sigma); **N2O -5.8 % (23 sigma)**, where
  Sneep's King factor (1.225) is the likely cause (his index-based value agrees with
  the fit); **CH4 +5.3 % (5.8 sigma)**. In the deep ultraviolet (Ityaksov, 198-270
  nm): SF6 +5 % (about 1 sigma per point); **CH4 +12 to +20 %**, and Ityaksov's own
  index-based prediction is +10-14 % while Sneep's is +14 %. Three refractometry sets
  fix methane's level at 633 nm to 0.03 %; the scattering data disagree with them for
  CH4 by an amount not explained here (not a King factor: CH4 is a spherical top).
- **Decision:** scattering determines alpha to 1-10 %, against 0.01-1 % from
  refraction, and carries King-factor systematics; it is used as a validator, not
  fitted. It does not narrow the ultraviolet working estimates, and it is insensitive
  to SF6's infrared strength (TC-146: 1.5e-4 of alpha at 250 nm).
- **Not usable yet:** Ityaksov's N2 and CO2 (wavelength-dependent King factors given
  only as formulas), Chopra's N2 (no King factor).
- **Status:** open.

## TC-156 Finding: HITRAN's N2O "vibrational" static polarizability includes orientation

- `data/external/hitran/N2O_bands.csv` contains pure rotational bands (upper = lower
  vibrational state, 51 bands, the largest "0 0 0 0 <- 0 0 0 0" at 18.71 cm^-1). They
  contribute 1.448 au of the 2.634 au static "infrared" polarizability; the
  vibrational bands give 1.186 au. The rotational part is the orientation polarization
  mu^2/3kT at 296 K (1.448 au corresponds to mu = 0.162 D); it scales as 1/T and is not
  a polarizability. CH4: rotational 0.0004 au; CO2: none.
- Evidence: Kirouac's A_eps(T) agrees with fit/N2O's electronic static (19.718 au) +
  1.186 + 1.448 x 296/T to -0.20, -0.34, -0.53 % at 279.65, 303.25, 348.25 K (the slope
  differs: Kirouac's mu = 0.18 D against HITRAN's implied 0.162); Watson (1936) Table
  VII gives N2O P_A + P_E = 7.77 (`watson_1936/dielectric_N2O`), P_E = 7.36, P_A = 0.41
  cm^3/mol: an atomic (vibrational) polarization of 1.10 au, close to 1.186, not 2.63;
  and fit/N2O electronic + HITRAN vibrational bands only = 7.814 cm^3/mol (+0.6 % on
  7.77), with the rotational bands 8.355 (+7.5 %).
- Consequence: fit/N2O's static value (22.35 au) is the 296 K dielectric A_eps with
  orientation, not the static polarizability (about 20.90 au). At optical frequencies
  the rotational terms are negligible (-f/w^2 with tiny f).
- **Action (2026-09-25):** `optmat.gas.infrared.infrared_bands` leaves out pure rotational
  bands (upper and lower vibrational quanta equal); N2O's static vibrational value is
  now 1.186 a.u. (CH4 0.2401, SF6 and CO2 unchanged); fit/N2O and fit/CH4 refitted.
  The optical-frequency effect of the rotational bands was negligible (f ~ 1e-8).
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-25): accepted when the records were merged; points marked open or to confirm above remain open.

## TC-158: conventions of the photoabsorption records (TC-159 to TC-165)

- **Quantity.** Absorption coefficients are stored as `photoionization_cross_section`
  (unit Mb), the quantity the noble-gas photoabsorption records use, although every O2
  and CO2 value here lies below the ionisation limit (absorption into bands and
  dissociation continua). The vocabulary lacks a photoabsorption cross section (format
  need, reported).
- **Conversion.** The printed k (cm^-1, natural log, layer "reduced to NTP") is kept as
  printed; `scale` turns it into Mb: scale = 1e18 / n0. Metzger & Cook state n0 = 2.69e19
  cm^-3 (scale 0.037174721). The others state no conversion: n0 = 101325 / (k_B 273.15)
  = 2.6867801e19 cm^-3 (scale 0.0372192721), the ideal-gas Loschmidt number, matching
  Weissler & Lee's explicit ideal-gas reduction to 0 C and atmospheric pressure. NTP is
  not defined by Watanabe et al. or Inn et al.: 0 C and 1 atm assumed (same group, same
  convention as Bethke's "1 atm at 0 C" and Metzger's Loschmidt number). The real-gas O2
  density at NTP differs by 0.1 %; irrelevant at these uncertainties.
- **Integrated continuum f values** (Watanabe 0.161, Metzger 0.142, Weissler about 6,
  Inn 0.0043/0.0053/0.12) are `oscillator_strength` datasets with an index abscissa and
  `use = "check"` (as `chan_1992`'s totals); their integration ranges are in the row
  labels or notes. Format need: a quantity for an oscillator strength integrated over a
  stated energy range.
- **Band oscillator strengths** (Bethke, Matsui) use the index v' as abscissa (Bethke
  prints no band positions).
- **Status:** open (the conventions to confirm; a photoabsorption quantity is a format need).

- **Not corrected, to check:** 13 more rows where the printed wave number and 1e8/lambda
  disagree beyond rounding (listed in the record's notes: rows 4, 8, 15, 17, 18, 32, 33,
  38, 48, 52, 63, 68, 71, 74). Rows 18 and 74 are digit transpositions of the wave number;
  row 33 (OI 886.618 A against 113815 cm^-1 = 878.62 A) is 8 A apart and cannot be
  decided from the paper. A line list would settle which column is wrong.
- **Paper inconsistencies (no data affected):** text p. 202 "k = 550 cm^-1" at 303 A
  against the abstract's and Table I's 530; Table II's percent difference 7.8 for 640/670
  (4.6 %).
- **Uncertainty:** 10 % (k > 100 cm^-1), 15 % (k <= 100, rows 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 11, 12, 13,
  15, 18), level not stated.
- **Doubt, use:** the values above about 1000 A are far above the photoelectric values of
  Watanabe (1953) and Metzger (1964) (e.g. 1206.4 A: 872 cm^-1 here, Metzger's band B at
  1205 A 430 cm^-1; 1217.645 A: 54 cm^-1 here, Metzger's Lyman-alpha window 0.28 cm^-1 2 A
  away). Kept primary; to decide whether to exclude the rows above about 1000 A, or the in-band
  rows (band location in the printed column).
- **Formula** `ladenburg_wolfsohn` (reproduced, text p. 200): the three resonance
  wavelengths and f values of Ladenburg & Wolfsohn (1932). Read as a per-molecule
  oscillator model, it reproduces the stored `fit/O2` to 0.24-0.45 % (static to 200 nm).
  The equation itself is not printed.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-25): accepted with the integration of TC-178 and TC-218; points marked open or to confirm above remain open.

## Agreement between the O2 sources (computed 2026-09-25)

- **Schumann-Runge continuum maximum:** Watanabe 380 cm^-1 at about 1420 A; Metzger 402 +-
  20 at 1422 A (Table 2's 420 is the misprint); both 20-25 % below Ladenburg & Van
  Voorhis's and Ditchburn & Heddle's 490 at 1450 A (reproduced in text only). 380 and
  402 differ by 5.5 %, within the combined 5 % + 5 %.
- **Continuum oscillator strength:** Watanabe 0.161 (57 000-78 000 cm^-1), Metzger 0.142
  (57 100-74 100 cm^-1, a narrower range); Bethke's f_el 0.163 +- 10 % from the bands;
  Ladenburg & Van Voorhis 0.193, Ditchburn & Heddle 0.215, Ladenburg & Wolfsohn's
  dispersion f2 = 0.202 (quoted).
- **Lyman alpha:** Watanabe 0.27 (zero pressure), Metzger 0.28 (window 1), Preston 0.28
  (quoted): agree to 4 %.
- **Weissler against the photoelectric data:** see TC-160 (not consistent above 1000 A).
- **Band oscillator strengths (12,0)-(17,0):** Matsui below Bethke by 15, 17, 17, 18, 24,
  28 %; below LBC by 2-9 %; YFEP (12,0) 2.43 against Matsui 2.38 (2 %); HCMK 21-47 %
  above Matsui. Bethke's stated 8 % does not cover the difference above (12,0), which
  Matsui attributes to band blending at low resolution, as Bethke himself foresaw
  (overlap errors "not included").

- **Against the fits' moments** (data/fit - 1): Ne CC3 +0.15, -0.08, +0.19, +0.66,
  +2.44 % (k = -2 ... -10); Ar CC3 +0.22, +0.09, -0.17, +2.77, +4.15 %; Kr CC3 +0.58,
  -0.14, -0.46, -5.64, -11.9 % (Kr CC3 falls below the DOSD with |k|, as the paper says;
  the first ab initio Kr dispersion, TC-94, but not converged per the authors). For
  reference the reproduced DOSD against the fits: Ne +0.3 ... +7.0 %, Ar 0.0 ... +6.6 %,
  Kr +0.15 ... -1.3 %.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-25): accepted with the integration of TC-178 and TC-218; points marked open or to confirm above remain open.

## TC-178 Integration into the fits (2026-09-25)

- **Copies switched to their originals:** bideau_mehu_1981 experiment rows now excluded
  where they reprint bideau_mehu_1976 (Ne, Ar 170.2/164.1 nm; Kr 228.8-164.1 nm; Xe
  170.2 nm) or abjean_1971 (Xe 253.7-180.7 nm), and the originals fitted instead (values
  identical, checked); `smith_1976/bideau_mehu_1981_Kr` now `reproduced_from =
  bideau_mehu_1976` and dropped from the Kr validators; `tang_1974/abjean_1971_Xe` now
  `reproduced_from = abjean_1971` and dropped from the Xe validators; the Burns copies in
  achtermann_1991 and egan_2019 now name `burns_1986`.
- **Fitted:** Kr gains bideau_mehu_1976, burns_1986 A_R (chi2 10.0 for 4) and hohm_1990;
  Xe gains abjean_1971, bideau_mehu_1976, burns_1986 A_R (6.1 for 4) and hohm_1990; CH4
  and SF6 gain burns_1986 A_R (SF6: 14.2 for 4; the level moves -186 ppm, between
  Burns's -0.18 % and Achtermann); O2, N2O and CO2 gain hohm_1994 (shape 1e-5 with a
  free-within-1e-3 scale; chi2 33.6, 4.8 and 31.8 for 5, 4 and 5 points: after the
  scale, O2 and N2O residuals about 1e-5 but 612 and 594 nm of O2 at 3-4 sigma; CO2
  about 4e-5).
- **N2O range extended to 320 nm** (was 450): Hohm's 325.13 nm point fits within 1e-5 of
  the visible shape (chi2 +1.4); the GVD moves +3 % at 800 nm, +7 % at 1030 nm and -6 %
  at 1800 nm against the previous fit, which rested on the Cuthbertsons' 1914 shape
  alone (its chi2 rises from 14 to 32 for 8: Hohm's precise shape disagrees with it by
  about 1e-4).
- **CO2:** Hohm's 325 nm point raises the ultraviolet (+370 ppm at 250 nm, GVD +0.7 %
  at 343 nm, 2 of the old sigma), toward bideau_mehu_1973 (mean deviation +0.15 % ->
  +0.06 %). bideau_mehu_1973 fitted with the range extended to 180 nm was tried and
  rejected: its residuals jump by 0.34 % between 185 and 194 nm (-0.19, -0.27, +0.09,
  +0.17, +0.24, +0.26, +0.10 % at 181-254 nm), several times its stated 0.08 %, which no smooth dispersion
  follows (chi2 42 for 7 fitted against 44 as a validator). Validator; range kept at 250
  nm.
- **Validators added:** pawlowski_2005 CC3 moments (Ne, Ar, Kr), burns_1986 A_R (He, Ne,
  Ar, N2, CO2), hohm_1990 (He, Ne, Ar), bideau_mehu_1976 (He, N2), hohm_1994/input_H2,
  simmons_1978 (N2, CO2).
- **Refractivity virial:** Xe gets its first pair term (burns_1986/B_R_Xe, first row,
  25.5(29) at 632.8 nm; the other lines 14.9-18.6: known to about 30 %). Ne and Kr keep
  Orcutt & Cole (Burns agrees, less precise).
- **Sneep's CO2 formula:** the infrared-numerator misprint recorded in sneep_2005's
  notes; with the term restored the formula reproduces Sneep's Table 2 value (427 at
  18 788.4 cm^-1), which resolves the rounding doubt in that formula's check.
- **D2 spin weights:** TC-105 resolved by murphy_1934 (TC-173).

Page numbers are journal pages unless marked "pdf". Ozone absorption (the checks on the
high-resolution data files fetched separately) and ozone theory.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-25): accepted with TC-218; points marked open or to confirm above remain open.

## Conventions common to the ozone records (to confirm)

- **Quantity.** Every ozone absorption value is an `absorption_cross_section` with its
  temperature in `parameters.temperature_k` where the paper states one (omitted, and
  said in `notes`, where it does not).
- **Conversion of absorption coefficients.** A printed coefficient (cm^-1, layer reduced
  to NTP or to 0 C and 760 mm Hg) is kept as printed; `scale` turns it into Mb:
  scale = 1e18 / n0 for a natural-log coefficient, ln(10) x 1e18 / n0 for a decadic one,
  with n0 = 101325 / (k_B 273.15) = 2.6867801e19 cm^-3 (ideal gas), as in
  `watanabe_1953` (scale 0.037219272080).
- **Integrated band strengths** (f of a continuum, a band) are `oscillator_strength`
  datasets with an index abscissa and `use = "check"`, as in the earlier records.

## TC-190 naves_2011 (Naves, Castro & Fonseca, J. Chem. Phys. 134, 054315 (2011))

- **Identity** checked (pdf p. 2).
- **Transcribed:** Table III (`tbl_a5631d2a2b1a`, cells, image checked), the mean
  polarizability rows only: `ccsd_opt`, `ccsd_expt`, `ccsd_t_expt` (4 frequencies each: 0,
  0.0239, 0.0428, 0.0656 hartree); Table II (`tbl_6e45fd86f96d`, image checked):
  `ccsd_relaxed_static` 16.74; text (p. 054315-7): `best_estimate` 18.55. All checks,
  electronic except the best estimate.
- **The ZPVA (key):** Table IV (image checked) gives zpva = [ ]^{1,0} + [ ]^{0,1} = 1.43 +
  0.03 = **1.46 a.u.** static (1.45+0.03, 1.51+0.03, 1.63+0.03 at the three frequencies)
  and pv = 1.41 a.u. static (-0.08, -0.02, -0.01, 0 at infinity). Kumar & Thakkar's
  "1.43 au" is the [ ]^{1,0} term alone, as is Naves's own best estimate (17.12 + 1.43 =
  18.55; with 1.46 it would be 18.58). Sharipov's Table 2 quotes Naves as ZPV 0.216 A^3 =
  1.46 a.u. (the total), PV 0.209 A^3 = 1.41 a.u.; Sharipov's own ZPV is 0.088 a.u.
  (0.013 A^3), from DFT geometries with MP4, and they call their O3 treatment inadequate.
  Bearing on the factor 16 (not a resolution): Naves's corrections are CCSD at the CCSD
  geometry, CCSD frequencies 6-15 % high (the curvature term scales as 1/omega_a), CCSD
  far from converged for O3 (orbital relaxation alone -15 %, triples matter), and the
  authors expect "some inaccuracy" in the zpva. Needs an independent calculation.
- **Format need:** a quantity for a vibrational correction to the polarizability (zpva,
  pv); Table IV's values are in `notes` only.
- **Inference to confirm:** the dynamic zpva uses the orbital-unrelaxed analytical CCSD
  response (not stated).
- **To do:** `kumar_2011/static_i` (17.12) now has its original here
  (`naves_2011/ccsd_t_expt`, row 0): switch its `reproduced_from` to `naves_2011`.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-25): accepted with TC-218; points marked open or to confirm above remain open.

## TC-211 farkas_1934 (new; D2 ortho-para conversion, short record)

- No datasets. PRINTS the nuclear statistical weights (t + 1)(2t + 1) (ortho) and t(2t + 1)
  (para) (p. 482), ortho = even J for Bose-Einstein statistics (p. 486), spin 1 most
  probable (p. 487, with the caveat that spin 1/2 is not excluded by these data), and
  n-D2 = 2/3 o-D2 + 1/3 p-D2 (p. 488): the 6 : 3 weights of raj_2018 (TC-105), which
  murphy_1934 gives as a ratio only.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-25): accepted with TC-218; points marked open or to confirm above remain open.

## CO: what is now curated (summary)

- Refractivity, 167.2-288.2 nm (vacuum, 0 C, real gas): smith_1976 `experiment_CO` 28
  points, 0.10 % (> 220 nm) / 0.58 % (< 220 nm), 90 %; plus the paper's Lagrange values
  (check) and Koch 1914 via the ICT (237.9-289.4 nm, reproduced).
- Refractivity, 480-671 nm (air, 0 C, ideal): cuthbertson_1920 `experiment_CO` 8 points
  (rms 1.2e-8, scale 0.045 %), formula `co_1920`; four older values at 546.1 nm
  (reproduced).
- 546.2 nm (vacuum, 25 C, ideal): watson_1936 `green_CO` 307.9e-6 (primary), formula
  `co` (A from Watson, B from Cuthbertson).
- 532.2 nm: sneep_2005 Rayleigh 6.19(0.4)e-27 cm^2 (F_k 1.016) and the n-based value;
  formula `co_eq17` (fit to Smith, numerator misprint).
- 1566 nm: zhao_2026 `A_R_1566_CO` 4.896795(185) cm^3/mol at 297.53 K (reconstructed,
  primary, 38 ppm): the most accurate CO datum.
- Theory: christiansen_1998 `electronic_CO` (static 13.06 au and 457.9-632.8 nm) with
  its Cauchy moments (formula) and pure vibrational oscillators (formula).
- Static anchors: electronic 13.059 au (zhao_2026 static, still containing the 1566 nm
  infrared response), 13.06 au (christiansen_1998 theory), 13.08 au (Werner and Meyer,
  reproduced); dielectric (electronic + vibrational) 4.98 cm^3/mol (watson_1936,
  reproduced) and Tsankova et al. reduced by Zhao 4.888(45) cm^3/mol; vibrational
  0.1213 au (bishop_1982) and 0.1246 au (christiansen_1998).
- Dipole sums: Kumar and Meath S(-4), S(-6), S(-8) = 48.26, 292.9, 2308 au (via
  zhao_2026); christiansen_1998's CCSD means 47.33, 274.7, 2267 au (computed).
- Faraday: ingersoll_1956 Verdet constants 363.5-987.5 nm (17 + 4 points).
- Gaps: 290-450 nm (no measurement; theory from 457.9 nm only), below 167 nm (the
  Gallagher et al. photoabsorption, TC-212), the infrared (no CO bands in
  data/external/hitran).

Page numbers are journal pages (journal page = PDF page + 7) unless marked "pdf".

## TC-212 gallagher_1988 (Gallagher, Brion, Samson & Langhoff, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 17, 9 (1988)): no numerical data

- **Main finding: the paper holds no numerical cross sections and no recommended
  values.** Tables 2-19 list the data sources per molecule; every cross section is a
  point or line in the figures. Section 5 (p. 28): "A tabular listing of all data
  presented in the figures is available in JILA Data Center Report No. 32". That report
  is where the numbers are (not available to the curators). Recommended tabulated values
  were expected; there are none. The record has no datasets; nothing was digitised from
  the figures.
- Identity checked against PDF page 2 (journal p. 9): title, authors, volume and year
  agree. The curators' library's author-check failure comes from the publisher's cover
  sheet (PDF page 1).
- Stated accuracy of sigma_abs^T (p. 28), quoted in the record: better than +-10 % "in
  almost all cases", better than +-5 % for N2, CO, O2, NO, CO2, N2O, H2O, NH3, CH4, H2S,
  CS2, COS; "a few data sets may be less accurate than +-10% ... particularly in the
  immediate threshold region". Level not stated. H2 and SF6 are not in the 5 % list.
- Method statements quoted with pages: photon I0/I 1-2 % (pp. 19-20), manometer "a few
  percent" (p. 20), TRK "better than ~5%" (p. 23), partials +-15 % and +-10 % (p. 29),
  Eq. 2.22 sigma[Mb] = 109.75 df/dE[eV^-1] (p. 17).
- Extraction faults in the curators' library (none affect data, since none were taken):
  the reference list in the extracted Markdown numbers C. E. Brion and K. H. Tan, J.
  Electron Spectrosc. 23, 1 (1981) as 149 (the page image, p. 151, shows 148), so 149
  appears twice; the markdown of Table 3 (N2) drops the row "a Adam 1983 E P --- beta B
  28-38" (it is in the image and the table note); the extractor's table labels are
  shifted (Table 4, O2, is "unlabelled").
- Per gas, the total-photoabsorption source rows ("Abs" ticked) were compared with the
  table images and their citations with the reference-list page images (pp. 149-153).
  All agree with the markdown except as noted.
- Format note: codespell flags the surname Wight (G. R. Wight, refs. 99, 138, 256) and a <!-- codespell:ignore wight -->
  `codespell:ignore` comment cannot sit inside a multi-line TOML string, so the record
  writes it `Wight` (a TOML escape; the loaded notes read "Wight"). An alternative <!-- codespell:ignore wight -->
  is adding `wight` to codespell's ignore list in `pyproject.toml`. <!-- codespell:ignore wight -->

## Conventions common to the vacuum-ultraviolet photoabsorption records (to confirm)

- **Quantity.** Total photoabsorption is recorded as the new `absorption_cross_section`
  (unit Mb, or cm2 where the paper prints a cross section); the earlier records
  (`watanabe_1953`, `weissler_1952`, `metzger_1964`, `inn_1953`) still use
  `photoionization_cross_section` for the same kind of value and were not changed.
  `parameters.temperature_k` is omitted everywhere: none of the five papers states the
  gas temperature (room temperature; Ditchburn & Heddle's line analysis assumes 20 C).
- **Conversion.** The printed absorption coefficient (cm^-1, natural log, at 1 atm and
  0 C) is kept as printed; `scale` = 1e18 / n0 gives Mb. Where the paper states its n0
  it is used: Ditchburn & Heddle N = 2.705e19 (scale 0.0369686), Ladenburg & Van Voorhis
  N = 2.706e19 (0.0369549). These are 0.67-0.71 % above the ideal-gas Loschmidt number
  2.6867801e19, so the stored cross sections are 0.7 % below alpha / n0 (to decide:
  paper's conversion, as `metzger_1964`, or the physical n0). Watanabe et al. and
  Zelikoff et al. state no conversion: n0 = 2.6867801e19 (scale 0.0372192721), as
  `watanabe_1953` and `inn_1953`.
- **Integrated continuum f values** are `oscillator_strength` datasets with an index
  abscissa and `use = "check"`, as in the earlier records.
- **Band oscillator strengths** use the index v' as abscissa.

## TC-213 ditchburn_1953 (Ditchburn & Heddle, Proc. R. Soc. A 220, 61 (1953))

- **Identity** checked against the first page (pdf 2): correct.
- **Table 1** (`tbl_9b71613fa0c5`, cells file only; image checked cell by cell, all
  agree): 21 group means `means` (nu mean, alpha mean, +- as sigma, probable error), 15
  single-line values of the 205 cm path `long_path` and 44 of the 0.043 cm path
  `short_path` (both `check`: the same observations as the means). The script checks
  that each group's bracketed observation counts add up to column 6 (all 21 do).
- **Conversion** with the paper's N = 2.705e19 (reproduces its 1.81e-17 cm2 from 490
  cm^-1); 0.68 % below alpha / 2.6868e19.
- **Doubt (group mean):** the group 64060-63810 cm^-1 (306 (7), 307 (6), 228 (3)) has
  the observation-weighted mean 63919 cm^-1, 291.8 cm^-1; the table prints 64108 and 277
  +- 16. A mean wave number above all its lines is impossible, so the printed row is
  inconsistent; no single misprint explains it; kept as printed, no erratum. The other
  20 groups reproduce (the 69484 group gives 69500 in nu, alpha exact).
- **Doubt (errors):** the text states the errors are 60 n^-1/2 cm^-1 (probable error);
  the printed ones are about 80 n^-1/2 (20 for n = 15-17; 16 for the n = 16 group
  above). Kept as printed.
- **Text values:** `maximum` 1.81 +- 0.1e-17 cm2 at 69000 cm^-1 (p. 67, check);
  `continuum_f` 0.215 +- 0.020 (note added in proof, p. 70, check).
- **Comparison:** about 20 % above the photoelectric maxima (watanabe_1953 380,
  metzger_1964 402 +- 20 cm^-1); the authors blame scattered light in Watanabe et al.'s
  work. Which to weight is for the model step.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-25): accepted with TC-218; points marked open or to confirm above remain open.

## TC-215 ladenburg_1933 (Ladenburg & Van Voorhis, Phys. Rev. 43, 315 (1933))

- **Identity** checked against the first page: correct.
- **Table I** (`tbl_0010b8557526`, CSV; image checked, agree): Ladenburg & Wolfsohn's
  (1932) (n - 1) x 10^7 at eight round wave numbers 52084-25000 cm^-1 extracted as
  `lw_refractivity` (`reproduced`, original not in the curators' library; "accurate to
  within one unit", bound). State assumed N.P.T. = 1 atm, 0 C (the paper's C uses N at
  N.P.T.); L-W's own reduction not described. Wave numbers: vacuum assumed (irrelevant
  at 1e-7).
- **G, H, I columns** (continuum contribution, remainder, one-term fit) are in the notes
  only (no vocabulary quantity; format need: a partial refractivity, useful as the check
  of a Kramers-Kronig integral of the S-R continuum). H = (n - 1) - G exactly.
- **Formulas:** `lw_1932` (L-W's three-resonance formula, reproduced) and
  `continuum_plus_one_term` (Eq. 4 with f_s = 7.143, lambda_s = 501.3 A). **Doubt:** both
  reproduce the table only with C = 1.2096e6 cm^-2, 0.30 % above N e^2 / 2 pi m c^2 from
  footnote 15's constants (1.2060e6): the one-term I to 0.5e-7, the three-term (n - 1) to
  3e-7. The origin of the 0.30 % is not identified.
- **Text:** `sr_maximum` about 490 cm^-1 at 69000 cm^-1 (N = 2.706e19; 10 % bound from
  "5-10 percent"); `continuum_f` 0.193 (check). The abstract's position 6.8e4 cm^-1
  against the text's 69000 (= 1450 A): rounding, not corrected.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-25): accepted with TC-218; points marked open or to confirm above remain open.

## TC-216 watanabe_1952 (Watanabe, Inn & Zelikoff, J. Chem. Phys. 20, 1969 (1952))

- **Identity:** the curators' copy is the 1952 letter (pdf 2, received 13 October 1952),

  I**: Part III (`inn_1953`) refers to "Part I of this series" for the method, i.e. the
  O2 paper `watanabe_1953`; Part II is `zelikoff_1953`.
- **OCR:** the curators' extracted text of this page is poor ("10SQ-2S00A", "14S0A",
  "0.8SA"); every value was read from the rendered page images (pdf 2-3).
- **Gases:** O2 (Fig. 1, figure only) and CO2 (text only).

  measurement as `watanabe_1953/sr_maximum`); `o2_lyman_alpha` 0.33 cm^-1 (excluded:
  pressure-dependent, about 75 mm Hg); `co2_lyman_alpha` 2.0 cm^-1 (check: `inn_1953`
  gives 1.97); `co2_continuum_maxima` about 14 cm^-1 at 1475 A and 18.5 cm^-1 at 1335 A
  (primary: the only printed k of these maxima; `inn_1953` has them only in figures).
- **Doubts:** the reference state of k is not stated in the letter (NTP assumed, as the
  full papers); the Lyman-alpha wavelength 1215.7 A is taken as in `watanabe_1953`.
  Whether preliminary values should be primary when the full paper gives the maxima only
  in figures is open.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-25): accepted with TC-218; points marked open or to confirm above remain open.

  Voorhis's 490 cm^-1 maximum and f = 0.193 (`ladenburg_1933`; quoted in
  `watanabe_1953`, `weissler_1952`, `bethke_1959`), Ditchburn & Heddle's 490 cm^-1 at 1450
  A and f = 0.215 +- 0.02 (`ditchburn_1953`; quoted in `metzger_1964`, `bethke_1959`).
  No dataset of those records holds them, so nothing changes.

## TC-218 Integration: ozone and carbon monoxide (2026-09-25)

- **Interface (decision 3):**
  - `optmat.gas.models.base.Model.complex_polarizability`,
    `optmat.gas.models.base.Model.refractive_index` and
    `optmat.gas.models.registry.refractive_index` added. Transparent models return a zero
    imaginary part.
  - The real-part methods of an absorbing model warn (`ModelAbsorptionWarning`) where
    |Im alpha / Re alpha| > 1e-4.
  - A species without an equation of state (ozone) takes the ideal-gas density in the
    model methods.
- **Ozone data:**
  - Thirteen files from the MPI-Mainz UV/VIS atlas are committed gzipped and byte for
    byte, with SHA-256s and the atlas's citation, in
    `data/external/mainz_uvvis/PROVENANCE.md`.
  - The atlas asks to be cited; it states no redistribution terms. **Check:** is
    committing the data files acceptable (as for Henke's files), or should only derived
    tables be kept (as for HITRAN)?
- **Measured-absorption term** (`optmat.gas.absorption`, `data/gas/absorption/O3.toml`):
  - The windows are Serdyuchenko 293 K for 213.33-1100 nm, Yoshino 1993 for 185-213.33
    nm (0.0135 nm, on an absolute scale at 12 lines; the paper is not in the curators'
    library),
    Mason 1996 for 110.2-185 nm (the atlas's digitisation of Fig. 5) and the curated
    Ogawa & Cook Table I for 103.3-110.2 nm.
  - Gaussian smoothing is 50 cm^-1 FWHM in wavenumber (decision 1). The Kramers-Kronig
    transform is an FFT principal value, checked against a direct midpoint sum to 2e-4.
  - The Hartley-band strength is 0.0766, against Kumar & Thakkar C's 0.0787 (-2.7 %: the
    newer cross sections).
- **The ozone fit** (`fit/O3`):
  - The model is the absorption term, plus kumar_2011_supplement/idos_C above 20.6 eV as
    fixed poles (`fixed_intervals`), plus one fitted oscillator for 12-20.6 eV (at Ogawa &
    Cook's effective 16.15 eV), plus HITRAN below 2500 cm^-1.
  - It is fitted to swift_1988 (10 % bound), cuthbertson_1914/ozone_adopted (1-2 %) and
    kalugina_2015/best_estimate with `correction_au = [1.46, 0.4]`: Naves et al.'s full
    zero-point correction ([ ]^{1,0} + [ ]^{0,1}, TC-190).
  - Result: f(12-20.6 eV) = 2.55 +- 0.07 (A 1.83, C 2.18, B1 2.48); chi2 3.6 for 6 dof.
  - **Check the ZPVA choice.** Sharipov's 0.088 a.u. would lower n - 1 by 2.5 %. Sharipov
    calls his own treatment inadequate for O3, and Naves's value is 1.46. With Naves's
    value, theory and the refractivity data agree; with Sharipov's they do not (the
    prototype's chi2 rose to 17 for the static point).
- **The Cuthbertsons' ozone dispersion (Table XI) is a validator, not fitted:**
  - Its 480/670.8 nm ratio is 1.0498. The model, and every variant of it considered,
    gives 1.041-1.042.
  - Replacing their 1909 O2 dispersion (subtracted with a factor of 15) by the modern
    O2 fit explains 0.28 % of the difference (1.0498 -> 1.0469).
  - The rest (0.6 %) is about 6 times their stated 1/200 accuracy of the dispersion.
  - Fitted with its stated uncertainty, it would drag the remote strength to 2.11 at
    chi2 193 for 8 points.
  - **Open:** possibly ozone decay during the measurement series.
- **Ozone GVD** (decision 1):
  - Replacing Serdyuchenko by Bogumil or Brion changes beta2 at 343 and 800 nm by 16-52
    %; the 243 K spectrum changes it by 23-34 %, and 25 or 100 cm^-1 smoothing by 6-40 %.
  - Working estimate 50 % at 343 and 800 nm; 1 % at 1800 nm.
  - n - 1 is known to about 2 %.
- **Temperature** (decision 2): 293 K only. The `T243` variant of the absorption
  configuration gives the sensitivity.
- **Vibrational static polarizabilities:**
  - **CO:** HITRAN 0.1223 a.u. against Bishop & Cheung's 0.1213 (+0.8 %).
  - **O3:** HITRAN 0.869 against Bishop & Cheung's 0.788 (+10 %) and Naves's pure
    vibrational 1.41 (ab initio). This does not affect the optical range; **open** for
    the static limit.
  - **Other gases**: Bishop & Cheung against HITRAN is CO2 -17 %, N2O -8 %,
    CH4 -4 %, SF6 +8.7 %. The fits' infrared terms stay on HITRAN, whose strengths the
    phase-matching data support (TC-104, TC-146).
- **The CO fit** (`fit/CO`):
  - It is fitted to smith_1976/experiment_CO, cuthbertson_1920/experiment_CO (level
    free), watson_1936/green_CO and zhao_2026/A_R_1566_CO (reconstructed,
    TC-197), with HITRAN below 5000 cm^-1. Reduced chi2 0.37.
  - Effective oscillators: f = 0.185 at 147 nm (the A-X system) and 4.27 at 73.6 nm.
  - Christiansen's electronic values lie -0.18 % from the fit.
  - Zhao's derived static value lies -0.11 % (23 sigma): its reduction from 1566 nm
    differs. **Open.**
- **Record links:** kumar_2011/static_i now reproduces naves_2011, and
  zhao_2026/may_2008_O2 reproduces may_2008; bethke_1959/ditchburn_heddle reproduces
  ditchburn_1954.
- **Not done:**
  - The Buckingham & Graham citation strings in achtermann_1991, burns_1986,
    hohm_1990 and vukovic_1996 are not converted to `buckingham_1974`: each needs its
    values checked against that record first.
  - zhao_2026's O2 A_mu convention (a cgs susceptibility over 4 pi, not
    chi_M/3) is not changed. No fit uses Zhao's O2 values; the effect on CH4 and CO is
    below 10 ppm. **Open.**
- **Format needs** reported during the curation and not implemented:
  - an interval oscillator strength;
  - a wavelength-integrated cross section;
  - a vibrational polarizability or correction;
  - a per-row temperature;
  - a refractivity difference;
  - a Cauchy coefficient A_2;
  - a magnetic susceptibility;
  - a partial refractivity.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-25): all accepted. The Mainz atlas files stay committed, with citation. Naves's zero-point correction is used. The Cuthbertsons' ozone dispersion is a validator. The fits stay on HITRAN rather than Bishop & Cheung. Zhao's CO static value remains a validator. The format needs are deferred.

Page numbers are PDF pages of the curators' copy unless marked otherwise.

## TC-219 sakamoto_2010 (Sakamoto et al., NIFS-DATA-109, 2010): Berkowitz's distributions

- **Source of the extracted values: the NIFS text files, not the curators' extracted
  cells (accepted 2026-09-26, TC-223).** `tools/extract/sakamoto_2010.py` reads the
  discrete tables from the committed `data/external/nifs_photoab/<gas>_table.txt.gz`. The
  curators' extracted tables of this report are OCR of sideways pages: reversed strings
  (`20+E0056 .7`), merged tables (Ar, CO pages) and misread digits (He Table I: 2.4425E+01, 6.8800E-04, 6.416E+01 and a repeated
  6.5181E+01 where the page prints 2.4452E+01, 6.6800E-04, 6.4816E+01, 6.5108E+01), while
  passing the extraction's grid checks. Data rule 2 says "from the library's tables" (the
  curators' library); the NIFS files are the report's own electronic tables, checked
  against the PDF as below.
- **Check of the committed NIFS files against the PDF (all 12 species, every row).**
  `pdftotext -layout` of the curators' PDF copy, pp. 14-258: every numeric row of every file
  (102 He, 96 Ne, 226 Ar, 326 H2, 289 N2, 741 O2, 352 CO, 1217 CO2, 682 N2O, 540 O3,
  285 CH4, 487 SF6: discrete, interval and continuum rows) is one run of cells on one
  printed line, and the multisets of all numbers agree exactly per species: **no
  difference**. By eye (page images): every discrete table (pp. 14, 28, 37, 42-44, 47,
  53, 65, 120) and a continuum page per species (pp. 15, 29, 39, 44, 47, 53, 60, 65, 110,
  120, 173, 190, 254), rows compared with the files: all agree. The NIFS text drops the
  footnote marks (He Table I a); Ar Table I a-f) and the rules that split tables into
  groups; the script restores both (marks in `printed`, groups as separate files).
- **Internal consistency of every row** (E x lambda = hc to 2e-4; sigma_a = 109.76097
  df/dE and mu_m = sigma_a N_A / M_A to 3e-4): all pass except **helium's df/dE column,
  1.25e4-1e5 eV (17 rows), printed '.80404E-10' ... '.62035E-13': a factor 10 too
  small** (the PDF prints the same). sigma_a and mu_m are right there (sigma_a matches the
  printed high-energy formula to 1e-5). A loader of `He_table.txt.gz` must use sigma_a
  (or df/dE x 10) above 1e4 eV. Not an erratum here (the continuum is not a dataset).
- **Datasets** (all `oscillator_strength` vs eV, `use = "reproduced"`: Berkowitz's book
  values; He Table I from `berkowitz_1997`; 22 datasets, 443 rows): He `discrete_He` 20
  (row I-20 = sum n >= 21), `excess_He` 18; Ne `discrete_Ne` 19, `resonance_2s_Ne` 6,
  `k_edge_Ne` 4; Ar `discrete_Ar` 21 (series sums a-c, e-f and the inter-threshold
  continuum d as single rows), `window_Ar` 7 (negative f: window resonances to subtract
  from the continuum), `k_edge_Ar` 1; H2 `lyman_H2` 37, `werner_H2` 14, `b_prime_H2` 9,
  `d_H2` 16, `rydberg_H2` 20, `predissociation_H2` 17, `autoionization_H2` 146; N2
  `discrete_N2` 47, `k_edge_N2` 3; O2 `intervals_O2` 11 (interval integrals, abscissa the
  lower edge), `k_edge_O2` 1; CO `discrete_CO` 19, `k_edge_CO` 2; N2O `intervals_N2O` 5
  (interval integrals). CO2, O3, CH4, SF6 have no discrete table.
- **Erratum:** `discrete_Ar` row I-6, energy printed 1.3606E+01 (lambda 911.27 A) for the
  first nd-series line (3d); corrected 13.864 eV from `chan_1992` (Moore). 13.606 eV is
  the Rydberg energy and the hydrogen Lyman limit (p. 11). To confirm with the book.
- **Doubt (not corrected):** Ar energies differ from `chan_1992`'s by 10-50 meV for 7s
  (15.159 vs 15.186), 5d (15.170 vs 15.118) and 4d' (14.984 vs 15.004 eV).
- **Formulas (12):** `tail_He` (Ry units, above 13 600 eV; reproduces the table's sigma_a
  at 2e4 and 1e5 eV to 1e-5), `tail_H2` (2.888 x the hydrogen formula above 10 keV;
  reproduces 12.5 keV-100 keV to 6e-5; the book's 10 keV point is 27 % below it), and
  the hydrogenic K-shell formula above 1e5 eV for Ne, Ar, N2, O2, CO, CO2, N2O, O3, CH4,
  SF6 (chi = sqrt(E_K/(E-E_K)), image checked), each 0.5-5 % off the table's 1e5 eV row
  (a step at the join). For N2 and O2 the text omits "of each atom"; only the two-atom
  sum joins the table.
- **Sums computed here, not printed (the report prints no totals and no
  polarizabilities; nothing to transcribe as `cauchy_moment`).** S(-2) [Ry^-2]
  (alpha = 4 S(-2) au) / S(0) vs Z, from lines + intervals + trapezoid on the printed
  grid + tails: He 0.3490 (1.396) / 1.9958; Ne 0.6469 (2.588) / 9.693; Ar 2.7493
  (10.997) / 18.031; H2 1.3184 (5.274) / 1.960; N2 3.0037 (12.015) / 14.031; O2 2.7135
  (10.854) / 16.004; CO 3.3152 (13.261) / 14.027; CO2 4.3584 (17.434) / 22.205; N2O
  4.8519 (19.408) / 22.309; O3 4.3474 (17.390) / 22.163 (Z 24); CH4 4.1977 (16.791) /
  9.903; SF6 7.6052 (30.421) / 69.042. The grid trapezoid reproduces the report's printed
  corrected partial moments to 0.03 % (CO2 S(2)), 0.6-1 % (Ar 243-253 eV), 3.5-4 % (CO
  IP-17.712 eV; Ar S(1) 500-929.7 eV). **S(0) misses TRK by 7.7 % for O3, 3 % for Ne, 2
  % for H2**: more than the integration explains. H2: the sources table cites
  Glass-Maujean's dissociation continua, but no table holds a df/dE below 15.426 eV, and

- **Joins and reproductions in the continuum** are in the record's notes (per species);

- **Identity** ASSERTED (the curators' BibTeX), confirmed against the title page (p. 3).

  sum rule analysis [24]' (the book, p. 228) 'leads to an enhancement in cross section by
  a factor 1.4' over his 1970 figure; p. 12, the 1968 abstract's 42 Mb at 725 A is 'about
  40% higher than shown in the 1970 figure'; the working total is Cook 1970 x ~1.4.
  Compare kumar_2011's scale factors for 12.00-20.60 eV (B1 1.34, C 1.18, A 0.986) and
  check whether sakamoto_2010's O3 continuum 11.24-20.66 eV (book Fig. 5.12) carries the
  1.4.

  Mb at 2555 A (p. 8; no source, temperature or medium stated; vacuum assumed, `check`);

  Geophys. Union 49, 736A).
- **Ionisation and appearance energies** (notes only, no quantity in the format; all
  reproduced from Willitsch et al., Weiss et al., Merkt et al., Moore, Taniguchi et al.):

  13.1322(4) eV, AP O+ 14.6802(4) eV, 2O + O+ 19.7668(2) eV (p. 12), PES peak energies

## TC-221 sharipov_2022 (Sharipov, Loukhovitski & Loukhovitskaya, SpringerBriefs, 2022)

- **Datasets:** `alpha_el_mp4_{CO2,O3,CH4,SF6}` (Table 3.4, p. 61, `tbl_268cb2f58193`,
  image checked), `use = "reproduced"` from `sharipov_2017` (the values are identical:
  2.611, 2.801, 2.464, 4.665 A^3). Script `tools/extract/sharipov_2022.py`.
- **What supersedes 2017: nothing numerically.** New: the PP thermal coefficients b^PP,
  c^PP (CO2 27.71/-4.07, O3 21.17/-2.88, CH4 140.07/-22.39, SF6 57.94/-6.11; x1e-6 A^3/K,
  x1e-9 A^3/K^2), the diatomic ZPV/PV corrections of Loukhovitski et al. 2016 (Table 3.1,
  p. 44: ZPV H2 0.037, N2 0.021, O2 0.016, CO 0.006; PV CO 0.020 A^3) and the Eq. 3.22/3.24
  fit parameters to more digits (p. 62). All in `notes` (no quantity for a correction:
  format need, as in 2017).
- **O3 PV inconsistency carried over:** Table 3.3 (p. 56) prints 0.208, Table 3.4 0.312
  (the CO2 row's digits), exactly as the 2017 paper (Table 2 vs Table A1). 0.208 agrees
  with Naves et al. (0.209); Table 3.4's 0.312 is probably the misprint. Not corrected
  (not extracted).
- **Stated reason O3 ZPV is below Naves et al.'s** (p. 55, quoted in notes): the O3
  ground state's "severe multireference nature"; the DFT (B97-2) treatment "is not
  capable to describe adequately the electronic structure of the ground state ozone",
  Naves et al. used coupled cluster. 0.013 vs 0.216 A^3 (0.088 vs 1.46 au): factor 15.
- **Section 6.1** summarised in notes (two-level model Eq. 6.1; dissociation trend
  Delta alpha_d/alpha_mol = 3.7e-4 Delta H_d^298 in kJ/mol, Fig. 6.2; O2 behind a Mach-8
  shock: O atoms ~2.5 % of n - 1, excited states 1.5 %, K^GD's temperature dependence up
  to 1.5 %). The printed "by 0.002 A^3 per one O2 molecule decay" (p. 92) looks small
  against Fig. 6.2's Delta alpha_d/alpha_mol of about 0 for O2 (consistent) but is not
  checkable here.
- **Computed here** (in notes): the thermal corrections at 296 K from b, c (UP: CO2
  0.026, O3 0.012, CH4 0.028, SF6 0.080 au; PP: 0.053, 0.041, 0.267, 0.112 au) and the
  diatomic corrections in au.
- **Reproductions quoted in Tables 3.1/3.3** (notes only): kolos_1967 (H2 ZPV 0.035),
  christiansen_1998 (N2 ZPV 0.007, CO ZPV 0.007 and PV 0.018), bishop_1982 (CO2 PV 0.26),
  naves_2011 (O3 ZPV 0.216, PV 0.209).
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-26): accepted with TC-223; points marked open or to confirm above remain open.

## TC-222 gallagher_1988 vs its second library copy (no new record)

- **The same scan of the same article** (J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 17, 9-153 (1988), DOI
  10.1063/1.555821 in both): the table images are pixel-identical in layout, fonts and
  defects (the same clipped last digit of "172" and "218" in Table 4). Copy 1
  (146 pp) is AIP's online PDF: an OCR text layer (Adobe Paper Capture)
  and an added publisher cover page, so journal page = pdf page + 7 (as the
  `gallagher_1988` record says). Copy 2 (145 pp) is image-only (no text
  layer) and has no cover: journal page = pdf page + 8, every table one pdf page
  earlier.
- **The curators' extractions**: both have 20 tables, 264 references, 111-112 figures; copy 1
  also has machine-generated figure descriptions (hence 591 KB of Markdown against 200
  KB). Running text: the same decimals except the cover's DOI and one misreading in copy
  1 (Eq. 3.14's factor read as `K^{2.48}`, the superscript reference 48 merged into the
  exponent; copy 2 reads `K^{2}.^48` correctly).
- **Tables 2-19 compared cell by cell** (the source lists the `gallagher_1988` record
  uses): identical except (a) layout (copy 2 keeps the caption as a first row in Tables 2
  and 9; row-shifted, same content), (b) notation (`O^+` vs `0^+`, subscript braces,
  `16-22` vs `16- 22`), and (c) **one real difference, Table 4 (O2), McCoy 1978: copy 1
  reads reference 216, copy 2 reads 218**; the reference list gives 218 (D. G. McCoy,
  J. M. Morton and G. V. Marr, J. Phys. B 11, L547 (1978)) and the image shows a clipped
  "21?": copy 2 is right. The `gallagher_1988` record does not quote this row.
- **Recommendation:** keep `gallagher_1988` on copy 1 (it has the text layer and the
  record's page convention); note copy 2 as a duplicate; neither holds a numerical cross
  section.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-26): accepted with TC-223; points marked open or to confirm above remain open.

## TC-223 Integration (2026-09-25)

- **NIFS tables** (`data/external/nifs_photoab`, fetched from dpc.nifs.ac.jp):
  - Checked number for number against the report's PDF (TC-219).
  - **He df/dE above 1e4 eV is printed ten times too small** in the report and the file.
    Any loader must use the cross-section column there.
  - **Copyright:** the report asks for copyright inquiries to the NIFS Research
    Information Office. The files are committed as the Mainz files were (TC-218).
    **Check.**
- **TC-219: the extraction reads the committed NIFS text, not the curators' extracted
  table cells.** The curators' OCR of the sideways tables is corrupt. The reading was
  checked cell for cell against the page images. Accepted as an exception to data rule 2
  (confirmed below).
- **Ozone** (with fit/O3, TC-218):
  - Berkowitz's recommended distribution (NIFS) has f(12-20.6 eV) = 2.25 by
    integration here. That is Kumar & Thakkar C (2.18) to B1 (2.48), and below the fitted
    2.55.
  - Its total S(0) is 22.2, 7.7 % short of 24: no data at 1.31-1.65 eV, and missing
    strength that could not be located (TC-219). Its S(-2) (17.4 au) is therefore not a
    usable static value.
  - Berkowitz 2008 states that Cook's 1968 calibration, preferred by sum rules, lies a
    factor 1.4 above Cook's 1970 scale, the one that Kumar & Thakkar's A distribution
    rests on (1.83). The fit's 2.55 is 1.39 times that. This is independent support for
    the fitted strength, which came from the refractivity and the static value alone.
    fit/O3 is not changed.
- **Static polarizabilities from the NIFS distributions**
  - The integration of TC-219 gives He 1.396, Ne 2.588, Ar 11.00, H2 5.27, N2 12.02, CO
    13.26, CO2 17.43, CH4 16.79 and SF6 30.42 au.
  - Against the fits' electronic static values they differ by -2.9 % (H2) to +2.5 % (O2)
    (He +0.9, Ne -2.8, Ar -0.7, N2 +2.4, CO +1.4, CO2 -0.5, N2O -1.5, CH4 -2.7, SF6
    +1.2 %), the level of Berkowitz's evaluations. O3 is -12.6 %: see the S(0) shortfall
    above. No fit uses them. They are candidate validators, and the
    starting data for extreme-ultraviolet models of the molecules (later work).
- **Sharipov 2022** adds nothing that replaces a 2017 value. It confirms that its O3
  zero-point correction is unreliable (multireference character): fit/O3's choice of
  Naves stands.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-26): the extraction from the committed NIFS text (TC-219) and the committed NIFS files are accepted.
