  `data/values/ionisation/{H2,CO,CH4,O2}/jagau_2018__*.csv` (54 files);
  `optmat.gas.molecular_ionisation_validation` (`JAGAU_2018`, `FITTED_REFERENCES`, the
  `reference` of `orientation_averaged_rates`, CH4's average);
  `molecular_ionisation_rates.toml` (O2, CH4); the manual page and its tables.
- **Transcribed:** the supplement's Tables S3 (H2, full CI and HF, parallel and
  perpendicular, the standard basis), S6 (CO, HF and CCSD, 13 angles, F = 0.06 and
  0.09), S8 (CH4, HF and CCSD, orientations A, B, C), S9 (O2, parallel and
  perpendicular, F = 0.04 to 0.16) and S10 (O2, 7 angles between, F = 0.06 and 0.10):
  the rates Gamma (au) of the molecule, all electrons, fixed nuclei. Every rate cell
  checked against the table images. Excluded rows, by the paper's own statement of the
  method's low-field limit (Gamma of at least ~1e-5 au, p. 4): O2's CCSD rate at 0.04
  au (7e-6), and CH4 at 0.04 au in all orientations (the rate rises to 0.06 au by 7 to
  14, where a tunnelling rate rises by some 400). Not taken: He (the method's
  calibration), H2 against the bond length, H2O (not an optmat gas), the moments.
- **Orientation averages:** O2 over its nine angles at 0.06 and 0.10 au (the fields
  of Table S10); CO over its thirteen (0 deg is the field from C to O, the reverse of
  majety_2015's; the average does not depend on it); H2 as (par + 2 perp)/3; CH4 as 0.3
  A + 0.3 B + 0.4 C, Lebedev's 14-point rule on the sphere (weight 1/15 on each of the
  six face normals, the C directions, and 3/40 on each of the eight cube corners, the A
  and B directions), exact to spherical harmonics of degree 5.
- **Checked (cross-checks of majety_2015):** H2: the default within 4 % of Jagau's
  full CI from 0.08 to 0.14 au (1.30 at 0.06 au, where the rate is 2e-5 au, at the
  method's floor), as of Majety's. CO: Majety's average 18 % above Jagau's at 0.06 au
  and 13 % at 0.09 au, as Jagau's text reports (its '4-8.10-4 a.u.' is read as a
  misprint of 10-5, the record); the default 1.54 and 1.14 times Jagau's.
- **Finding (O2):** with N2's alpha of 14 the default was 0.32 of Jagau's CCSD average
  at 0.06 au and 0.12 at 0.10 au: the correction, exp(-alpha F/(I_p kappa^3)), is a
  factor 0.03 at 0.10 au for O2's small I_p kappa^3. Jagau places O2's barrier
  suppression at about 0.12 au, not the atomic formula's 0.05.
- **Finding (CH4):** with the first maximum of the 1t2 band, 13.6 eV, the default was
  2 to 4.8 times Jagau's average, and no alpha reproduces the reference's dependence on
  the field (the best, 19.7, leaves 2.4 falling to 0.5). With the middle maximum, 14.4
  eV, it does (below). Jagau's EOM-IP-CCSD puts CH4's vertical energy at 14.43 eV: at
  fixed nuclei the tunnelling electron sees the degenerate state at the neutral's
  geometry, the centre of the Jahn-Teller-split band, not its first peak.
- **Decision:** O2's alpha 6.1 (the least-squares value with 2 electrons, 6.10; both
  fields within 10 %); CH4's energy 14.4 eV (`heilbronner_1977/vertical_CH4#1t2_2`) and
  alpha 18.0 (17.99; 0.06 to 0.12 au within 27 %). Uncertainty factors: O2 2 (was 3),
  CH4 2 (was 5). CO2, N2O and SF6 keep N2's 14.
- **Consequence (measured yields):** O2's rate at 800 nm rises (2.8 times at 1e14
  W/cm2). Against Wahlstrand et al. O2 is now 5.0 to 6.5 times above (was 2.2 to 2.9),
  as N2's 5 to 9; relative to xenon 0.65 to 2.4 (was 0.34 to 0.90), which brackets the
  measurement. Against Guo et al.'s text O2/Xe is 0.035 to 0.055 (was 0.022), 2 to 3
  times below 'roughly ten times below Xe+' (was 4.5): TC-683's conflict is reduced,
  not closed.
- **Doubt:**
  1. One method for O2 and CH4: CCSD without triples ((T) raises CO's rate by about
     20 % at 0.06 au, Jagau p. 6) and complex basis functions (5 % above explicit
     complex scaling for He, more below 0.14 au).
  2. alpha is not one constant: H2 6.0, O2 6.1, N2 14.0, CH4 18.0, and CO would ask for
     16.3. Whether CO2's and N2O's pi orbitals follow O2's (6) or N2's (14) is not
     known; at 1e14 W/cm2 the difference is a factor of about 2 in CO2's rate, within
     its factor 3.
  3. O2's fit rests on two fields; beyond 0.10 au the reference keeps rising where the
     model's range (1.5 times the barrier-suppression field, 0.077 au for O2) has
     ended.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-29).

## TC-699 Values read from figures: the rule (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `AGENTS.md` (data rule 8), `docs/data.md` (`digitised`, `table`),
  `optmat.datasets.Dataset` (`digitised`, `_check_digitised`),
  `tests/test_datasets.py`, `pyproject.toml` (`pypdfium2`, a development dependency of
  the extraction scripts), `tools/extract/_figure.py`.
- **Decision (J. C. Travers, 2026-09-29, without an OEP):** a value a source gives
  only in a figure may be taken from it, when no table, text, supplement or data
  repository gives it. Before, figures were never digitised and such values were read
  qualitatively only (TC-508, TC-510 to TC-512, TC-683).
- **Why:** most figures of the last two decades are vector drawings in the PDF, whose
  markers and lines are stored as coordinates. Read from the drawing, with the axes
  calibrated from the drawing's own tick marks, they reproduce the numbers a paper also
  prints to about 1 % (van der Hart 2007, TC-700). An embedded image can be read too,
  less precisely.
- **The rule:**
  1. Vector figures are read from the PDF by the source's extraction script;
     raster figures from the image, with the calibration and the picked pixels written
     in the script.
  2. `digitised = "vector"` or `"raster"`; `table` names the library figure (`fig_...`);
     the uncertainty is stated and includes the digitising uncertainty. The loader
     rejects a figure dataset without either.
  3. Every extraction is checked against every number the source prints for the same
     quantity and against an overlay on the rendered figure, both recorded here.
  4. Figure values are `use = "check"`. Values read from an image are never fitted (the
     loader rejects it); values read from a vector drawing may be `primary` only with
     J. C. Travers's approval, recorded here.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-29).

## TC-700 vanderhart_2007 (van der Hart, Phys. Rev. A 76, 043405 (2007)): time-dependent R-matrix rates of Ar at 390 nm; the first vector figure (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/vanderhart_2007.toml`,
  `tools/extract/vanderhart_2007.py`, `tools/extract/_figure.py`,
  `data/values/ionisation/Ar/vanderhart_2007__*.csv`;
  `optmat.gas.ionisation_validation.rmatrix_rates`, `docs/ionisation_rates.md`.
- **Transcribed:** Table I (the rates of Ar at 0.48, 0.75 and 1.50e14 W/cm2 with one
  and with two Ar+ target states; the library's cells print the times sign as a
  backspace and run the exponent into the 10, read by the script's check of that
  shape, every cell checked against the image). Fig. 4, a vector drawing, read from the
  PDF by data rule 8 (TC-699): the nine circles at intensities Table I does not print
  (the time-dependent rates), and the 1221 vertices of the R-matrix Floquet curve
  within the frame (van der Hart 2006's, `reproduced`). The axes are calibrated from
  the drawing's ticks (x at 0.25e14 steps, y 1e8 to 1e14 in two-decade steps; every
  tick within 0.001 pt).
- **Checked:** the figure's circles at Table I's intensities are 1.013, 1.056 and
  1.003 times the table's one-state rates; the script fails if one strays beyond 6 %.
  The intensities come out at round values (0.250, 0.480, 0.650 ...). The overlay of
  the extracted circles and vertices on the rendered figure matches every marker and
  the line through its resonances (inspected 2026-09-29). Uncertainty: 6 % (the
  table check), 10 % at 2.5e14 W/cm2 (the paper's).
- **Doubt:** the calculation's ionisation energy of Ar is not stated; the polarisation
  is not stated in words (recorded as linear, from the paper's 'm = 0' counting).
- **Status:** verified (2026-09-29).

## TC-701 vanderhart_2006 (van der Hart, Phys. Rev. A 73, 023417 (2006)): R-matrix Floquet rates of He, Ne, Ar at 390 nm, read from an image; the default against them (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/vanderhart_2006.toml`,
  `tools/extract/vanderhart_2006.py`, `data/values/ionisation/{He,Ne,Ar}/vanderhart_2006__*.csv`;
  `rmatrix_rates`, `tests/test_ionisation_validation.py`, `docs/ionisation_rates.md`,
  `docs/gallery/plot_ionisation_rmatrix.py`.
- **Transcribed:** Fig. 6, an image embedded in the PDF (900 x 635 pixels, 300 dpi),
  read from its native pixels by data rule 8: the frame and inward ticks found in the
  image and checked against the calibration written in the script (every tick within
  0.3 pixel); each curve traced column by column from its crossing of the 1.30e14 W/cm2
  column (Ar above Ne above He there) and sampled every 0.05e14 W/cm2 on its smooth
  part: He 1.05-2.45 (29), Ne 0.90-2.10 (23), Ar 0.65-1.90 (25), without the peaks of
  Ne's resonances at 1.01 and 1.45e14 and Ar's 3d at 0.90e14, where the curve changes
  by some 40 % within a pixel. A sample in a gap of the dashes is interpolated between
  the nearest traced columns within 10 pixels; each value's pixel is in its printed
  cell. One pixel is 3.4 % in the rate.
- **Checked:** the Ar samples are 0.97 to 1.04 times TC-700's vector copy of the same
  curve (median 1.004; 1.37 on the 3d peak, left out); the script and a test fail
  beyond 5 % and 4 %. The overlay of the samples on the image was inspected. Hence 5 %.
- **Finding (helium):** Parker et al.'s two-electron rate is 0.96 to 1.25 times the
  Floquet rate away from the resonance at 1.5e14 W/cm2 (0.8 on geometric average, with
  the resonances): two all-electron methods agree, and the Floquet rates are not low.
  The default is 1.13 times them on average (its 1.47 electrons).
- **Finding (argon):** the default is 1.6 to 2.9 times the Floquet and the
  time-dependent R-matrix rates from 1.25e14 to 3e14 W/cm2 (Keldysh parameter 2.1 to
  1.4) and 7 to 12 times at 0.25 to 0.75e14 W/cm2 (4.7 to 2.7), where the rate is
  multiphoton and resonant; the `one_electron` model likewise. Its one-electron form
  matches tRecX's one-electron calculation of argon at 800 nm to a Keldysh parameter of
  2.8 (TC-653): the gap is between one active electron and the atom. It points the
  way Wahlstrand et al.'s measurement does (TC-660), and against argon's all-electron
  static rates, which lie above the model at low field (TC-669). Neon: 1.4 to 3 times
  above.
- **Doubt:** one ionic state in both calculations; their ionisation energies are not
  stated (at 390 nm the rate is a 5- to 6-photon process and depends steeply on it).
  No change to the model follows from one method at one wavelength.
- **Status:** open (argon's rate against the atom's).

## TC-702 travers_2026_trecx: argon's one-electron ionised fraction in a 42 fs pulse (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/external/trecx/ar_42fs/` (`results.csv`, `manifest.csv`),
  `PROVENANCE.md` there (its section on the 42 fs runs),
  `src/optmat/data/sources/travers_2026_trecx.toml` (`ionised_gauss42_Ar_m0`),
  `tools/extract/travers_2026_trecx.py`, `optmat.gas.ionisation_validation.long_pulse_yield`,
  `docs/ionisation_rates.md`, `docs/gallery/ionisation/plot_ionisation_measured.py`.
- **Transcribed:** the ionised fraction, 1 - (ground + bound states up to n = 10) at the
  end of the pulse, of one electron (Ar 3p, m = 0, Tong and Lin's potential) in
  Wahlstrand et al.'s pulse (800 nm, a Gaussian of 42 fs full width at half maximum of
  the intensity) at 17 peak intensities from 4.0e13 to 1.35e14 W/cm2: J. C. Travers's
  tRecX runs of 28-29 September 2026, with a build that adds the bi-orthogonal
  populations of the field-free states (tRecX's own `Occupation` is not a population
  under complex scaling). Tier 3 (`use = "check"`), as the 6 fs runs.
- **Checked** (against the archived table, 2026-09-29): the initial energy in every run
  (spread 8e-12); the pulse as run (FWHM 41.99977 fs, peak field to 4e-7); the norm never
  above 1; the drift without a field (4.8e-9, below every yield by 900 or more); the
  bound populations constant after the pulse; the convergence runs at 4.0e13, 7.8e13
  and 1.35e14 W/cm2 (angular functions, radial elements and order, box, step, ECS angle,
  cutEnergy, operator threshold): the largest change, 2.6 %, 1.3 % and 0.1 %, is the
  stated uncertainty. The cutEnergy part is one-sided: the yields are low by about 3 %
  at 4.0e13 and 1.5 % at 7.8e13. The three BOX 120 runs warn of an eigenproblem of H0
  satisfied to 1e-7 and agree with BOX 80 to 0.03 %.
- **Finding:** the `one_electron` model is 0.99 to 1.8 times the calculation (1.24 on
  geometric average), the most just past each channel closing: the calculated yield
  has a resonance structure (local slope 2.4 to 10.7) that no rate has. The calculation,
  one electron, is 1.3 to 4.1 times Wahlstrand et al.'s measured yield of the atom;
  excited states hold 1 to 30 % of it. So the disagreement of TC-660 is not in the
  rate's dependence on frequency or pulse length, nor in Rydberg atoms counted as
  ionised: it is between one active electron and the measurement. With the all-electron
  R-matrix rates of argon at 390 nm below the one-electron model (TC-701), two
  references point to the atom ionising less than one active electron; argon's
  all-electron static rates (TC-669) point the other way.
- **Not curated:** the chi-loss, norm-loss and iSurff (biased low, TC-703) of these runs
  (PROVENANCE.md), the populations by shell, the convergence rows. The inputs, the scripts and the runs'
  report are kept with the runs, recorded by sha256.
- **Doubt:** the model's ionisation energy is 0.579689 au (15.774 eV), 14 meV above
  argon's; the models are evaluated at argon's, about 2 % higher in the yield at 1e14
  W/cm2. One orbital: how the atom's electrons combine is the open question.
- **Status:** verified (2026-09-29); the finding is open with TC-660.

## TC-703 travers_2026_trecx: iSurff is biased low with the untruncated potential (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/external/trecx/PROVENANCE.md` (the 42 fs section, *Not
  curated*); `src/optmat/data/sources/travers_2026_trecx.toml` (the record's notes, and
  `isurff_cos8_Ar_m0`, `isurff_cos8_Ar_m1`, `isurff_cos8_He`); `docs/ionisation_rates.md`.
- **Checked:**
  - In the 42 fs argon runs (TC-702), iSurff is 1.4 to 23 % below the ionised fraction.
    The shortfall is least at 4.0e13 W/cm2 and largest at 5.0e13, just above a channel
    closing.
  - The shortfall shrinks as the surface moves out: at 1.35e14 it is 10.8 % at
    BOX = 80 and 6.6 % at 120.
  - It is not the infinite-time part of iSurff, which is at most 0.3 % of the total.
  - J. C. Travers's runs with the same pulse and the potential switched off between 60
    and 80 bohr, at 4.0e13, 5.0e13, 7.8e13 and 1.35e14 W/cm2: the truncated potential
    has 41 bound states, all projected, so its 1 - bound is complete. iSurff equals it
    to 0.04 to 0.15 % below 1.35e14, and to 1.7 % at 1.35e14, where summing the
    spectrum on every second momentum point changes iSurff by 0.8 %. The norm-loss
    equals it to 0.5 % or better.
  - So the shortfall comes from the Coulomb tail at the tSurff surface. tSurff maps the
    flux through the surface onto free-electron (Volkov) waves, which assumes no
    potential there.
  - The table and script of the check are recorded by sha256 in PROVENANCE.md.
- **Decision:**
  - The 6 fs iSurff yields (TC-666) are lower bounds, not one side of a spread: their
    inputs (`inputs/*isurff*.inp`) keep the full potential at an 80 bohr surface. Their
    notes now say so; the values are unchanged.
  - No correction is derived. Truncation changes the model: it removes the Rydberg
    states above n of about 6, moves the resonances, and changes the ionised fraction
    by -11 to +5 %. The size of the bias at 6 fs was not measured.
  - The 42 fs ionised fraction (TC-702), a projection on the bound states, is not
    affected. The check confirms it: projection, flux and absorption agree when the flux
    is exact.
- **Doubt:** the 6 fs spectra were computed on 150 momentum points. At 42 fs that grid
  was too coarse, wrong by up to 15 %; at 6 fs the peaks are broader, but it was not
  checked.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-29); open with TC-666: the 6 fs yields as a projection on
  the bound states. Done: TC-812.

## TC-704 puchalski_2020 (Puchalski, Szalewicz, Lesiuk & Jeziorski, Phys. Rev. A 101, 022505 (2020)): the alpha^3 QED static polarizability of 4He (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/puchalski_2020.toml`,
  `tools/extract/puchalski_2020.py`, `data/values/refractive/He/puchalski_2020__*.csv`
  (3 files).
- **Transcribed** (by script, Table VIII, p. 11; image checked):
  - "Total" 1.38376078(14) a0^3: static electric polarizability of 4He, all
    corrections (check).
  - Molar polarizability 0.51725408(5) cm^3/mol (check).
  - "Experiment, Ref. [58]" 0.5172544(10) (reproduced from gaiser_2018).
  - The component rows are in the notes: nonrelativistic 1.3838099864, alpha^2
    -80.3599e-6, alpha^2/M -0.0935(1)e-6, alpha^3 QED 30.4738e-6 + 0.1822e-6,
    alpha^3/M 0.01112(1)e-6, alpha^4 0.56(14)e-6, finite size 0.0217(1)e-6.
  - Also in the notes, from the text: the field derivative of the Bethe logarithm,
    0.0485572(14) (p. 5).
  - Uncertainties are convergence estimates; the total's (14) is the alpha^4
    allowance. Level not stated.
- **Checked:**
  - The components add to 1.38376078182, matching the printed total.
  - 30.4738 + 0.1822 (+ 0.01112) gives the printed 30.6560 and 30.6671.
  - The total times the package's (4 pi/3) N_A a0^3 gives 0.517254083 cm^3/mol,
    matching the printed 0.51725408(5).
- **Finding:**
  - Against puchalski_2016's static total 1.38376077(14): the change is
    +0.0104e-6 a0^3 (+7.5 ppb, 0.07 sigma). It comes from the field-derivative term
    (0.1822, where 2016 used a preliminary 0.183(1)) and from the QED recoil +0.01112,
    which 2016 left out.
  - The paper gives no dynamic polarizability and does not revise alpha_2, alpha_4, ....
  - fit/He's electric S(-2) = 1.38376077 is 5 ppb (0.04 sigma) below this total.
  - Theory is 0.3 sigma below Gaiser and Fellmuth's 0.5172544(10).
- **Doubt:** the alpha^4 QED term is incomplete (one-loop only, 25 % allowance). It
  dominates the uncertainty.
- **Decision:** both datasets are checks. They carry the same theory as
  puchalski_2016/cauchy_total row -2, which fit/He fits, so fitting them beside it
  would count it twice.
- **Status:** verified (2026-09-29).

## TC-705 pachucki_2019 (Pachucki & Puchalski, Phys. Rev. A 99, 041803(R) (2019)): the retardation correction to helium's refractive index (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/pachucki_2019.toml` (formula `retardation`; no
  datasets); `yang_2025.toml` (`puchalski_He`: `reproduced_from` now uses the ids).
- **Transcribed:** Table I (p. 3; read on the image, because the extracted cells merge
  the last two rows into one garbled cell): alpha_0(0) = 2.0747883, alpha_1(0) =
  4.0751385, alpha_2(0) = 9.3176426, alpha_3(0) = -4.4176694 and kappa = -0.5069525, in
  atomic units, for infinite-mass nonrelativistic He. These are the coefficients of the
  formula `retardation`, [alpha + chi]_ret = alpha_nrel (a0 k)^2 kappa (Eqs. 29-30).
  Also taken from the text: -1.40e-7 of n - 1 at 633 nm (Eq. 30) and -1.98e-7 at
  532 nm (p. 4). No uncertainty is stated.
- **Checked:**
  - kappa recomputed from the printed alpha_i: -0.50695245 (printed -0.5069525).
  - (2/3) alpha_0(0) = 1.3831922, the infinite-mass static value (liu_1997: 1.38319194).
  - Eq. (30) with a0 = 0.529e-10 m gives -1.3978e-7 at 633 nm and -1.9789e-7 at
    532 nm, matching both printed values.
  - The paper compares with a relativistic omega^2 term of -1.24e-7 (n - 1). That
    term equals puchalski_2016's (alpha_2^(20) + alpha_2^(21)) omega^2 / alpha:
    -1.236e-7.
- **Finding:**
  - The correction is a pure omega^2 term of the refractive polarizability,
    kappa alpha_nrel alpha_em^2 omega^2 = -3.7341e-5 omega^2 a.u. (omega in hartree).
    This is -24.2 ppm of S(-4).
  - fit/He does not contain it: fit/He's S(-4) = 1.5432396, the uncorrected
    puchalski_2016 value.
  - Against fit/He, adding the term changes n - 1 by -0.087 ppm at 800 nm and
    -0.139 ppm at 633 nm. The fit's stated sigma is 0.102 and 0.103 ppm, so these are
    0.9 and 1.35 sigma.
  - It changes the group-velocity dispersion by -23.9 ppm at 800 nm and -23.6 ppm at
    633 nm, and the third-order dispersion by about -23 ppm. The fit's GVD sigma is
    3.96 and 3.93 ppm, so the GVD shift is 6 sigma.
  - Measurement agrees with the correction:
    - yang_2025's measured A_2 = 1.332468(6)e-4 cm^3/mol (formula `he_A2`) is 4.8 of
      its sigma below fit/He's A_2 (1.332497e-4). With the correction the gap is
      0.6 sigma (1.332465e-4, Yang's theory row).
    - rourke_2021/A_R_He (0.52025565(5) cm^3/mol at 632.9908 nm, retardation
      included) is +0.14 ppm (1.4 sigma) from fit/He, and 0.0 with the correction.
- **Doubt:**
  1. kappa has no stated uncertainty.
  2. The derivation is first order in density, with static alpha_i(0). The omega^4
     terms are not given, so extending the term beyond the visible (it reaches
     -2.2 ppm of n - 1 at 150 nm) extrapolates the paper.
  3. The package has no quantity or correction part for the term.
- **Decision:** recorded as a formula, not data. The fit change is recommended (see
  *Implications*) but not made.
- **Status:** open (whether fit/He takes the term, and in what form); decided (2026-09-29) by TC-728.

    cm^3/mol, which is -7.81(16)e-5 a.u.
  - (ii) The revised argon uncertainty line (Rourke 2021) is printed -2.16(15) x 10^-5; it
    should read x 10^-4, since rourke_2021's -8.09(57)e-5 cm^3/mol is -2.164e-4 a.u. This
    line is not extracted.
  - (iii) Table X's "this work" argon value, -2.29548(32)e-4, disagrees with the abstract,
    the text and Table IX, which give -22.9545(32)e-5. The Table IX rows reproduce the
    latter. Not extracted.
- **Comparison:**
  - The new values are 0.064 % (Ne) and 0.20 % (Ar) smaller in magnitude than the values the
    fits now use (TC-71). Argon's change comes mainly from the mass-velocity correction to
    the wavefunction, +0.0529e-5.
  - The effect on n - 1 at 632.99 nm is +0.020 ppm for Ne and +0.041 ppm for Ar, against
    the fits' 12.6 and 3.5 ppm.
  - Barter et al.'s argon value is not an independent measurement (p. 9). It is 6.3 % below
    theory in magnitude, and its neon value 8.0 %. Yet it is the value behind rourke_2021's
    and nie_2025's A_mu.
- **Doubt:**
  - The published version (Phys. Rev. A 109, 012820 (2024)) is not in the library, so the
    numbers are the preprint's.
  - Erratum (i) is not stated by the authors. The original Barter et al. 1960 paper is not
    in the library.
  - chi_0 is static. The authors estimate its frequency dependence at order alpha^5, which
    is negligible.
- **Decision:** the new chi_0 supersedes lesiuk_2020's and lesiuk_2023's for the magnetic
  term. The fit change is made separately (see below).
- **Status:** verified (2026-09-29), against the preprint.

## TC-707 egan_2023 (Egan and Yang, Int. J. Thermophys. 44, 181 (2023)): A_R of Ar and N2 at 632.99 nm on a piston-gauge scale; N2's temperature coefficient (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/egan_2023.toml`.
- **Transcribed (text, inline points; standard uncertainties, p. 8):**
  - `A_R_Ar`: 4.195735(13) cm^3/mol at 632.9908 nm (vacuum), from the 303 K isotherm with
    T* = 302.9184 K (p. 11); `primary`.
  - `A_R_N2`: A_303 = 4.446175(14) cm^3/mol at 632.9908 nm, 303 K (p. 17); `primary`.
  - Formula `n2_temperature`: Eq. (8), with A_theta = 1.18(4)e-6 K^-1.
  - A_R is the electric plus the magnetic term, i.e. the refractive polarizability (p. 5).
- **Checked:**
  - Eq. (8) at 293.1529 K is 3.7e-6 above egan_2019's N2 value; the paper says "3.7e-6".
  - Eq. (8) at 302.919 K is 8.0e-6 above Egan et al. 2016's value; the paper says "8.0e-6".
  - Argon is 11.9e-6 above egan_2019 (the paper: 11.8e-6).
  - Argon against Lesiuk & Jeziorski's recommendation, computed with S(-8) and
    chi_0 = −2.3004e-4: −5.0e-6. The paper says 5.3e-6; the 0.3e-6 difference is not
    resolved. Without S(-8) the difference is −0.3e-6.
- **Comparison with the stored fits (633 nm):**
  - fit/Ar gives alpha_refr = 11.224482 a.u. (sigma 3.5 ppm). Egan 2023 is −2.7 ppm from
    it (0.6 sigma combined); egan_2019, which the fit uses, is −14.6 ppm (1.0 sigma).
  - fit/N2 gives 4.446143 cm^3/mol (sigma 15 ppm). Egan 2023 is +7.2 ppm at 303 K and
    −4.4 ppm when carried to 293.15 K with A_theta.
- **Dispersion finding (Ar):**
  - Inputs: Egan's A_R, gaiser_2018's static alpha_0 11.077183(27), lesiuk_2023's S(-6) and
    S(-8), and lesiuk_2023b's chi_0.
  - Result: S(-4) = 27.965(9), 0.031 %. That is −0.039 % from lesiuk_2023's 27.976(15)
    (−0.6 sigma) and +0.059 % above yang_2025's 27.9486 (+1.9 sigma).
  - Omitting S(-8) gives 27.975(9), which equals lesiuk_2023 and is 3.1 sigma above
    yang_2025.
- **No double counting:**
  - Independent of egan_2019: different apparatus (Fabry–Perot cavity rather than the MIRE
    cells) and a different pressure scale (a piston gauge rather than helium-calibrated
    transducers). The paper presents the N2 values as a closure test between three pressure
    scales, and it does not supersede egan_2019.
  - Not reproduced in yang_2025 or egan_2026. yang_2025 uses the same cavity and this
    paper's B_rho for Ar and N2, so it is correlated but not a copy.
- **Doubt:**
  - The correction (doi 10.1007/s10765-024-03473-6) is not in the library.
  - A_R(Ar) is tied to the gallium point's consensus T − T90. A_303 and A_theta of N2 depend
    on the T − T90 function used (Fischer 2011); the authors give no number for that
    dependence of A_303.
  - The helium theory enters through kappa (at about 0.5 ppm).
- **Status:** open (the correction is not checked; the fit decision is pending).

## TC-708 lang_2026 (Lang et al., arXiv:2607.21261 (2026)): ab initio polarizability, Cauchy moments and magnetic susceptibility of N2 at 303 K; N2's first magnetic term (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/lang_2026.toml`.
- **Transcribed:**
  - Eq. (53), p. 14, at 303 K: alpha_0 = 11.717(13), alpha_2 = 29.928(80), alpha_4 = 100.62(82), alpha_6 = 383(38) a.u. These are stored as S(-2) to S(-8) (`cauchy_303K`, k = 2; alpha_6 carries a flat 10 %). Also chi_0 = -1.75(9)e-4 a.u. (`chi0_303K`, a flat 5 %, level not stated).
  - p. 15, the semi-empirical values: alpha_0(303 K) = 11.735962 ("no worse than 10ppm") and alpha_2(303 K) = 30.086359 (`semi_empirical_303K`), and alpha_0(273.16 K) = 11.735585 (`semi_empirical_273K`).
  - p. 15, Egan & Yang's measured molar polarizabilities at 303 K: 11.762120(37) at 1542.383 nm and 11.894428(37) at 632.9908 nm (`egan_yang_303K`, reproduced).
  - p. 15, four historical chi_0 values as the paper converts them (reproduced; originals not in the library): Hector 1924 -1.34e-4 (2 %), Vaidyanathan 1928 -1.45e-4 (303 K, 5 % bound), Bitter 1930 -1.66e-4 (298 K), Havens 1933 -1.338(2)e-4.
  - Formulas:
    - `cauchy_theory_303K`, the alpha_series of Eq. (53), 455.6 nm to static.
    - `alpha_n_of_R`, Eq. (50) with Table III.
    - `chi0_of_R`, Eq. (51) with the text's parameters.
  - Electric polarizability throughout; the magnetic term is separate.
- **Checked:**
  - Eq. (53) and the p. 15 numbers against the pdf text; Table III against its image.
  - Eq. (55) reproduces the paper's theoretical 11.743(13) and 11.875(13) (computed 11.743019 and 11.874645).
  - The semi-empirical alpha_0 and alpha_2, with the theoretical alpha_4, alpha_6 and chi_0, reproduce the measured 11.762120 and 11.894428 to 1e-6.
  - Eq. (50) reproduces Table I's totals at R = 1.75, 2.07 and 2.60 bohr within their uncertainties. Eq. (51) reproduces Table II's aug-cc-pV5Z diamagnetic + paramagnetic sums.
  - The 633 nm "experimental" value is Egan & Yang 2023's A_303 = 4.446175(14) cm^3/mol (in the library, not curated).
- **Doubt:**
  - The paper is a preprint.
  - The ab initio values sit below the measurements: alpha_0 by 1600 ppm (2.9 sigma of k = 2 / 2) and alpha_2 by 0.53 % (4 sigma).
  - chi_0 is 5-31 % larger in magnitude than every measurement, and the authors cannot explain why. Havens' neon agrees with theory to 1.1 % and his argon is 6.3 % low (lesiuk_2023b). Scaled by argon's 6.3 %, his N2 is still 18 % below this theory.
  - Papers I and II are cited only as "Paper I/II" and are absent from the reference list. Neither is in the library.
  - The supplement (alpha_n(T), chi_0(T), Eq. (52) parameters) is not in the library. The 1542.383 nm value's original is not in the library either; yang_2025's laser corresponds to 1542.3912 nm.
  - The conclusions speak of "the single experimental result", but p. 15 quotes four.
- **Decision:**
  - The polarizability and Cauchy moments are `check`, not fitted: a preprint, 100 times less precise than the metrology, and 3-4 sigma low.
  - The semi-empirical values are `check`: they rest on Egan & Yang's measurements.
  - Egan & Yang's two values are `reproduced`, the best copy in the library.
  - chi0_303K is `primary`, as the value to adopt for fit/N2's chi0_au. It is the only calculation of N2's susceptibility in the library.
  - fit/N2 is not changed here.
- **Status:** open (fit/N2's chi0_au and temperature reference to be decided; the supplement and Egan & Yang 2023/2024 to be curated).

## TC-709 garberoglio_2023 (Garberoglio et al., J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 52, 031502 (2023)): the metrology review; helium's relativistic A_mu (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/garberoglio_2023.toml`.
- **Transcribed:** p. 30, helium's molar magnetic term A_mu = -7.92128(13)e-6 cm^3/mol (16 ppm, level not stated). This is the reviewers' conversion of Puchalski, Lesiuk & Jeziorski's relativistic susceptibility (Ref. 80, "in preparation", published as Phys. Rev. A 108, 042812 (2023)). The original is not in the library, so this copy is reproduced and is the best one available. Nothing else is transcribed. Every other optical number is another paper's, and each is already curated from its original or is not a number:
  - Table I = puchalski_2020;
  - the p. 25 molar polarizabilities = gaiser_2018 and puchalski_2020;
  - the p. 30 uncertainties of lesiuk_2020 and lesiuk_2023.
- **Checked:**
  - The A_mu value and the p. 9, 14, 25, 30 and 40 statements against the pdf text.
  - Table I's contributions sum to its total, 1.38376078(14). That total is 7 ppb above puchalski_2016's static 1.38376077(14): the Bethe-logarithm derivative term changed from 0.000000183 to 0.0000001822, and an alpha^3/m recoil term of 0.00000001112 was added.
  - A_mu/(0.3738031 cm^3/mol per a.u.) gives chi_0 = -2.119105e-5 a.u. That is 1.4e-4 of itself below fit/He's Bruch & Weinhold value (-2.1194(1)e-5, about 3 of its sigma) and a change of 2.1e-9 in helium's refractive polarizability.
  - The p. 9 ratio A_mu/A_eps ≈ -1.53e-5 agrees with fit/He (-1.532e-5).
- **Doubt:** the library copy is in a preprint-like layout ("Dated: 21 July 2023"), and its pages are the pdf's, not the journal's. Identity is VALIDATED_WITH_WARNINGS.
- **Decision:**
  - A_mu_He is `reproduced`: fit/He's chi0_au could move to -2.119105e-5 (2 ppb; optional).
  - The record is otherwise a citation for the review's statements.
  - In Table IV, He A_eps and all three A_mu agree with optmat's backbones, and experiment beats theory for Ne and Ar A_eps (the gaiser_2018 anchor).
  - The review's B_R sources (Garberoglio & Harvey 2020; Hellmann et al. 2021) are not in the library.
  - The review has nothing for Kr, Xe or molecular susceptibilities, and no molecular refractivity virial.
- **Status:** verified (2026-09-29).

## TC-712 wilmouth_2019 (Wilmouth & Sayres, JQSRT 234, 32 (2019)): BBCES Rayleigh cross sections at 333-363 nm; methane resolved (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/wilmouth_2019.toml`.
- **Transcribed:**
  - No printed cross sections: they are in Figs. 2-4 only (218 wavelengths, raster).
  - Text: the mean ratio of measured to n-based cross sections over 333-363 nm (p. 37):
    Ar 0.998, CO2 0.990, SF6 0.978, CH4 0.778. Mean 1-sigma uncertainty (p. 35): 2.5, 1.9,
    1.6 and 1.6 %, including 1.3 % from the path length (the N2 reference), 0.3 %
    temperature and 0.1 % pressure. SF6 was raised by 0.1 % for purity.
  - Table 1 (image checked): identical to wilmouth_2020's Table 1 (Sneep & Ubachs's
    formulas; N = 2.5469e19 cm^-3). F_k = 1 except CO2 (1.1364 + 2.53e-11 nu^2).
  - Eq. (4), image checked: CH4 (n - 1) x 10^8 = 40161.8 + 4.75e-6 nu^2, at 288.15 K and
    101325 Pa (ideal), from the measured cross sections with F_k = 1. Recorded as
    formula `CH4_eq4`.
- **Reconstructed (not printed):** `band_{Ar,CO2,SF6,CH4}` are cross sections at 348.0 nm,
  each the printed ratio times Table 1's n-based value there.
  - Ar 2.625e-26, CO2 7.761e-26 (F_k 1.1573), SF6 1.945e-25, CH4 6.756e-26 cm^2.
  - Each carries the printed mean relative 1-sigma. `use = "check"`.
  - This is the same kind of reconstruction as zhao_2026's A_R_1566.
  - It assumes a flat ratio over the band. For CH4, Eq. (4) against Table 1 runs
    0.781-0.775 (mean 0.7780, reproducing the printed 0.778). Eq. (4) at 348.0 nm gives
    6.7552e-26 against the reconstruction's 6.7556e-26.
- **Checked:**
  - Eq. (4) reproduces the printed CH4 mean ratio.
  - Against wilmouth_2020's Eq. (5), cross sections differ by -0.6 to +0.4 %; against its
    Eq. (7), by -1.1 to -0.4 % over 333-363 nm.
- **Against the fits** (alpha measured / alpha model - 1; electric; the fits' own
  statistical uncertainties are 0.005-0.03 %, negligible):

  | Gas | This paper, 348 nm | wilmouth_2020 reconstructed, 280.5 nm |
  |---|---|---|
  | Ar | +0.01 % (0.0 sigma) | +0.49 % (+0.3 sigma) |
  | CO2 | +0.34 % (+0.4 sigma) | +0.38 % (+0.4 sigma) |
  | SF6 | +1.82 % (+2.3 sigma) | +2.01 % (+2.1 sigma) |
  | CH4 | +0.88 % (+1.1 sigma) | +0.32 % (+0.3 sigma) |

  The n-based formulas the papers compare with differ from the fits by: Ar +0.10 %, CO2
  +0.85 %, SF6 +3.0 % (+4.2 % at 280 nm), and **CH4 +14.4 %**.
- **Finding (CH4, TC-150):** these data resolve the discrepancy in favour of the
  refractive level.
  - Sneep & Ubachs's CH4 formula (sneep_2005 `ch4_eq18`, from Hohm's polarizabilities)
    sits a flat **+14.3 % above fit/CH4 in alpha (n - 1)** at 325-633 nm. That is a level
    error of the formula, not dispersion.
  - The "22 % disagreement" the authors report is this error. Their measured cross
    sections are +0.9 +- 0.8 % (333-363 nm) and +0.3 +- 1.0 % (264-297 nm) from the
    refractive fit.
  - The CH4 outliers of TC-150 remain outliers against BBCES: Sneep's 532 nm CRDS
    (+5.4 %, 5.8 sigma) and Ityaksov's 198-270 nm CRDS (+12 to +20 %). Eq. (4)
    extrapolated gives -0.5 % at 532 nm.
  - The index-based predictions quoted in TC-150 (Sneep +14 %, Ityaksov +10-14 %) are
    `ch4_eq18`'s level error, not evidence against refraction.
- **Finding (SF6):** both BBCES papers lie about 2 % above fit/SF6 in alpha (2.1-2.3 sigma
  each; correlated through the shared 1.3 % path length, 0.65 % in alpha). Below 458 nm,
  fit/SF6 has no data (Burns 458-633 nm, Swift 458-1315 nm), so there it is an
  extrapolation. Ityaksov's +5 % at 250-270 nm has the same sign. This is the only
  evidence on SF6's UV dispersion.
- **Doubt:**
  - The reconstruction assumes the ratio is flat and that wavelengths are vacuum. The
    spectrometer was calibrated on Hg lines; the medium is not stated, and it matters
    0.06 % in alpha.
  - F_k = 1 for CH4 is assumed.
  - The ratios are 3-digit means (+-0.05 % in alpha from rounding).
- **Status:** open, pending J. C. Travers's acceptance of reconstructed check datasets.

  `data/values/refractive/Xe/kramer_1985__fig3_Xe.csv`.
- **Transcribed:** Fig. 3 (p. 3), the 26 measured points of n_3(Xe) = (n - 1)/N (cm^3,
  all negative, -9.8e-24 at 115.23 nm to -1.7e-21 at 117.03 nm, vacuum wavelengths), the
  only place the paper gives its result. The page is an embedded scan (400 dpi, one bit),
  read by data rule 8 (TC-699) as `digitised = "raster"`, `use = "check"`,
  `beyond_resonance`: the axes are bilinear maps of (column, row), fitted to the ticks of
  opposite sides (the scan is skewed and keystoned by up to 11 pixels across the plot),
  every tick within 1.5 pixels; each open circle's centre is the centroid of the white
  region it encloses (two overlapping circles at 117.02-117.03 nm split by k-means). One
  pixel is 0.0022 nm and 1.3 % in n_3. The sigma column is the paper's uncertainty:
  alpha = -9.0(+-0.9)e-19 cm^2 through Eq. (1), 0.1 |n_3 - lambda_3 beta| (41 % at 115.23
  nm, 10 % near 117 nm), with 2 % for the reading. State nominal (1 atm, 0 degrees C),
  as for mahon_1979 and ferrell_1987; the reduction then adds a Lorentz-Lorenz factor
  of at most 0.8 % (at 117.03 nm) that the paper's dilute definition does not have.
- **Checked:** against every number the text prints for the quantity: the pairs R = 4.00
  at 115.41 nm and R = 40.0 at 116.94 nm, with the printed alpha (interpolated between
  -9.9e-19 at 115.24, -9.0e-19 at 116.23 and -8.4e-19 at 117.02 nm) and beta = 2.6e-18
  cm^2, give -1.498e-23 and -3.654e-22 cm^3, 2.4 % and 0.8 % from the reading (the script
  fails beyond 6 %). The upper ends of the error bars drawn at 115.23, 115.41 and 115.81
  nm are 1.09, 0.99 and 1.07 times the sigma above. The overlay of the 26 centres on the
  page image matches every marker (inspected 2026-09-29). The package's own fit/Ar and
  fit/Xe give alpha = -1.019e-18, -9.32e-19, -8.72e-19 cm^2 at 115.24, 116.23, 117.02 nm
  (3-4 % beyond the printed values, inside their 10 %) and beta = 2.564e-18 (1.4 % below).
- **Doubt:**
  1. The text's third pair, R = 9.11 at '106.23 +- 0.01 nm' (page image checked), lies
     outside the tuning range; read as 116.23 nm (the centre, where alpha and beta are
     quoted), it gives -6.51e-23, 23 % (1.5 sigma) more negative than the figure's point
     at 116.229 nm. Fig. 2's tuning curve for 60 Torr Xe and 550 Torr Ar (R = 9.17) peaks
     near 116.49 nm by eye, which is consistent with Fig. 3 there. The pair is not used.
  2. The uncertainty is mostly common to all points (argon's VUV index in alpha), not
     independent; the wavelength's +-7 cm-1 (+-0.0094 nm) is not in the sigma and moves
     n_3 by 20 % or more within 0.03 nm of the 117.04 nm line.
  3. The phase-matching pairs (R, lambda_3) are the primary measurement; the package has
     no quantity for the density ratio that phase-matches a sum-frequency process
     2 omega_1 + omega_2 (`phase_match_density_ratio` is for harmonics).
- **Finding:** fit/Xe (range 148 nm to the static limit) evaluated here fails, as
  expected: its effective oscillator at 119.77 nm (f = 0.775) stands for the 119.20 nm,
  125.02 nm and higher lines and it has no 117.04 nm (7s) line, so it is 4.3 times too
  negative at 115.23 nm, crosses the data at 116.3-116.5 nm and is 0.05 of the data at
  117.03 nm (chi^2 = 886 for 26 points). euv/Xe (Chan et al.'s lines, including 7s at
  10.593 eV, f = 0.0859, and continuum) has the right shape: 0.79-0.94 of the data from
  115.9 to 117.02 nm (median 0.83), 0.45-0.60 at 115.2-115.4 nm where the discrete and
  continuum parts nearly cancel, and 1.34 at 117.03 nm next to the line (chi^2 = 54 for
  26, about 1.4 sigma per point, the sigma being mostly common). With NIST's line
  energies instead of Chan's 1-meV-rounded ones euv/Xe moves by 1-3 % below 116.9 nm and
  by 5-10 % at 116.99-117.02 nm (median 0.85). Re-reducing the points with the package's
  alpha and beta instead of the paper's makes them 4-14 % more negative (14 % at 115.2 nm,
  6 % at 116.2 nm, 4 % near 117 nm), and euv/Xe is then 0.74-0.87 of them (about 20 %).
- **Decision:** a check dataset; not proposed as a fit/Xe validator (outside its range, it
  would only record that the effective oscillators are not physical below 129.6 nm).
  The natural test is of euv/Xe between its lines.
- **Status:** verified (2026-09-29) for the transcription; open for the R = 9.11 pair and
  the euv/Xe offset.

## TC-714 laporte_1975 (Laporte, Damany & Damany, Phys. Rev. A 12, 1944 (1975)): density shift of the Kr and Xe resonance lines to 80 amagat; Table I's oscillator strengths (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/laporte_1975.toml`, `tools/extract/laporte_1975.py`,
  `data/values/absorption/{Kr,Xe}/laporte_1975__*.csv`.
- **Transcribed:** Table I, the oscillator strengths of Kr 123.58 nm and Xe 146.96,
  129.56, 125.02 and 119.22 nm (header wavelengths, nm, vacuum), from 14 references
  (Refs. 32-42 experimental, 43-45 theoretical). There are four datasets, experimental
  and theoretical per gas, all `reproduced` with the originals' citations (none is in
  the library). Rows name the reference. Refs. 43 and 45 print two values per line under
  a brace, which become rows a and b. There are no uncertainties. The cells were checked
  against the table image. The header's 119.22 nm is the line the text calls 119.20 nm
  (NIST 119.204).
- **Not transcribed:** the measured shifts (Figs. 2-6, images only). The package has no
  quantity for the density shift of an absorption line. Read by eye only: Kr 123.58 nm
  about 0.13 nm at 80 amagat; Xe 146.96 nm about 0.05 nm at 20 amagat and 0.12 nm at 41
  amagat. Stated accuracy is +-0.01 to 0.02 nm. Selective reflection can only lower the
  shift, by at most 0.007 nm.
- **Checked:** Eq. (3)'s constant, q_e^2/(24 pi^2 m_e eps0 c^2) = 1.4950e-16 m, matches
  the printed 1.494e-16 (truncated). Eq. (2), the Lorentz shift with the background
  factor (n_0^2 + 2)/3, is the pole of the Lorentz-Lorenz susceptibility 3y/(1 - y) for
  a line on a background: the package's density-dependent index carries the shift
  already. With fit/Xe's f (0.2678) and background, the shift of Xe 146.96 nm is 0.0034
  nm per amagat (0.070 nm at 20 amagat, 0.142 at 40; the background factor 1.016 and
  1.033). With fit/Kr's f (0.2050), Kr 123.58 nm shifts 0.0016 nm per amagat (0.131 nm at
  80). By eye, the measured Kr shift follows this. The Xe 146.96 nm shift is about 70 %
  of it at 20 amagat, closer to the paper's f = 0.214 curve. The paper expects a lower
  shift of the absorption maximum (kappa_max) than of n kappa at high density,
  depending on the damping it did not determine. Amagat here is the real gas's
  0 degrees C, 1 atm density (Xe 27.067e18 cm^-3, Kr 26.953e18).
- **Finding:** Table I's f values scatter widely. For Xe 146.96 nm: 0.214-0.28 (mean
  0.257; NIST 0.265, fit/Xe 0.2678). For Xe 129.56 nm: 0.180-0.27 (0.213; NIST 0.191,
  fit 0.1910). For Kr 123.58 nm: 0.158-0.266 (0.195; NIST 0.205, fit 0.2050). For Xe
  119.22 nm: 0.395, 0.381 (chan_1992 0.379). For Xe 125.02 nm: 0.0095, 0.012 (chan_1992
  0.0105). The fits' NIST priors (2 %) lie inside the historical spread.
- **Doubt:** Ref. 37 (Vaughan 1968) is given Kr 0.204. Gerardo & Johnson 1974 give 0.204
  to Lewis 1967. Which one measured it is not resolved; both are outside the library.
- **Status:** verified (2026-09-29).

## TC-715 laporte_1981 (Laporte, Subtil, Bon & Damany, Appl. Opt. 20, 2133 (1981)): VUV reflectance spectrophotometer; a misprinted Lorentz-Lorenz formula (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/laporte_1981.toml`.
- **Transcribed:** nothing. The paper describes an instrument (105-200 nm reflectance and
  transmittance of gases, liquids and solids, -200 to +100 degrees C, 0-150 bar) and is
  recorded for method only. Figs. 4-5 (liquid and solid Xe-MgF2 reflectance, excitons)
  are condensed phases, outside the package.
- **Checked:** the stray-light test (p. 5). With n_0(Xe, 190 nm, 0 degrees C, 760 Torr) =
  1.000995, quoted from Chashchina & Shreider 1969 or Abjean et al. 1971 (which one is not
  said), and n'(MgF2) = 1.430, the paper finds n = n' at N/N_0 = 389 and observes a
  reflectance minimum of 0.05 % at 383. Its formula is printed L = (n^2 - 1)/(n^2 + 1) x
  N_0/N (page image checked). The 389 follows only from (n^2 - 1)/(n^2 + 2) (389.5); the
  printed form gives 345. So the formula is misprinted and the calculation is right.
  fit/Xe gives n - 1 = 996.9e-6 at 190 nm (real gas, 0 degrees C, 1 atm), 0.19 % above
  the quoted value; abjean_1971's measurements interpolate to about 998e-6. With fit/Xe's
  A_R = 14.790 cm^3/mol and Burns et al.'s B_R = 25.5 cm^6/mol^2 (the package's choice,
  633 nm), n = 1.430 is reached at 377.7 amagat (Xe amagat 4.4927e-5 mol/cm^3), and at
  388.8 amagat without B_R. The observation, 383, lies between.
- **Doubt:** the test does not measure B_R. 0.001 in MgF2's index (source and axis not
  stated) moves the crossing by 0.5 %, the temperature and the density scale are not
  given, and residual Xe absorption raises the minimum.
- **Status:** verified (2026-09-29).

## TC-716 gerardo_1974 (Gerardo & Johnson, Phys. Rev. A 10, 1204 (1974)): photoattenuation of dense Xe and Kr in the red wings of the first resonance lines; Table II's oscillator strengths (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/gerardo_1974.toml`, `tools/extract/gerardo_1974.py`,
  `data/values/absorption/{Xe,Kr}/gerardo_1974__table2_*.csv`.
- **Transcribed:** Table II, the oscillator strengths of the 3P1 and 1P1 resonance lines,
  each from two references. Xe 1470 A: 0.26 (Wilkinson 1966), 0.256 (Anderson 1965).
  Xe 1296 A: 0.27, 0.238. Kr 1236 A: 0.204 (Lewis 1967), 0.158 (Wilkinson). Kr 1165 A:
  0.184, 0.135. Wavelengths are as printed, rounded to 1 A. `reproduced`, originals not
  in the library, no uncertainties. The cells were checked against the image.
- **Not transcribed:** Figs. 3-5, k_s (cm^2, the attenuation per atom linear in N) and
  k_a (cm^5, the N^2 part) against nu_0 - nu = 2000-20000 cm-1 at 273-373 K. They are
  images only. k_s is an attenuation cross section (Rayleigh scattering plus other
  processes, temperature-dependent), not the vocabulary's `rayleigh_cross_section`, and
  k_a has no quantity. Also not transcribed: Figs. 7-9 (derived Xe2*, Kr2* potentials and
  A coefficients) and Table I (Beattie-Bridgeman constants; not optical).
- **Checked:** Eq. (7a), k_s = 330 lambda^-4 N^-2 (n - 1)^2 (cgs), is the dilute Rayleigh
  cross section (32 pi^3/3 = 330.7). By eye, the 300 K xenon k_s is about 1e-23 cm^2 at
  7000 cm-1, 5e-24 at 12000 and 2e-24 at 20000. That matches fit/Xe's Rayleigh cross
  section per atom, (8 pi/3) k^4 (alpha/4 pi eps0)^2 = 1.09e-23, 5.26e-24 and 2.01e-24
  cm^2 at 163.8, 178.4 and 208.1 nm, to about the reading (10-20 %). The 373 K k_s is
  higher, which the paper attributes to other scattering. Since sigma goes as alpha^2,
  this tests alpha only to 5-10 %.
- **Doubt:** Laporte et al. 1975 (Table I) give Kr 123.58 nm 0.204 to Vaughan 1968, not
  Lewis 1967.
- **Status:** verified (2026-09-29).

## TC-717 garrett_1986 (Garrett, Ferrell, Payne & Miller, Phys. Rev. A 34, 1165 (1986)) (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/garrett_1986.toml`.
- **Transcribed:** from the text on p. 1175, krypton's
  [n(3 omega) - 1]/N = 2.61e-23 at 146.4 nm (refractivity_per_density, `check`). The
  printed unit, "cm^-3", is wrong: it should be cm^3, the same misprint as in
  ferrell_1987. It comes from the Xe-Kr phase matching of Fig. 9, 1.64 nm to the blue
  of Xe 6s. No uncertainty is stated. The state is nominal (per atom).
- **Recorded in notes, not as data:** no quantity holds the Delta k = 0 conditions of
  the Xe-Ar mixtures (see the decision below):
  - p. 1171: 6.8 Torr Xe with 800 Torr Ar (ratio 0.0085) phase-matches at 439.62 nm
    (harmonic 146.54 nm), 1.26 nm from the 6s line at 440.88 nm.
  - Fig. 11: 0.76 Torr Xe with 202.2 Torr Ar phase-matches at 440.3 nm.
  - Fig. 8: ratio 0.0198 at 1.004 nm from 5d[3/2]1.
  - Fig. 10: 4.04 Torr Xe with 701 Torr Ar, 5d[3/2]1.
  - The Fig. 6 annotations: kappa = 2.48e14 P_Xe and Delta k_R = -0.057 P_Ar, in
    cm^-1 and Torr.
  - The fitted F_01 = 0.26 and 2 beta = 1e-4 P_Xe P_Kr.
- **Checked:**
  - Against fit/Kr, the Kr value is 0.14 % above (27.99 au; the model's sigma there
    is 0.20 %).
  - It is ferrell_1987's 2.607e-23 at 146.413 nm, rounded.
  - The Fig. 6 constants reproduce the printed -1.26 nm for the 6.8/800 mixture
    (computed: -1.27 nm).
  - The 6.8/800 condition gives Ar (n - 1)/N at 146.54 nm of 1.428e-23. That is
    ferrell_1987's 146.542 nm point (1.427e-23) within 0.1 %.
  - The Fig. 10 condition puts the harmonic at 119.12 nm, which is ferrell_1987's
    119.120 nm argon point.
- **Finding (misprint):** for Fig. 10's Delta lambda_m, the text prints -2.47 nm and
  the caption -0.247 nm. The caption is correct:
  - Eq. (12) scales Delta lambda_m with P_Xe/P_Ar, and Fig. 8's -1.004 nm at 0.0198
    gives -0.29 nm at 0.00576.
  - -0.247 nm reproduces ferrell_1987's 119.120 nm.
  - It is not a dataset value, so there is no erratum entry.
- **Doubt:**
  - Fig. 6's raster axis puts the peaks 0.2-0.4 nm from where the printed constants
    place them, so the figure is not digitised.
  - The temperature behind "per Torr" is not stated.
  - The pressure shift of the Xe lines by several hundred Torr of Ar is not given.
- **Decision:**
  - The Kr point is `check`: it is the same determination as
    ferrell_1987/experiment_Kr and never enters a fit beside it.
  - The mixture ratios are not stored. phase_match_density_ratio is Shelton's
    equal-mismatch ratio (rho_gas/rho_ref = Delta alpha_ref/Delta alpha_gas > 0),
    whereas a mixture with Delta k = 0 has N_A/N_B = -Delta alpha_B/Delta alpha_A.
    That needs a new quantity or a parameter (reported).
  - No third-order data: Omega_3 is not measured, and no chi(3) is printed.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-29).

## TC-718 cotter_1979 (Cotter, Opt. Lett. 4, 134 (1979)) (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/cotter_1979.toml`.
- **Transcribed:** none as data. The paper's one dispersion number is calculated, not
  measured: Delta k = -140 p cm^-1, p in atm (p. 135), with
  Delta k = 6 pi (n_3 - n_1)/lambda_1, tripling 337.1 nm to 112.4 nm in Kr.
  - It comes from an eleven-term Sellmeier formula: ten lines with literature f
    values, plus one lumped term fitted to visible and ultraviolet indices.
  - The temperature behind "per atm" is not stated, so the value is not a mismatch
    per atom.
- **Recorded in notes:**
  - An optimum Kr pressure exists for each lens (3-5 atm for the short lenses, p. 134;
    Fig. 1 plots bar), which requires Delta k < 0 at 112.4 nm.
  - The confocal parameter is not measured and the beam is not Gaussian, so
    b Delta k = -4 gives no number.
  - Dye-laser tripling gave output at 111.6-116.5 nm. In the note added in proof it
    was 110.0-116.5 nm, "closely" the range of calculated Delta k < 0 (p. 135).
- **Checked:** against fit/Kr, evaluated at 112.37 nm, below its 125 nm range limit,
  with warnings suppressed.
  - 112.37 nm lies blue of both resonance lines (116.49 and 123.58 nm), between them
    and the effective oscillator at 99.88 nm.
  - fit/Kr gives Delta alpha = alpha(112.37) - alpha(337.1) = -10.9 au. That is
    Delta k = -149 cm^-1/atm at 0 C and -139 at 20 C, against Cotter's -140.
  - fit/Kr's own sigma on alpha(112.37 nm) is 5.5 au (77 %), about 50 % on Delta k.
  - fit/Kr's Delta alpha changes sign at a 110.07 nm harmonic (330.21 nm
    fundamental). The model's sigma there puts the crossing within about +-2 nm.
  - This matches the observed short-wavelength limit of the tunable output, 110.0 nm.
- **Doubt:** the paper does not say whether the 110.0 nm limit is set by phase
  matching or by the dye's tuning range, so it is not used as a constraint.
- **Decision:** a method-only record. There is no measured dispersion, and a
  calculated per-pressure mismatch at an unstated temperature fits no quantity. No
  third-order data: the efficiencies are not reduced to a susceptibility.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-29).

## TC-719 junginger_1981 (Junginger, Puell, Scheingraber & Vidal, IEEE J. Quantum Electron. 17, 557 (1981)) (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/junginger_1981.toml`.
- **Transcribed:** Table I, note 2 (p. 560): Kr "linear susceptibility",
  2.59e-24 ESU at 431.0 nm and 4.37e-24 ESU at 143.7 nm.
  - These are per-atom values with n^2 - 1 = 4 pi N chi, i.e. the polarizability
    volume, stored as polarizability in cm3.
  - The paper interpolated them from Leonard 1974 and Chashchina & Shreider
    (120 measurements, 670-135 nm, p. 559), so they are `check` with
    `reproduced_from`.
  - The wavelength medium is not stated. The values are recorded as vacuum; the
    0.03 % air-vacuum difference is below their three digits.
- **Not transcribed:** magnesium is not a material of the package. This covers:
  - Table I's Mg susceptibilities;
  - the Mg third-order table, whose first row is printed chi_T^(1)(3 omega) for
    chi_T^(3) (image checked);
  - sigma(3 omega) = (4.5 +- 0.7)e-19 cm^2;
  - the pressure-broadening coefficient.
- **Checked:**
  - The convention: 2.59e-24 cm3 is 17.48 au. fit/Kr gives 17.42 au at 431.0 nm,
    0.31 % below the paper (model sigma 80 ppm; the printed three digits allow
    +-0.19 %).
  - At 143.7 nm the paper is 1.37 % above fit/Kr (model sigma 0.25 %). This matches
    Chashchina & Shreider's own offset from fit/Kr: +0.92 % at 140.4 nm and
    +1.55 % at 152.5 nm (bideau_mehu_1981/chashchina_shreider_1969_Kr).
  - The mixture condition: from Table I, N_Kr/N_Mg = -Delta chi_Mg/Delta chi_Kr is
    12.84 with the measured chi_Mg(3 omega) (-5.35e-24) and 11.92 with the
    calculated one (-3.72e-24). The printed ratios are 12.7 and 11.8, 1.1 % and
    1.0 % lower.
- **Doubt:**
  - The residual 1 % in the ratio reproduction is unexplained. It may be rounding
    of the Kr digits or a density detail of the heat pipe.
  - The PDF's first page is an unrelated correction by Byer and Eggleston.
  - The library title drops "in".
- **Decision:**
  - The Kr values are `check`. They are an interpolation of others' data (the
    Chashchina & Shreider scale), never fitted.
  - The measured P_Kr/P_Mg = 12.7 at 431.0 nm (the Delta k = 0 condition of a
    mixture) is not stored. Mg is not a material, and no quantity holds a mixture
    ratio.
  - The ratio determines Mg's chi(3 omega) given Kr's, so it cannot test Kr.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-29).

## TC-720 voronin_2017 (Voronin & Zheltikov, Sci. Rep. 7, 46111 (2017)): the generalized Sellmeier equation for air; its CO2, N2, O2 and Ar terms (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/voronin_2017.toml`, `tools/extract/voronin_2017.py`.
- **Transcribed:** Table 1 (JSON cells, checked against the image): the CO2 rows r = 1-4
  and the electronic rows of N2, O2 and Ar (r = 12-14) as formulas without a form,
  coefficients in e-notation with the printed digits (the cells lose the superscripts of
  `x 10^-k`; the script reads them back and asserts every coefficient). The water rows
  (r = 5-11, 15), the air SSE (Ciddor 1996's coefficients as printed) and Fig. 5's
  single-term formulas are in the notes. The GSE is n - 1 linear in each species'
  density (no Lorentz-Lorenz, ideal gas); per molecule each term is a Lorentz oscillator
  f = 2A at E = hc/lambda.
- **Checked:** (1) A is dimensionless, not 'ps^2' as headed: the electronic rows sum to
  half the electron count (N2 7.000, O2 8.000, H2O 5.000). Eq. (4) misprints the second
  numerator as A_2r lambda_1r^2 (Eqs. 5-6: lambda_2r^2; only lambda_2r^2 reproduces
  S(-2) below). (2) The N2, O2 and H2O terms reproduce Margoliash & Meath's (1978) S(0)
  and S(-2) to 1e-6 and S(-4) to 1e-4 and 1.2e-3. (3) Against the stored fits, per
  molecule: N2 +185 ppm at 633 nm, +174 ppm static; O2 +178 and +277 ppm; Ar -6.53 % at
  633 nm and -6.50 % static (10.357 against 11.077 au). (4) The four electronic terms at
  the Fig. 1 densities reproduce Ciddor's standard-air formula to 1e-5 over 300-1500 nm.
  (5) The CO2 terms' strengths are HITRAN's principal isotopologue's (within 0.10-0.15 %
  in the 15 and 4.3 um regions) and 1.6-1.7 % below optmat's all-isotopologue HITRAN 2024
  bands; static 2.0837 against 2.1212 au.
- **Doubt:** the fitting procedure, weights and spectral range of the pole wavelengths
  are not stated. The Fig. 1 densities (total 2.551e19 cm^-3) are those of 1 atm near
  15 degrees C, not the 296 K stated. The Ar term matches Peck & Fisher's 0 degrees C
  formula only at Fig. 5's argon density 2.879e19 cm^-3 (7.1 % above 0 degrees C, 1 atm):
  it is not argon's polarizability. No CO2 electronic term. The stated 1e-10 accuracy is
  against the authors' own line sum, which shares the electronic terms.
- **Decision:** method source and formulas for comparison only; nothing enters a fit.
  The Ar term must not be used for argon.
- **Status:** verified (2026-09-29).

## TC-721 mathar_2004 (Mathar, Appl. Opt. 43, 928 (2004)): line-by-line refractivity of water vapour and moist air from HITRAN; method only (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/mathar_2004.toml`.
- **Transcribed:** nothing as data. The notes record the method (Eq. 1, a linear
  superposition of Lorentz oscillators in eps with n = sqrt(eps); f from HITRAN's squared
  transition moments, Eq. 2), the line counts (water 31,646 lines, 441 nm-24.96 mm; CO2
  27,123 lines, 1.036-22.6 um; HITRAN 2000), the ultraviolet oscillators used per species
  (Margoliash & Meath for N2, O2, H2O, CH4; Padial et al. for CO2; Eggarter and Chan et
  al. for Ar, S(0) = 13.3; Hibbert et al. and Chan et al. for Ne) and the stated
  comparisons (pp. 929-931).
- **Checked:** the pure-N2 value at 28 um and 833.3 hPa, 2.31e-4 (p. 931), against
  fit/N2: 2.2050e-4 at 26 degrees C (the temperature of the air calculation it sits
  beside) and 2.3135e-4 at 12 degrees C. The value is a 12 degrees C one.
- **Doubt:** the temperature of the N2 comparison is not stated. No Lorentz-Lorenz local
  field (eps linear in density; the successor mathar_2007 adds it).
- **Decision:** method source for the OEP (line-by-line HITRAN plus ultraviolet
  pseudospectra); nothing fitted or checked against it.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-29).

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/mathar_2007.toml`.
- **Transcribed:** nothing as data. The notes record Eqs. (5)-(6) (fifth-degree
  polynomial in sigma - sigma_ref, each coefficient quadratic in 1/T, p and relative

  the captions of Tables 3 and 5, read on the page), and the method (Eq. 2 line sum,
  Lorentz-Lorenz Eq. 4, virial densities, temperature-dependent line strengths, 370 ppm
  CO2 fixed, stated accuracy 2e-4 of the susceptibility).
- **Checked:** the tables evaluated at 17.5 degrees C, 750 hPa and H = 0 (linear
  extrapolation from 5-60 %) against the stored fits of the CIPM-2007 dry-air
  constituents (CO2 at 370 ppm) by Lorentz-Lorenz at CoolProp's air density. Dispersion
  within each window agrees within 0.23e-8 (1.3-2.5 um), 0.34e-8 (4.49-5.2 um) and 1.4e-8
  (3.0-4.0 um); departures of 2-3.4e-8 at the band edges (2.8, 4.2, 4.35 um), -1.25 to
  +2.4e-8 over 7.5-14.1 um and up to 7e-8 over 16-24 um. Level: Mathar is 5.0-5.4e-8
  (2.7e-4) higher at 1.3-2.5 um, rising to 7.8e-8 at 10.8 um and 16e-8 at 20 um; the same
  optmat sum lies 3.0e-8 below Edlen 1966 at 15 degrees C, 1013.25 hPa, 0.5-2 um (within
  Edlen's +-5e-8), and Mathar states his raw theory lies about 4e-8 above dry-air
  measurements.
- **Doubt:** the comparison's H = 0 is an extrapolation; the mixture density in the
  comparison is CoolProp's pseudo-pure air (x_CO2 changed without re-solving the
  density). The level offset growing into the far infrared (16e-8 at 20 um) is not
  explained; it lies where water's rotational band and CO2's 15 um band dominate.
- **Decision:** method source; no dataset or formula (moist air). Not a validator for
  optmat's CO2 bands: at 370 ppm CO2's infrared term is 1e-9 to 6e-8 of n - 1 in the
  windows, below the comparison's resolution except at band edges.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-29).

## TC-723 tang_1972 (Tang, J. Opt. Soc. Am. 62, 644 (1972)): bounds on the one-term Sellmeier formula, and what they say about optmat's one pole per infrared band (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/tang_1972.toml`.
- **Transcribed:** no values (atomic hydrogen only, in figures). The notes record the
  three constructions of alpha_a = alpha0 eta^2/(eta^2 - omega^2): eta = omega_1 (upper
  bound below omega_1; Eqs. 11-13, 36); eta^2 = N/alpha0 = S(0)/S(-2) (lower bound;
  Eqs. 14-19, 37); eta fixed by one value alpha(omega0) (upper bound below omega0, lower
  bound above, one crossing only; Eqs. 20-38), and the refinement with f_1 known
  (Eqs. 39-45). Three text misprints noted (Eq. 21 for 20; f_omega for f_1 in Eq. 43;
  '.V' for N in Eq. 19), none affecting a coefficient.
- **Checked:** derived here: the omega0 -> 0 limit of Eq. (20) is eta^2 = S(-2)/S(-4)
  (the one-term formula that keeps the first Cauchy coefficient), a lower bound and the
  tighter one, since omega_1^2 <= S(-2)/S(-4) <= S(0)/S(-2). optmat.gas.infrared's pole
  per band, E^2 = sum S / sum(S/nu^2), is Tang's Eq. (14) applied to a band's lines; by
  the same argument as Eqs. (10)-(19), it lies below the band's true contribution at
  frequencies below the band and above it (smaller in magnitude) at frequencies above
  the band. Size, from Voronin & Zheltikov's P/R-branch pair for CO2's 4.3 um band
  (voronin_2017): the one pole is 1.5 % low at 2200 cm^-1, 1.6 % small at 2500 cm^-1,
  0.1 % at 3000 cm^-1, 2e-4 at 4000 cm^-1 and 6e-6 at 633 nm.
- **Doubt:** the error estimate uses a two-pole model of the band, not its lines; the
  bounds need all f >= 0 (true of HITRAN's net intensities).
- **Decision:** method source for the OEP; no change to the band poles (their error at
  optical frequencies is 1e-5 of a band's small contribution).
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-29).

## TC-724 egan_2024_correction (Egan & Yang, Int. J. Thermophys. 45, 177 (2024)): the Gouy phase correction to egan_2023 (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `egan_2024_correction.toml` (new, no datasets); `egan_2023.toml`
  (`[[errata]]` of `A_R_Ar` and `A_R_N2`; notes).
- **Transcribed:** the correction's whole text (2 pages): the Gouy phase shift of the
  Fabry-Perot cavity does not depend on the refractive index (the beam waist depends
  on the wavelength in the medium), so the working equation loses the factor
  (1 + eps_d) (corrected Eq. (3)); the reported molar refractivities of Ar and N2
  were "fractionally small by 0.3 x 10^-6 A_R".
- **Applied:** errata of egan_2023: A_R(Ar) 4.195735 -> 4.1957363 and A_R(N2, 303 K)
  4.446175 -> 4.4461763 cm^3/mol at 632.9908 nm (the stated factor applied; the
  correction prints no new values). One tenth of each standard uncertainty (3.1e-6).
- **Effect:** egan_2023's argon value moves from -2.7 ppm to -2.4 ppm of fit/Ar, and
  the argon S(-4) derived from it in TC-707 (27.965(9)) by +0.001 %: nothing in TC-707's
  conclusions changes.
- **Doubt:** N2's temperature coefficient A_theta is not addressed (a common relative
  factor leaves it unchanged to first order, not stated). Whether yang_2025 (same
  cavity, 2025) used the corrected equation, and whether lang_2026's reproduced
  `egan_yang_303K` is the corrected value, is not stated in either paper.
- **Status:** corrected (2026-09-29).

- **Where:** `data/gas/fits/{He,Ne,Ar,N2,O2}.toml`; every stored fit re-run in

    0.003); fit/Ar `thalman_2014/bbces_Ar` (+0.17 %, chi-squared 1.1 for 4); fit/N2
    `thalman_2014/crds_N2_405` (-0.07 %), `crds_N2_532` (+0.25 %),
    `egan_2023/A_R_N2` (+8 ppm at 303 K, chi-squared 5.8: the model has no
    temperature dependence and N2's A_R rises 1.2 ppm/K, so it tests the temperature),
    `lang_2026/cauchy_303K` (chi-squared 26 for 4, the ab initio moments 3-4 sigma

  -1.03 ppm at 800 nm, GVD at 800 nm -55 ppm (0.3 of its statistical sigma); through
  Shelton's ratios fit/Kr -0.28 ppm and GVD -31 ppm, fit/Xe -1.32 ppm and -26 ppm; He,
  Ne, N2, O2, CH4, SF6 change by 0.02 ppm or less; H2, D2, CO, N2O, O3 unchanged.
- **Finding (CO2):** re-run with its configuration unchanged and its N2 partner
  moved by 0.01 ppm, fit/CO2 lands in another minimum: chi-squared 234.3 against the
  stored 239.3 (72 degrees of freedom; 1.5 after the Birge scaling), the same with 12

## TC-726 fit/CO2: the two weak bands below 10 eV as lines; the effective oscillators from 10 eV (2026-09-29)

- **Where:** `data/gas/fits/CO2.toml` (`[[model.lines]]`, `effective_min_energy_hartree`,
  `starts`, description); `models/fitted/CO2.json`, `models/robustness/CO2.json`; the
  accuracy and gas-model pages.
- **The problem (TC-725):** with two free effective oscillators bounded at 0.225
  hartree (202 nm), the lowest minimum put one on the bound with f = 0.0033. Tried in
  memory, the minimum follows the bound: bound 0.27 hartree, chi-squared 207.3 with
  f = 0.018 on it (7.35 eV); bound 0.30, 243.6 with no oscillator below 11.8 eV;
  the GVD at 250 nm varies by 25 % across these. chan_1993_co2 (Table 2, curated) shows
  CO2's only strength below 10 eV is two weak diffuse bands, 1Delta_u (f = 0.00565,
  about 8.38 eV) and 1Pi_g (0.00753, about 9.30 eV), and none at 6-7.5 eV: the
  low-bound solutions stand in for these bands with a misplaced and too strong pole.
- **Decision:** the two bands are lines at 147.95 and 133.32 nm (the table's peak
  energies, approximate; the bands are diffuse), f priors 0.00565 and 0.00753 with sigma
  0.0012 each, the spread of the other measurements the table compares (1Delta_u
  0.0040-0.0062, 1Pi_g 0.0053-0.0075); the effective oscillators are bounded at 0.37
  hartree (10.07 eV, just below the strong 1Pi_u and 1Sigma_u+ bands near 11 eV);
  24 starts.
- **Result:** chi-squared 237.45 for 70 degrees of freedom (reduced 3.39); the lines
  fit at f = 0.00601 and 0.00761 (within 0.4 and 0.1 of their priors' sigma); effective
  oscillators at 0.431 and 0.708 hartree (11.7 and 19.3 eV). Moving the bound to 0.40
  hartree changes the GVD by at most 0.3 % at 250 nm and 0.03 % from 300 nm to 1 um
  (checked in memory). Against the fit before TC-725: n - 1 within 6 ppm and the GVD
  within 0.32 % (250 nm) and 0.05 % (300-1064 nm), 0.09 % at 1300 nm; against TC-725's:
  the GVD -24 % at 250 nm, +0.26 % at 343 nm, +0.35 % at 633 nm.
- **Held out:** Bideau-Mehu et al.'s 181-254 nm interferometry (a validator, TC-178):
  chi-squared 57 for its points, against 17363 with TC-725's solution; other
  validators unchanged within 1 %.
- **Robustness:** the largest leave-one-out shift of the GVD at 343 nm is 0.50 %
  (Shelton 1986), 0.20 % at 800 nm (Old, Gentili & Peck); no dataset moves the model by
  more than 3.3 sigma. The working estimate at 343 nm returns to 1 %.
- **Doubt:** the band energies are approximate peak energies of diffuse bands; as poles
  they matter only below about 200 nm, outside the declared range (250 nm). The
  tension between Old, Gentili & Peck with Egan 2026 and Hohm with Shelton's 1986 ratios
  (TC-148, TC-400) remains, and is what the reduced chi-squared of 3.4 reflects.
- **Status:** decided (2026-09-29).
