## TC-872 Vocabulary: four quantities for two-photon data (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/vocabulary.py` (`QUANTITIES`), the data page's quantities
  table (`docs/data.md`).
- **Decision** (the maintainer, 2026-10-08, before any data of these kinds; data rule 7):
  - `two_photon_transition_strength`: the rotationally averaged two-photon strength
    delta^TP of a bound transition from the ground state, in atomic units, with the
    rotational average's convention (F, G, H), the polarisation and the frequencies
    stated (`rotational_average`, not the third-order `convention`). For the response-theory tables of Hattig et al. (1998) and Henriksson et
    al. (2005).
  - `two_photon_excitation_cross_section`: the frequency-integrated generalised cross
    section sigma_0^(2) of a bound two-photon line, W = sigma_0 g Phi^2, with the
    variable its line profile g is normalised in (angular or ordinary frequency: a
    factor 2 pi), the polarisation and the photon statistics (G2(0)) stated. For the
    measurements and calculations in cm4 or m4 (Kroll and Bischel 1990, Shekhtman et
    al. 2020, Drag et al. 2021, Dakka et al. 2018). A profile-dependent peak cross
    section in cm4 s is not this quantity.
  - `excited_state_photoionization_cross_section`: the one-photon photoionisation
    cross section of a named excited level, which sets the ionisation that follows a
    two-photon excitation; `photoionization_cross_section` is the ground state's and is
    not bent to hold it.
  - `multiphoton_ionization_polarization_ratio`: sigma_circ / sigma_lin of N-photon
    ionisation (McGuire 1981's R).
- Two-photon ionisation itself stays `multiphoton_ionization_cross_section` with
  photons = 2; its datasets state the polarisation, method, definition and energy axis
  in their parameters, as mckenna_2004's do (TC-856). The coupling coefficients of the
  two-level helium 1s2s models (Kumar et al. 2026; Kapralova-Zdanska 2025) stay in their
  records' notes (the maintainer, 2026-10-08).
- **Status:** decided (2026-10-08).


## TC-873 saenz_1999 (Saenz & Lambropoulos, J. Phys. B 32, 5629 (1999)): two-, three- and four-photon partial ionisation cross sections of He, LOPT in a B-spline basis, on the authors' shifted energy axes (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/saenz_1999.toml`, `tools/extract/saenz_1999.py`
  (vector figures), `data/values/ionisation/He/saenz_1999__*.csv`.
- **Transcribed:** the paper's own generalised cross sections, W_N = sigma^(N) F^N with
  F the photon flux in cm^-2 s^-1 (Eq. 2), partial by the final symmetry, all
  use = check: two-photon 1S and 1D, 12.65-23.88 eV (Fig. 1); three-photon 1P and 1F,
  8.50-11.95 eV (Fig. 2); four-photon 1S, 1D and 1G, 6.34-8.14 eV (Fig. 3); the 1D
  two-photon cross section in the velocity and length gauges (Fig. 4; the length gauge
  as the vertices of its 80 dashes). Every vertex of each drawn line (634 to 1832 per
  curve), 0.5 % digitising uncertainty; every tick within 0.019 pt. No total is drawn
  and none is taken. Six text values at 13.5 eV (p. 5634) as inline points: 1D 1.3e-51
  (velocity), 1.35e-51 (length), 1S 0.2e-51 (velocity), 0.15e-51 (length), and the
  authors' own complex-scaled CI calculation (length gauge), 1D 1.15e-51 and 1S
  0.1e-51 cm4 s. The complex-scaling values are not reproduced from another paper:
  Froelich and Flores-Riveros (1986) is cited for the method (on hydrogen) only.
- **Energy axes:** recorded as drawn, not shifted. The authors' ground state is about
  0.69 eV off, and they moved the photon-energy axis of each order N 'so as to reach
  the same energy above the ionization threshold. This is what has been done in
  figures 1-4. Needless to say, this scaling changes with the order N' (p. 5632). The
  computed ground-state energy and the formula of the shift are not given. Each
  dataset says so in `parameters.energy_axis`.
- **Checked:** every number the text prints for these curves, at 13.5 eV: 1D velocity
  1.3e-51 read 1.295e-51 (Fig. 4) and 1.294e-51 (Fig. 1(b)); 1D length 1.35e-51 read
  1.340e-51 (Fig. 4, dashed); 1S velocity 0.2e-51 read 0.192e-51 (Fig. 1(a)).
  sigma^(4) 'about 1e-118, or perhaps larger by a factor of about two' at 7.5 eV
  (p. 5635): the three partial cross sections add to 2.65e-118. The text's 'sigma^(2)
  ~ 1e-51' read from Fig. 1 at 13.5 eV: the drawn sum is 1.49e-51. The overlays of the
  extracted values on the rendered pages follow every drawn line.
- **Finding:** the gauge of Figs. 1-3 is not stated. Fig. 1 is the velocity gauge:
  Fig. 1(b) and Fig. 4's velocity line agree within 0.32 % from 13 to 22 eV, and Fig.
  1(a) at 13.5 eV gives the velocity value 0.2e-51 (-4 %), not the length value 0.15e-51
  (+28 %). The gauges differ by up to 25 % at 20 eV (the length gauge is higher), and
  the complex-scaling 1D value is 12 % below the B-spline velocity value. The
  polarisation is not named; it is linear, since the 1S two-photon final state
  appears.
- **Not taken:** the ion-yield estimates for Kobayashi et al.'s experiment and for
  four-photon ionisation at 7.5 eV (no quantity holds them, and they rest on assumed
  densities and volumes). Copies of these curves in mihelic_2021 and
  nikolopoulos_2001 (Fig. 3 in each) are not taken.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-08).

## TC-874 mihelic_2021 (Mihelič & Horvat, Phys. Rev. A 103, 043108 (2021)): two-, three- and four-photon partial ionisation cross sections of He below and above the one-photon threshold, ECS (2026-10-08)

  (on the 1s3p tail); the parenthesised errors per point, their level not stated, none

  extrapolated to 1e10 W/cm2 (5.1, 550, 2.2 x 10^-52 at 61.4, 58.4, 56.0 nm, p. 5)
  inline. All use = check, the house convention for the gases' multiphoton cross sections
  (as uiterwaal_1998): none is fitted. Not taken: Table 2's H2 row (Chung et al.'s measurement),
  Table 1 (no quantity holds a yield's exponent), Figs. 1-3 (images; Fig. 3's values at
  2e13 and 5e13 W/cm2 exist only there).

  LOPT values against Table 2's column; Eq. 5 with Table 1's exponents extrapolates
  Table 2 to 1e10 W/cm2 as 5.19 (61.4 nm; printed 5.1) and 2.06 (56.0 nm; 2.2); the
  LOPT column against nikolopoulos_2001's figure files: its Fig. 3 (the D wave) gives

  -0.46; Table 1's stated errors allow 1100 to 5800): Table 1's n1 at 58.4 nm, the

  rotation interpolated out, each curve traced and its line style (solid, dashed,
  dash-dot, dash-double-dot) checked by script; samples within about a line width of

  energy axis is the photon energy; the calculation uses HF energies except the

  lines A, B, C, a, b, c lie at Table III's energies within 0.045 eV (Fig. 2's A 0.071)

## TC-879 mcguire_1981 (McGuire, Phys. Rev. A 24, 835 (1981)): central-potential two-photon cross sections and circular/linear ratios of Ne, Ar, Kr and Xe, read from the scanned figures (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/mcguire_1981.toml`, `tools/extract/mcguire_1981.py`
  (raster figures, 1-bit page scans at about 600 dpi).
- **Transcribed:** the paper's own lowest-order sigma_2^C (circular polarisation; cm4 s,
  W = sigma Phi^2, Eq. 1) and R = sigma_2^C / sigma_2^L of Figs. 1-4, against the photon
  wavelength in angstrom: Ne 593-1120, Ar 829-1390, Kr 960-1600, Xe 1120-1940 angstrom
  (sigma, 75-105 points each), R over 594-1100, 830-1390, 946-1560, 1152-1860 angstrom
  (50-98 points each); all use = check. The method: an approximate Hermann-Skillman
  central potential with an exact characteristic Green's function, jl coupling,
  dipole-length matrix elements; each Green's function's ionisation energy adjusted so
  that the nearest resonance of each series lies at its experimental (Moore) level, the
  higher members moving with it, and the 'differences of as much as twenty-five percent'
  at the boundaries of the spectral ranges smoothed over (p. 835). Xe's step at 1843
  angstrom is the 2P1/2 channel closing; the Beutler autoionising structure above it is
  neglected (p. 844). sigma_2^L is not stored: it is sigma_2^C / R. Not taken: the
  three-photon Figs. 5-8 (not read in this curation), Fig. 1's dashed 3d'' enlargement
  (and the solid line from 611 to 617 angstrom that it crosses), Fig. 2's LS-coupling
  circles and its triangles (Pindzola and Kelly's sigma_L converted with McGuire's R),
  Tables I-IV (binding energies below the ion limits, experimental and model; not
  `level_energy`), V (algebra) and VI (Xe lifetimes).
- **Checked:** the wavelength axis is piecewise linear (expanded at resonances): each
  segment calibrated from its own ticks, worst residual 0.3-2.9 pixels; segments of a
  single unchecked division left out (Ar 950-1000; Kr 1100-1160, 1240-1250; Xe
  1400-1460, 1480-1500 angstrom). Log axes calibrated decade by decade (residuals within
  4.0 pixels; 265-335 pixels per decade). Xe's drawn step reads 1843.1 angstrom against
  the printed 1843. McCown et al.'s quotation of this Xe value at 193 nm (mccown_1982,
  8e-32 cm4 W-1, circular) times hbar omega is 8.23e-50 cm4 s; the curve reads 8.36e-50 at
  1930 angstrom (+1.5 %), and R there (1.15-1.20 at 1840-1860 angstrom) puts sigma_L
  13-17 % lower, against their '~20 % lower'. Overlays of the values mapped back through
  the calibration on the page images inspected. Digitising uncertainty 5 % (sigma).
- **Finding:** the drawn 'R = 1.5' line reads 1.57 (Ne), 1.62-1.65 (Ar), 1.67-1.71 (Kr)
  and 1.50-1.52 (Xe) on the figures' right axes, and Kr's curve reads up to 1.58 where it
  meets the line although R <= 3/2 by Eqs. 3a-3b: the R values of Ne, Ar and Kr may be
  high by up to 5, 10 and 14 % (their stated uncertainties). Whether the sigma curves
  share the offset cannot be told from the figures; for Xe the McCown check holds to
  1.5 %.
- **Doubt:** the text puts Fig. 1 'at 1 A per division near the 3d resonances' (p. 837);
  the axis is 5 angstrom per division there and 1 angstrom per division only from 592 to
  604 (4d, 5s); the figure is followed. The top axes' ticks lie up to 12 pixels (median
  2-5.5) right of the bottom ones carried along the frame: a drawing offset, part of the
  wavelength uncertainty (at most 0.1 angstrom in the 1-angstrom segments, 6 angstrom in
  the 50-angstrom ones). No values at the resonance peaks or steep flanks (the trace's
  run-height rule), nor of R where it touches the R = 1.5 line.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-08).

  and 2 omega screening), left for a later round; Fig. 12 (sigma_2 F / sigma_1), Fig. 5,

## TC-884 mccown_1982 (McCown, Ediger & Eden, Phys. Rev. A 26, 3318 (1982)): the two-photon ionisation coefficient of Xe at 193 nm (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/mccown_1982.toml`, `tools/extract/mccown_1982.py`
  (Table I, `tbl_0641e78d7d33`, JSON cells).
- **Transcribed:** Table I's xenon row, cm4 W-1 as printed, abscissa 193 nm: the
  measurement alpha = 4 x 10^-32 (`alpha_Xe`, use primary; ArF, 140 cm-1 FWHM, 13 ns
  FWHM, randomly polarised (`polarization = "natural"`), ~20-146 MW/cm2 at the focus,
  10-300 Torr; absolute electron density by microwave bridge; no uncertainty printed),
  and, use = check with reproduced_from, Bischel et al.'s estimate 1 x 10^-34
  (IEEE JQE 15, 380 (1979), not in the library), Hodges, Lee & Moseley's lower limit
  5 x 10^-34 (Int. J. Mass Spectrom. Ion Phys. 39, 133 (1981), not in the library;
  `limit = "lower"`) and McGuire's circular-polarisation calculation 8 x 10^-32
  (mcguire_1981; linear ~20 % lower, p. 3322). The definition, verbatim: 'dn/dt =
  alpha [Xe] I^2 / hbar omega ... alpha is the two-photon ionization coefficient and
  has the units of cm^4 W^-1' (Eq. 9, p. 3322); n = (alpha [Xe] / hbar omega) int I^2 dt
  (Eq. 10). Propane's row is not taken (not a curated material).
- **Checked:** every cell against the table image and the page; identity on the first
  page.
- **Finding:** alpha is the ionisation rate per atom times hbar omega / I^2, so the
  generalised cross section on the photon flux (Gamma = sigma_2 Phi^2, Phi = I / hbar
  omega; uiterwaal_1998, mckenna_2004) is sigma_2 = alpha hbar omega = 4.11 x 10^-50
  cm4 s at the line centre (two photons 103 466 cm-1, hbar omega = 6.414 eV). Santra and
  Greene quote this measurement as 'about 4 x 10^-50 cm^4 s' (santra_2004), the same
  conversion; the script checks it. Not stored as data.
- **Finding:** two 193 nm photons (12.83 eV) lie between the Xe+ 2P3/2 and 2P1/2 limits,
  in the autoionising region; the authors attribute the size of alpha to the
  7d'[1 1/2] (J = 2) autoionising state within the 140 cm-1 linewidth (pp. 3322-3323).
  alpha is a bandwidth average across a resonance, not a smooth continuum value.
  Independent-particle theory without the 2P1/2 limit (santra_2004, 6.2 x 10^-50 cm4 s)
  lacks this structure.
- **Doubt:** Eq. (10) with the printed int I^2 dt (9.7 x 10^7 W2 s cm-4 at 84 MW/cm2)
  and the slope-2 lines of Fig. 2 (read on the library image: n = (I/12.2)^2 x 10^12
  cm-3 at 300 Torr, (I/21.15)^2 x 10^12 at 100 Torr) gives 5.1 x 10^-32 cm4 W-1 at
  both pressures with the gas at 296 K (fill temperature not stated): 1.3 times the
  printed value, whose reduction the paper does not describe. The published value is
  kept.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-08).

## TC-885 santra_2004 (Santra & Greene, arXiv:physics/0407010; Phys. Rev. A 70, 053401 (2004)): independent-particle multiphoton cross sections of Xe and Xe+ (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/santra_2004.toml` (inline points; no script).
- **Transcribed:** from the library's arXiv preprint v2 (the journal version, doi
  10.1103/PhysRevA.70.053401, is not in the library and was not checked; pages are the
  preprint's): sigma_2 of Xe+ at 12.7 eV, 4.5 x 10^-49 cm4 s (Eq. 17, 5p only) and
  4.6 x 10^-49 (Eq. 27, with the crude 5s-mediated estimate); sigma_2 of neutral Xe at
  6.42 eV, 6.2 x 10^-50 cm4 s (p. 7); the one-photon cross section of Xe at 12.7 eV,
  119 Mb (p. 7). All use = check: Hartree-Fock-Slater potential tuned to the 5p binding
  energy, CAP-Floquet, length gauge, linear polarisation, rate dn/dt = sigma_N (I /
  omega)^N n (Eq. 24; the photon-flux convention). No uncertainty stated.
- **Checked:** every number against the rendered pages; identity on the first page.
  Eq. 15's m-averaged rate 2.35 x 10^-5 a.u. at 10^11 W/cm2, times 6 electrons (Eq. 16),
  over the photon flux at 12.7 eV, gives 118.6 Mb: the printed 119 Mb.
- **Doubt:** the model has one ionisation limit per charge state (no spin-orbit, no
  multiplets): neutral Xe's two-photon sigma at 6.42 eV has none of the autoionising
  structure between the 2P3/2 and 2P1/2 limits that dominates the measurement it is
  compared with (mccown_1982; 'about 4 x 10^-50' quoted). The same model's one-photon
  cross section is 'a little more than a factor of 2' from experiment (p. 7).
- **Not taken:** sigma_3 to sigma_6 of Xe2+ to Xe5+ (Eqs. 18-21, 28-31): no such
  materials in the registry; Table I's ionisation potentials and X-alpha parameters
  (model inputs, mostly quoted); the quoted experimental 4 x 10^-50 (mccown_1982 holds
  the original); Figs. 4 and 6 (a model of one FEL experiment).
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-08) against the preprint; the journal version open.

## TC-886 geohegan_1986 (Geohegan, McCown & Eden, Phys. Rev. A 33, 269 (1986)): Kr (2+1) ionisation at 193 nm; the 6p[3/2]2 photoionisation bound (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/geohegan_1986.toml` (inline points; no script).
- **Transcribed:** the upper-limit estimate of the photoionisation cross section of
  Kr 4p5 6p[3/2]2 at 193 nm, ~6 x 10^-19 cm2 (Eq. 16, p. 273; `limit = "upper"`,
  excited_state_photoionization_cross_section, use = check), from sigma_PI I_min Delta t
  / hbar omega ~ 1 with I_min ~ 60 MW/cm2 and Delta t ~ 25 ns; and footnote 2's upper
  limit of Kr's nonresonant three-photon ionisation cross section at 248 nm, 3 x
  10^-45 cm6 W-2 (multiphoton_ionization_cross_section, photons = 3, the source's Eq. 3
  definition n_e = [Kr] sigma int I^N dt / hbar omega; use = check).
- **Checked:** the numbers against the rendered pages; identity on the first page.
  hbar omega / (I_min Delta t) = 6.85 x 10^-19 cm2 (printed '~6'). Eq. (15) with the
  quadratic lines of Fig. 4 (read on the library image; tau = 30 ns, 296 K assumed)
  gives 2.25, 2.05 and 2.05 x 10^-32 cm4 W-1 at 10, 20 and 50 Torr: the printed
  effective 2 x 10^-32. The printed line-shape factor (sqrt(2) Delta / delta)
  exp[((2 omega_L - omega_0)/Delta)^2] = 24 840 takes it to 4.97 x 10^-28, the printed
  5 x 10^-28. In the photon-flux convention the 248 nm bound is sigma_3 = 1.9 x 10^-81
  cm6 s2; uiterwaal_1998's Kr sigma_3 (1.2 x 10^-82 at 248.6 nm) is 16 times below it.
- **Decided:** the effective two-photon cross section, 2 x 10^-32 cm4 W-1 (p. 273,
  'for an ArF laser with a bandwidth (FWHM) of 140 cm-1', p. 275), is not taken. Kr is
  not ionisable by two 193 nm photons: the value is the bandwidth-averaged rate of the
  two-photon excitation of 6p[3/2]2 (2.1 THz off the laser's centre) with the
  ionisation step saturated. It is not a multiphoton ionisation cross section, and not
  the frequency-integrated cm4 quantity two_photon_excitation_cross_section holds
  (TC-872); converting it needs a line shape. Nor is the line-centre 5 x 10^-28 cm4 W-1
  (peak-normalised Gaussian, an estimated 300 MHz atomic width). The conclusions print
  it '5 x 20^-28' (p. 275), a misprint of Sec. V B's 5 x 10^-28 (not data, no
  erratum). The quoted values (Bokor/Bischel TPA (1-2.3) x 10^-31 cm4 W-1 for 100
  cm-1; Chang & Kim 8.0 x 10^-19 and Bokor et al. 3.2 x 10^-19 cm2 for 6p[3/2]2, photon
  energies not stated) are not taken.
- **Doubt:** the text says the effective value comes 'From Fig. 3 and Eq. (15)'; the
  densities are in Fig. 4 (Fig. 3 shows waveforms): a slip of the figure number.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-08).

## TC-887 hattig_1998b (Hättig, Christiansen & Jørgensen, J. Chem. Phys. 108, 8355 (1998)): coupled-cluster two-photon transition strengths of He, Ne and Ar; the tables' S^0f and K (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/hattig_1998b.toml`, `tools/extract/hattig_1998b.py`
  (Tables II-V, from the library's cells).
- **Transcribed:** the CCS, CC2 and CCSD two-photon transition strengths (a.u.) of the
  1Se levels, He 1s2s, Ne 2p5 3p, Ar 3p5 4p, for omega_1 = omega_2 = omega_f0/2 and for
  omega_2 = 10.49 eV (18 one-row datasets, two_photon_transition_strength, TC-872;
  polarization linear_parallel, F = G = H = 2, as Eqs. 16-19 and p. 8356 state); the
  CCS, CC2 and CCSD oscillator strengths of the ground state to the lowest 1Po level (9
  datasets). t-aug-cc-pV5Z, valence electrons correlated for Ne and Ar; no spin-orbit.
  All use = check; no uncertainty stated. Every cell checked against the table images.
- **Checked:** all 36 rate constants K of Tables III-V (1Se and 1De, both frequency
  pairs, CC and the reproduced SCF/MCSCF rows) reproduced from S^0f with each method's
  own Table I excitation energy and omega_2 = 0.3855 au, within the printing (worst
  0.26 %); Table II's CCSD values within the experimental uncertainties the text cites
  (He 0.2766 vs 0.280 +- 0.007, Ne 0.1650 vs 0.171 +- 0.008, Ar 0.3219 vs 0.331 +-
  0.016); the text's 1.83e-51 and 2.05e-51 cm4 s and 10.49 eV = 0.3855 au.
- **Finding:** Eq. (15), K = a0^4 t0 (2 pi)^2 alpha^2 omega_1 omega_2 delta^TP, gives
  every tabulated K 2 pi too small (ratio 6.278-6.300); the tables follow (2 pi)^3.
- **Finding:** for a 1De level the printed S^0f is not delta^TP but the square of the
  one tensor element S_xy of the level's xy component: argon's SCF 90.23 and MCSCF
  108.66 and neon's SCF 8.799 are the squares of the S_xy of Sundholm et al. (1994) and
  Hettema et al. (1992) as henriksson_2005 quotes them (9.499, 10.424, 2.9663), and the
  1De K follow from (4/15) S^0f, the F = G = H = 2 average of that one component (the
  K is one of the five components'). Summed over the level it is (4/3) S^0f,
  henriksson_2005's convention. The 1De rows are not taken (no quantity holds S_xy^2).
  Neon's MCSCF 11.289 is not 3.3450^2 (the SD RAS of Hettema et al. that
  henriksson_2005 quotes, at 19.170 against 18.874 eV here): a different calculation.
- **Errata:** Table V labels argon's levels '2p5 3p1' (neon's shells), corrected to
  3p5 4p1 (6 errata); Table II's heading prints the level as 1Pe, corrected to 1Po (a
  dipole transition from the ground state; the text's 'ground state to 1Po
  transitions'; 9 errata). Table V's K '1.19 x 20^-51' (Ar, SCF, 10.49 eV), printed so
  in the PDF, is 1.19e-51 (reproduced 1.1875e-51); not held, so recorded in the notes.
- **Not taken:** the 1De rows; the K columns; the experimental argon 1De K, 2.05e-51
  cm4 s (a rate constant, from Payne et al. 1981 and McCann, Chen & Payne 1989, not in
  the library); Table I's computed excitation energies; Table II's experimental rows
  (chan_1991, chan_1992_neon, chan_1992) and SCF/CAS rows (Sundholm et al. 1994).
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-08).

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/henriksson_2005.toml`,
  `tools/extract/henriksson_2005.py` (Tables I-V, from the library's cells).
- **Transcribed:** per gas (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe), non-relativistic TDHF and relativistic

  (two_photon_transition_strength, TC-872; degenerate photons; summed over M_J) and the

  configuration, split from the table image and checked to rejoin exactly; every row of
  Tables I-V (78) found in the PDF's text layer; parity against the term marks; the
  text's numbers: Ne and Ar 1D2 delta = (4/3) S_xy^2 from the quoted tensor elements
  (11.060, 5.6086, 113.40, to 2e-4), He 2 1S0 1.6002, Ne oscillator strengths 0.0043,
  0.1608, 0.1645, argon's 9 % leakage (0.089); the TDDHF strengths summed over each J
  within 1.4 % of TDHF (Ne, Ar), as the text says.

  convention.
- **Doubt:** Table II prints neon's 2p5 4s 3P0 experimental energy as 16.761 eV, out of
  sequence (19.664-19.780 eV); not taken, not corrected.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-08).

## TC-889 shekhtman_2020 (Shekhtman, Mustafa & Parziale, Appl. Opt. 59, 10826 (2020)): calculated two-photon excitation cross sections of eight Kr 5p, 5p' and 6p levels; four printed inconsistencies (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/shekhtman_2020.toml`, `tools/extract/shekhtman_2020.py`.
- **Transcribed:** sigma_o^(2) (cm4, two_photon_excitation_cross_section, TC-872) of
  Tables 5, 6 and 7 (basis sets 1-3), quantum-defect and quantum-defect with NIST
  oscillator strengths, and Table 9 (single path): seven datasets of eight lines,
  192.749-216.667 nm. Row: the final level (Racah notation, from Table 3); abscissa: the
  laser's vacuum wavelength as printed. Linear polarisation; a calculation (photon
  statistics: corrected); no uncertainty stated. Basis set 3 with oscillator strengths,
  the authors' result, is primary; the others are checks. Version of record; tables
  read from their JSON cells and checked against the table images.
- **Checked:** the profile-dependent column sigma^(2) (cm4 s), divided by sigma_o^(2),
  is Eq. (9)'s Gaussian peak with Delta omega_L = 2 pi x 1350 MHz and Kr's Doppler width
  at 2 omega_L and 298 K, both angular: 1.0045-1.0125 (mean 1.008; 1.000 at 292 K) in
  all 52 regular cells, against 2 pi times less with ordinary frequency: the line
  profile is normalised in the two-photon angular frequency (frequency_variable =
  angular, as kroll_1990 and drag_2021). Each normalised column agrees with sigma^(2) /
  max to its rounding. Table 3's lambda_L equal 2 h c / (E - E_G) from its own energies
  to 0.0005 nm (vacuum; air would be 0.07 nm shorter). The text's 4.18e-35 cm4 at
  214.769 nm is Table 7's.
- **Errata:** Table 6, QD, 193.494 nm (6p[3/2]2): sigma_o^(2) printed 9.85 x 10^-35,
  the 204.196 nm cell repeated; the row's sigma^(2) 7.42e-46 and ratio 0.084 give 2.26
  x 10^-35 (+-0.01 from the spread of the regular cells' ratios), corrected. Table 9,
  214.769 nm (5p[3/2]2): sigma_o^(2) printed 8.54 x 10^-35; sigma^(2) 3.05e-46 and ratio
  0.318 give 8.54 x 10^-36 (ratio 1.010), corrected. Table images and the PDF text
  layer agree with the printed values.
- **Finding:** two misprints in columns not taken: Table 5, QD, sigma^(2) at 214.769
  and 216.667 nm, 1.98 x 10^-46 and 2.24 x 10^-46 for 1.98 and 2.24 x 10^-45 (their
  sigma_o^(2) g and printed ratios 0.404, 0.455); Table 7, QD, the normalised ratio at
  193.494 nm, 0.198 for 0.169. The text quotes dakka_2018 as 5.2 +- 2.2 x 10^-35 cm4;
  the library's (submitted) copy prints 5.2 +- 2.1.
- **Doubt:** the bases differ by up to three orders of magnitude for the 6p lines
  (192-194 nm), which the paper calls predictions; the QD Einstein coefficients (Table
  4) differ from NIST's by 2-541 %. Basis set 3 with OS gives 4.18e-35 cm4 for
  5p[3/2]2, 0.80 times dakka_2018's 5.2e-35, and 5.08e-35 cm4 for 6p[3/2]2, about 94
  times Khambatta et al.'s 5.4e-37 cm4 as reproduced by drag_2021.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-08).

## TC-890 kroll_1990 (Kröll & Bischel, Phys. Rev. A 41, 1340 (1990)): Xe 2p5, 2p6, 2p9 two-photon excitation and 2p5, 2p6 photoionisation cross sections (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/kroll_1990.toml`, `tools/extract/kroll_1990.py`.
- **Transcribed:** Table I's 'This work' rows (10^-35 cm4, two_photon_excitation_cross_section,
  TC-872, label abscissa 2p5, 2p6, 2p9 = 6p[1/2]0, 6p[3/2]2, 6p[5/2]2): the measured
  product sigma_tot G2(0), 7.0, 2.4, 4.0 (use = check), and sigma_tot = the same over an
  assumed G2(0) = 1.4, 5.0, 1.7, 2.9 (use = primary); 30 % (2p9 50 %), one standard
  deviation of 15 (7) independent measurements; linear polarisation; the line profile
  normalised in the two-photon angular frequency (Eq. 4). Table II's measured
  photoionisation cross sections (10^-18 cm2, excited_state_photoionization_cross_section):
  2p5 4.3 +- 0.7 (248 nm) and 1.9 +- 0.7 (193 nm), 2p6 3.7 +- 0.7 and 1.8 +- 0.5
  (fluorescence depletion; the level of the +- not stated). Scanned PDF: every cell
  checked against the table images and the rendered pages.
- **Decided:** both two-photon rows are kept: the measurement is the product, the
  correction rests on G2(0) = 1.4, measured for the second anti-Stokes line of the same
  laser (Bamford et al., JOSA B 5, 1369 (1988)) and assumed for the first, with no
  stated uncertainty; sigma_tot is primary, the product a check, never used beside it.
- **Checked:** sigma_tot G2(0) / 1.4 rounds to every printed sigma_tot. Sec. V's
  sigma^(2) = 4.0 x 10^-45 cm4 s for 2p5 is 7.0e-35 cm4 times the peak of a Gaussian of
  the stated 0.086 cm-1 Doppler width normalised in angular frequency (5.80e-11 s):
  4.06e-45 (sigma_tot would give 2.9e-45). So Eq. (4)'s integral is over the two-photon
  angular frequency, and Sec. V's fractional-ionisation estimate (Fig. 8) uses the
  as-measured product. The 0.086 cm-1 is xenon's Doppler FWHM at 80 119 cm-1 and 295 K
  (0.0860).
- **Finding:** dakka_2018 compares with this paper's 2p6 value as 2.4 +- 0.8 x 10^-35 cm4,
  the G2-uncorrected product; drag_2021 quotes the corrected 5.0, 1.7, 2.9 x 10^-43 m4
  without saying they assume G2(0) = 1.4.
- **Not taken:** Table I's other experiments (Chen, Hurst & Payne, Chem. Phys. Lett. 75,
  473 (1980); Gornik et al., J. Chem. Phys. 75, 68 (1981); Raymond et al., Phys. Rev. A
  29, 721 (1984)): the paper does not say how they were brought to its definition;
  Pindzola, Payne & Garrett's range 4-13 (Phys. Rev. A 24, 3115 (1981)); Table II's
  theory (Pindzola, Phys. Rev. A 23, 201 (1981), ranges; Chang & Kim, Phys. Rev. A 26,
  2728 (1982), a configuration average). None is in the library.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-08).

## TC-891 drag_2021 (Drag, Marmuse & Blondel, Plasma Sources Sci. Technol. 30, 075026 (2021)): Xe 6p'[3/2]2 and 6p'[1/2]0 integrated two-photon cross sections by absorption (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/drag_2021.toml`, `tools/extract/drag_2021.py`.
- **Transcribed:** the paper's results, sigma-bar^(2) = 1.36 (+0.46 -0.34) x 10^-43 m4
  (6p'[3/2]2, 224.3 nm) and 1.88 (+0.75 -0.54) x 10^-43 m4 (6p'[1/2]0, 222.6 nm), text
  (p. 25 and abstract), inline points, two_photon_excitation_cross_section (TC-872),
  primary; the asymmetric errors as parameters error_plus and error_minus (as
  uiterwaal_1998); no stated confidence level. Single-mode laser, G2(0) = 1; linear
  polarisation implied (Brewster-angle windows), not stated; the profile normalised on
  the 2 omega scale (Eq. 8). Table 1's absolute values of other authors as reproduced
  datasets (m4): Khambatta et al. (J. Appl. Phys. 64, 4809 (1988), not in the library)
  Kr 6p[3/2]2 5.4e-45 +- 50 %; dakka_2018 Kr 5p[3/2]2 5.2e-43 +- 40 %; kroll_1990 Xe
  6p[1/2]0, 6p[3/2]2, 6p[5/2]2 5.0, 1.7, 2.9e-43 +- 30, 30, 50 %. The library holds the
  accepted manuscript (HAL); its text layer has line-number debris and a garbled
  abstract, so every number was read on the rendered pages.
- **Checked:** the wavelengths are half the level energies the text gives (224.310,
  222.568 nm, vacuum). The errors are the value times (F - 1) and (1 - 1/F), F = 1.334
  and 1.396 the products of Table 3's (1 + u), to 0.4 % (the printed relative -26 % is a
  point more than -0.34 gives). The ratio 1.88/1.36 = 1.382 (printed 1.38 +0.21
  -0.18). Table 2: D(0) of Eq. (32) at 300 K 5.13e-11 s (5.1e-11), sigma-bar D(0)
  9.18e-54 (9.2e-54), sigma-bar / (pi beta) 3.82e-51 (3.9e-51), sqrt(2 sigma-bar / pi)
  Phi_0 5.75e7 (5.9e7). Table 1 against the curated records: kroll_1990's sigma_tot and
  dakka_2018's sigma_0^(2), converted 10^-35 cm4 = 10^-43 m4, with their uncertainties:
  exact.
- **Finding:** Table 1 quotes kroll_1990's G2-corrected values (G2(0) = 1.4 assumed)
  without saying so; the 6p'[3/2]2 result is 0.38 times the 3.6 x 10^-43 m4 deduced from
  Niemi et al. (2005) and Bamford et al. (1987) (p. 26). Khambatta et al.'s Kr
  6p[3/2]2, 5.4e-45 m4, is about 94 times below shekhtman_2020's calculation for that
  level (5.1e-43 m4).
- **Not taken:** Table 1's ratios to H, N and O (Niemi et al. 2001, 2005; Goehlich et
  al. 1998; Elliott et al. 2016) and the ratio 1.38 of the two levels: no quantity;
  Table 3 (the budget, described); Table 4's partial two-photon amplitudes (a.u.,
  without signs, from Aymar & Coulombe and Salah & Hassouneh's dipole elements); the
  pressure shift and broadening of the 6p'[1/2]0 line; Fig. 5's caption units ('m4
  s-1', 'm2') are slips, no value taken.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-08).

## TC-892 dakka_2018 (Dakka et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 121, 093201 (2018)): Kr ground-2p6 two-photon cross section and 2p6 photoionisation cross section (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/dakka_2018.toml`, `tools/extract/dakka_2018.py`.
- **Transcribed:** Table I, 'This work' (the library holds the submitted version,
  arXiv:1805.05669v1): sigma_0^(2) = 5.2 +- 2.1 x 10^-35 cm4 for 4p6 1S0 -> 2p6
  (5p[3/2]2), near 215 nm (two_photon_excitation_cross_section, TC-872, label abscissa,
  primary); sigma_ei = 3.8 +- 1.7 x 10^-18 cm2 for the 2p6 level at 215 nm
  (excited_state_photoionization_cross_section, check). Both fitted with a four-level
  density-matrix model to the 760 nm fluorescence of 5 ns, 200 GHz-wide OPO pulses
  (phase-diffusion model, so G2(0) = 1 in the model; not measured); polarisation not
  stated; the errors' level not stated. Table image checked.
- **Checked:** sigma_0^(2) is defined through Eq. (2), Omega = sqrt(2 sigma_0 / pi)
  I / hbar omega_0, which is drag_2021's Eq. (11) derived from the cross section
  integrated over the two-photon angular frequency: frequency_variable = angular. Table
  I's 'Literature' 2.4 +- 0.8 is kroll_1990's xenon 2p6 product sigma_tot G2(0), not its
  G2-corrected 1.7 (script, against the record).
- **Doubt:** Eq. (3) writes the ionisation rate as sigma_ei I / (2 hbar omega_0) with
  omega_0 the laser frequency; with the photon flux I / hbar omega_0 the printed
  sigma_ei would be twice the usual one-photon cross section, or Eq. (3) is misprinted;
  kept as a check. The published version is not in the library: shekhtman_2020 quotes
  sigma_0^(2) as 5.2 +- 2.2 (this copy: 2.1; drag_2021's +- 40 % fits 2.1).
- **Not taken:** the branching ratio 75 +- 4 % to 1s5 (and the literature average 76
  +- 3 %): no quantity. The 'Literature' sigma_ei, 3.3 x 10^-18 cm2, 'calculated from'
  H. Hyman, Appl. Phys. Lett. 31, 14 (1977) (not in the library; the calculation not
  given).
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-08).

## TC-893 andrade_2025 (Andrade et al., Nat. Photon. 19, 1240 (2025)): eFROG of few-fs VUV pulses by two-photon photoionisation of Xe and Kr; no values taken (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/andrade_2025.toml` (notes only).
- **Transcribed:** nothing. Two-photon ionisation enters only through the measured
  traces and a fitted, delay-independent response function; no cross section is
  printed. The TD-CIS method (HF reference, small-core relativistic ECP, 164
  spin-angular partial waves, surface-flux spectra) is recorded in the notes.
- **Checked:** Extended Data Tables 1 and 2 against their images and against
  nist_asd_2026 (TC-862): the half ionisation energies agree to the printed digits
  except He (12.30 printed, 12.2937 eV) and Xe (6.07, 6.0649 eV); the 'lowest
  Rydberg state' is the lowest odd J = 1 level for Ne-Xe (to 0.004 eV) but the
  spin-forbidden 1s.2s 3S1 level (19.82 eV) for He. Table 2's experimental Xe
  ionisation potentials (5p3/2, 5p1/2, 5s1/2: 12.130, 13.436, 23.397 eV) agree with
  NIST to the printed digits; its 'Rel. Delta' column is in per cent though headed
  '(eV)'.
- **Doubt:** the text says the ECP gives the 'correct spin-orbit splitting'; the
  table's TD-CIS splitting is 1.457 eV against the experimental 1.306 eV.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-08).

## TC-895 bergeson_1998 (Bergeson et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 80, 3475 (1998)): the He 1 1S-2 1S two-photon frequency; not held, compared with NIST (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/bergeson_1998.toml` (notes only).
- **Transcribed:** nothing. The result, 4 984 872 315(48) MHz (1 sigma), is a
  frequency; `level_energy` holds cm^-1 or eV, and a hand conversion is not data.
- **Checked:** the binding energies against the page image (the library's text has
  lost their minus signs and parentheses). Converted for comparison only: 166 277.44234
  (160) cm^-1, 0.00471 cm^-1 (141 MHz, 2.9 sigma of Bergeson) above nist_asd_2026's
  `level_He_1s2s_1S0`, 166 277.437635(63) cm^-1; the derived ground-state binding
  energy, 5 945 204 356(48) MHz = 24.5873896 eV, is 144 MHz (3.0 sigma) above

## TC-898 kumar_2026 (Kumar et al., Phys. Rev. Research 8, 013009 (2026)): two-photon excitation of He 1s2s 1S0 by femtosecond pulses; coefficients in the notes (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/kumar_2026.toml` (notes only, the maintainer's
  decision of TC-872).
- **Transcribed:** nothing. Table I's coefficients of the two-level model at 120.27 nm
  (S_g, S_e, Omega_ge^P = 0.886278 E_0^2, delta E_e/hbar, Gamma_e = 0.869215 E_0^2 a.u.)
  and Table II's two-colour ones are in the notes, checked against the table images;
  the 10 TW/cm^2 columns are reproduced (their E_0^2 is 0.02 % below CODATA's). The
  journal is Phys. Rev. Research, not Phys. Rev. A.
- **Finding:** in Eq. 7 the off-diagonal is Omega_ge^P/2 and the 1s2s diagonal carries
  -(i/2) Gamma_e, so Gamma_e is the population ionisation rate (as Eq. 11, the golden
  rule, also gives). With Phi = I_0/(hbar omega), Gamma_e/Phi is the 1s2s 1S0
  photoionisation cross section at 10.31 eV: 1.691e-18 cm^2 (1.69 Mb); at 19.06 eV
  (Table II) 0.46 Mb. Not data: no curated value of this cross section exists to
  compare with (`excited_state_photoionization_cross_section`, TC-872, holds none for
  He). See the next entry for kapralova_zdanska_2025.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-08).

## TC-899 kapralova_zdanska_2025 (Kaprálová-Žďánská, Phys. Rev. A 111, 043105 (2025)): non-Hermitian Floquet coupling of He 1s2 and 1s2s at 120.3 nm; coefficients in the notes; agreement with kumar_2026 (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/kapralova_zdanska_2025.toml` (notes only, the
  maintainer's decision of TC-872).
- **Transcribed:** nothing. Table I (|mu_0| = 2.03 a.u., gamma = 25.5, delta_omega =
  58, gamma_1s2s = 25.3 microE_h/(TW cm^-2), with the other fits' values) is in the
  notes, checked against the table image. The library copy is the author's manuscript
  with its supplementary material (99 PDF pages), not the version of record.
- **Checked:** gamma I_0 is a full width (quasi-energies carry I_0 (delta - i
  gamma/2), Eqs. 25-28; Eq. 109 calls gamma I_0/2 hbar the cycle-averaged ionisation
  rate), so the 1s2s population decays at gamma_1s2s I_0/hbar. Appendix F's intensity
  conversion is printed the wrong way round; read as I_0[a.u.] = 2.84937923e-5
  I_0[TW/cm^2], it reproduces the paper's a = 0.52 (Eq. 111).
- **Finding:** the implied 1s2s 1S0 photoionisation cross section at 120.3 nm is
  1.727e-18 cm^2 (1.72-1.73 for gamma_1s2s = 25.2-25.4), 2.1 % above kumar_2026's
  1.691e-18 cm^2 at 120.27 nm: no factor 2, the two calculations (complex-scaled
  Gaussian Floquet; finite-volume R-matrix) agree. In the same units the two-photon
  couplings agree too: Omega = |mu_0| sqrt(2/(c eps_0)) I_0 = 0.8694 E_0^2 against
  kumar_2026's Omega_ge^P = 0.886278 E_0^2 (1.9 %), both with Omega/2 off the diagonal.
- **Doubt:** crosswise the coefficients match more closely (Kumar's Gamma_e
  0.869215 against this Omega 0.8694, 0.02 %; Kumar's Omega_ge^P 0.886278 against
  this gamma_1s2s 0.8879 E_0^2, 0.2 %): either chance within Table I's three figures
  or Kumar's Table I rows Omega_ge^P and Gamma_e interchanged. Neither paper decides
  it; the cross section would change by 2 % (1.73 Mb). Also: the text's gamma_1s2s =
  25.2 +- 0.2 (p. 44) against Table I's 25.4* for the same fit.
- **Status:** open (the possible interchange).

## TC-900 rupper_2004 (Rupper & Merkt, Rev. Sci. Instrum. 75, 613 (2004)): argon two-photon resonances for VUV four-wave mixing; the first adiabatic ionisation energy of CO2 (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/rupper_2004.toml` (inline text points, no script).
- **Transcribed:** the first adiabatic ionisation energy of CO2 (X 2Pi_3/2g (0,0,0)
  J+ = 3/2 from the neutral's J'' = 0), cm^-1, as printed: the abstract's 111 112.3 +-
  0.8 (p. 613; `adiabatic_CO2`, primary) and the text's two derivations, 111 112.0 +-
  0.8 via the PFI-ZEKE A-state ionisation energy and the A-X interval of Johnson and
  Rostas (p. 621), and 111 112.7 +- 1.0 via the B state and the B-X band system of
  Watson et al. (p. 622) (`adiabatic_CO2_routes`, check). Levels of the uncertainties
  not stated.
- **Checked:** each value against the page text (PDF pp. 2, 10, 11); Table I against
  its image. Minnhagen's argon two-photon term values reproduced in Table I are
  NIST's strings (nist_asd_2026 `level_Ar_even_J2` 105617.2700, `level_Ar_even_J0`
  107054.2720 cm^-1; the other three identical to rows of `Ar_I_levels.tsv`); the
  paper's own nu_1 + nu_Ex agree within its uncertainties (differences 0.01-0.27 cm^-1, 0.17 with the second F2 line).
- **Doubt:** the paper prints three values of one quantity and does not say how the
  abstract's is formed; the inverse-variance mean of the two derivations is 111 112.27
  cm^-1 (+-0.62), consistent with it, but the abstract keeps the A route's +-0.8. Both
  routes rest on others' optical spectroscopy of CO2+ for the interval to the X state.
- **Not taken:** Table I's argon 3p5 4p two-photon resonance positions, widths (laser
  bandwidths) and relative four-wave-mixing efficiencies (1.2, 1, 4.0, 1.0, 7.5 for
  4p[5/2]2, [3/2]2, [1/2]0, 4p'[3/2]2, [1/2]0; +-30 %): not cross sections. The F2
  lines, 63 439.322(40) and 63 482.257(40) cm^-1 (157.6308 and 157.5242 nm), lie
  below argon's two-photon ionisation threshold (157.344 nm, half of `ie_Ar_I`): two
  main-line photons fall 231 cm^-1 short. The acetylene ionisation energy (C2H2 not
  registered) and the CO2+ A- and B-state ionisation energies (Table IV, text) are
  not taken.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-08).

## TC-901 parker_2007, parker_2009, lehmberg_1995: notes amended for the two-photon curation (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/parker_2009.toml` and
  `src/optmat/data/sources/lehmberg_1995.toml` (notes only; no dataset changed).
  `parker_2007.toml` unchanged.
- **Checked:** parker_2007 holds helium rates at 390 and 780 nm only (two text
  points, `ionization_rate`, check; 8 and more photons); parker_2009 holds only the
  static-field rates of its Table 1, and its notes already say the 195 nm rates are in
  figures only and not taken. At 195 nm (omega = 0.23366 au) single ionisation of He
  needs four photons (Ip/omega = 3.87 at zero intensity, with parker_2007's Ip =
  0.903724 au): not two-photon ionisation. No ultraviolet He rate is held as
  `ionization_rate` beyond parker_2007's 390 nm text point.
- **Decision:** parker_2009's notes now say so in one sentence. lehmberg_1995's notes
  gain a paragraph pointing to kroll_1990 (Kröll and Bischel, Phys. Rev. A 41, 1340
  (1990), Lehmberg's Ref. [5]) for the 6p[1/2]_0 two-photon cross section, and
  recording as not taken the Appendix's upper limit on the Xe2 dimer's two-photon
  excitation rate (W < 3.7e5 I^2 s^-1, I in GW/cm^2) and the dimer photoionisation
  cross section quoted from Ref. [22] (printed '4 x 10^-18 cm^-1', meaning cm^2;
  checked on the page image, p. 88).
- **Status:** decided (2026-10-08).

## TC-902 The two-photon data on one footing: thresholds, coverage and comparison; what is missing (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** `tools/two_photon_tables.py`, the manual page *Two-photon ionisation and
  absorption: the data* (`docs/two_photon.md`), `tests/test_two_photon_page.py`; the
  roadmap's *Papers and data we are looking for*.
- **Transcribed:** nothing new. The tables are computed from the records of TC-873 to
  TC-901, TC-856 (mckenna_2004) and nist_asd_2026 (TC-443, TC-862). The thresholds are
  half the ionisation energy, and half of it plus the ion's 2P1/2 level. E1 and E2/2 are
  the levels OEP 5's support records select. Values are on one footing:
  - cm4 s, with Gamma = sigma Phi^2;
  - McCown's alpha times hbar omega, by its Eq. 9 (TC-884);
  - against photon energy, each curve on its own source's axis, none shifted;
  - interpolated in log sigma between a curve's own vertices, never extrapolated;
  - partials summed where only partials are drawn.
- **Finding, the window of direct two-photon ionisation without a one-photon resonance,
  [I_p/2, E1):**
  - He 100.85 to 58.43 nm;
  - Ne 114.99 to 74.37 nm;
  - Ar 157.34 to 106.67 nm;
  - Kr 177.13 to 123.58 nm;
  - Xe 204.43 to 146.96 nm.

  The 2P1/2 thresholds are at Ne 114.48, Ar 155.59, Kr 169.08 and Xe 184.55 nm. Argon
  at the F2 laser lines (157.52, 157.63 nm; TC-900), Kr at 193 nm and Xe at 248 nm are
  below their thresholds. Xe at 193 nm is between its two.
- **Finding, per gas (ratios to the first-named calculation, off resonance):**
  - **He:** Saenz & Lambropoulos (S + D, velocity), Mihelic & Horvat (0.89 to 1.13) and
    Nikolopoulos & Lambropoulos (Fig. 4, 0.85 to 1.01) agree within about 15 % from 13
    to 20 eV. Sato et al.'s one measured point in the window (61.4 nm, 2.6(6)e-52 cm4 s
    at 1e13 W/cm2) is about a third of them. Sato's LOPT column is Nikolopoulos's Fig. 3
    D wave alone (TC-875, TC-876).
  - **Ne:** a single calculation (McKenna & van der Hart). McGuire's circular values are
    0.59 to 0.96 of its linear ones.
  - **Ar:** McKenna & van der Hart, and Petrov et al. with core polarisation in both
    gauges, agree within 10 % from 8 to 11 eV. Without core polarisation Petrov's is
    0.71 to 0.81. Starace & Jiang's IIC and ESI (raster) bracket them, 0.72 to 1.27.
    McGuire's circular values are 1.2 to 1.9 times the linear calculations.
  - **Kr:** only raster curves, L'Huillier, Tang & Lambropoulos's MQDT and McGuire's
    circular. No vector or tabulated cross section and no measurement exists in the
    library: the data do not support a model of krypton.
  - **Xe:** above the 2P1/2 threshold, L'Huillier & Wendin's RPAE and L'Huillier et
    al.'s MQDT (raster) are 0.27 to 0.61 of Lagutin et al.'s CIPFCP. Karamatskou &
    Santra's TDCIS starts above the window and is 20 to 200 times Lagutin's there
    (TC-881). Lagutin computes nothing between the thresholds, where the only
    measurement lies: McCown's 4.1e-50 cm4 s at 193 nm (natural polarisation, averaged
    over a 140 cm-1 band across an autoionising resonance). Santra & Greene's
    single-threshold 6.2e-50 and the MQDT curve's 5.7e-50 are drawn near it. Lagutin's
    circular/linear ratio is 0.92 to 1.08 in the window; McGuire's circular values are
    2.8 to 4 times Lagutin's linear.
- **Finding, the drawings of McCown's point disagree:** Lagutin et al. and L'Huillier &
  Wendin draw it at its printed value (within 1 %); L'Huillier, Tang & Lambropoulos 1.39
  times higher (TC-882).
- **Missing:**
  - any Kr cross section from a vector or tabulated source;
  - any measured Ar or Ne cross section;
  - calculations of Xe between its thresholds other than the raster MQDT;
  - Fink & Johnson's relativistic Ne to Xe;
  - measured bound two-photon strengths of He, Ne and Ar, and their excited levels'
    photoionisation;
  - the higher members of every two-photon series below I_p/2.

  The requests are on the roadmap.
- **Decided:** the manual's comparison names the comparator of each gas only for the
  ratios; no source is preferred or fitted (data rule 8: every figure value is use =
  check). A model and its references are OEP 6's.
- **Status:** decided (2026-10-08).


## TC-903 OEP 6: evaluation on propagation grids, and the time-resolved loss current as a documented gap (2026-10-08)

- **Where:** OEP 6 (accepted 2026-10-08), section 6 (*Warnings and refusals*) and section
  4 (*Broadband fields*, Q9); the roadmap's OEP 6 entry. Part I is frozen; these are the
  author's decisions for the implementation, to be reported as deviations in Phase 1's
  Part II report.
- **Decided** (the author, 2026-10-08, on the review's revisions):
  1. **No raising on propagation grids.** Section 6 as accepted raises when an input array
     contains a frequency outside the reference coverage (a data gap, at or above E1). A
     propagation grid always contains such points. Phase 1 therefore:
     - adds a read-only availability query (for example `available(omega)`, a boolean
       mask from the support record);
     - evaluates arrays without raising at unavailable points.

     The value returned there is settled in Phase 1, recommended NaN with the mask
     defining it. It is never a zero or an extrapolation: optmat still manufactures no
     value. Scalar requests outside coverage may still raise.
  2. **The time-resolved loss current is a documented gap.** The review withdrew the
     causal-filter loss current, because the spectral factor's phase, and with it the
     time dependence, is not fixed by sigma^(2). optmat supplies:
     - the cross section;
     - the pair-spectral-density yield and its energy, which are integral identities in
       the stated approximation.

     It does not supply how the loss is distributed within a pulse. That needs the
     nondegenerate amplitudes of Q9. It is recorded as a gap on the roadmap and in the
     manual, open for OEP 6 Phase 2 or for the propagation code. A band-centroid rate (the
     paired solprop proposal's first phase) is unaffected.
- **Status:** decided (2026-10-08).

## TC-904 vanderhart_2005 (van der Hart & Bingham, J. Phys. B 38, 207 (2005)): R-matrix Floquet two- and three-photon ionisation cross sections of He at 1e13 W/cm2 (2026-10-09)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/vanderhart_2005.toml`, `tools/extract/
  vanderhart_2005.py` (vector figures).
- **Transcribed:** the generalised two-photon (Fig. 2, 0.453-0.840 au) and three-photon
  (Fig. 9, 0.302-0.420 au) cross sections of ground-state He, transformed by the authors
  from the R-matrix Floquet total ionisation rate at 1e13 W/cm2 (`intensity_w_cm2 =
  1e13`; higher orders included; the three-photon autoionising spikes near 1s2p are in
  the two-photon line, 'absent in the true generalized two-photon cross sections');
  abscissa the photon energy in hartree, the ground state shifted by the authors to its
  experimental energy. With them, `reproduced_from = saenz_1999` (TC-873), the dashed
  lines: Saenz and Lambropoulos's perturbative totals (1S + 1D, 1P + 1F), supplied in
  numerical form, on those authors' scaled axis. Every vertex of each drawn line (every
  tick within 0.06 pt; 1 % (Fig. 2) and 1.5 % (Fig. 9) at a vertex). All use = check.
  Linear polarisation inferred (not named); gauge not stated. No table holds a cross
  section: Tables 1-3 (energies and widths of the autoionising states, field-free and
  dressed) and Figs. 1, 4-8 (rates against frequency at 1, 2, 5, 10 x 10^13 W/cm2) are
  not taken (no quantity).
- **Checked:** the transformation, which the paper does not print, is Gamma = sigma^(N)
  Phi^N with Phi = I / (hbar omega): Fig. 1's 1e13 rate so converted is 0.3 to 0.8 %
  above Fig. 2, Fig. 7's 0.9 to 2.4 % above Fig. 9 (two readings of 0.7 to 1.1 % each).
  The text: RMF within 10 % of perturbation theory off resonance (read 9.1 %), within
  15 % in the three-photon regime (read 15.8 %); resonance strengths 30 and 5.6 times
  (read 29.6 and 5.75); 'three orders of magnitude' at 1s2p (drawn peaks 1230 times);
  'a factor of 10' at 1s2s (drawn 7.5); I^2 scaling of Fig. 1's curves (within 0.7 %,
  2.3 % and 4.0 % at 2, 5, 10 x 10^13 W/cm2, which also confirms the dash-to-intensity
  assignment). The ground state's rate at the 2p3d 1Po resonance, 4.3e-7 and 1.1e-5 au
  at 1e13 and 1e14 W/cm2 (p. 216): Fig. 1 reads 4.8e-7 and 1.0e-5 at 0.7856 au, where
  Fig. 6 draws it. The dashed lines equal saenz_1999's partial curves summed, at
  frequency x 27.2114 eV, within 0.6 % at 16 frequencies. Overlays of the extracted
  values on the rendered figures inspected.
- **Finding:** sato_2011's 'Theory (R-matrix Floquet)' column (TC-876), supplied by van
  der Hart: 8.5, 63 and 3.5 x 10^-52 cm4 s at 61.4, 58.4 and 56.0 nm are 0.97, 1.05 and
  0.99 times Fig. 2 (8.74, 60.0, 3.54; 58.4 nm on the 1s2p peak, where the line runs
  from 5.1 to 6.4e-51 within 0.001 au); 6.9 at 53.4 nm (0.8532 au, beyond Fig. 2's
  0.840 au) is 1.30 times the 5.29 from Fig. 1's 1e13 rate converted. 53.4 nm lies on
  the steep flank of the 1s3p resonance (drawn peak 0.8485 au): the line reaches 6.9e-52
  0.0012 au (0.07 nm) lower, five times the drawing's frequency quantum. Not resolved.
  sato_2011 names this paper by a citation string in `reproduced_from`; it can now be
  `vanderhart_2005`.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-09).

  against Pan, Gao and Starace's final length total (pan_1990b): velocity 0.93-1.29,

## TC-911 xenakis_1996 (Xenakis, Faucher, Charalambidis & Fotakis, J. Phys. B 29, L457 (1996)): two-XUV-photon ionisation of Ar at 82.9 nm observed, no cross section (2026-10-09)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/xenakis_1996.toml` (no datasets, no script).
- **Transcribed:** nothing into data. The record states what the letter measured: Ar+
  from two photons of the third harmonic (82.9 nm, 14.96 eV) of a 248.6 nm, about
  450 fs KrF pulse, made in a Xe jet and imaged into an Ar jet; the first photon
  between the 6s'[1/2]1 and 6s[3/2]1 levels (detunings 485.6 and -915.5 cm-1); the Ar+
  yield rises with slope 3 in the fundamental's energy, not 6, which the authors
  ascribe to saturation of the near-resonant first step. Not taken: the harmonic's
  intensity, 'estimated to be in the range of 10^5-10^8 W cm^-2' from Xe and Kr
  one-photon ion signals, the He two-photon cross section, the extraction volume and
  the pressure (no absolute photon number was measured; a condition, not a property
  of Ar); the estimated resonant absorption cross section of the first step, ~7e-11
  cm2 (Lorentzian, g ratio 3) reduced to ~7e-12 cm2 for the detunings and bandwidth
  (assumed line shapes; 'the absorption cross section to these states is not known to
  us'); the ion yields (arbitrary units) and time-of-flight spectra of Figs. 3 and 4.
  Curated by a delegated agent.
- **Checked:** identity on PDF p. 2 (J. Phys. B 29, L457-L463); every quoted number
  against the page's text layer (pp. L458-L462).
- **Finding:** no two-photon cross section of Ar is measured or deduced, absolute or
  relative. The He two-photon cross section used to bound the harmonic's intensity is
  cited to 'Starace et al 1987' = Starace and Jiang, Phys. Rev. A 36, 1705 (1987)
  (starace_1987, TC-878), which computes argon only (it says its approach 'is ...
  applicable with minor modifications to He'), and to a private communication (Cormier
  1995): the He value behind the intensity range cannot be traced.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-09).

## TC-912 fink_1990 (Fink & Johnson, Phys. Rev. A 42, 3801 (1990)): relativistic TDDF two-photon ionisation cross sections of Ar, Kr and Xe, linear and circular, from raster figures (2026-10-09)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/fink_1990.toml`, `tools/extract/fink_1990.py`
  (raster figures of a scanned PDF).
- **Transcribed:** the total generalised two-photon cross sections (J_tot = F^2
  sigma^(2), F the photon flux, Eq. 4.1), length form, relativistic time-dependent
  Dirac-Fock (second order in the field, J = 0 and 2 final channels, Dirac-Fock
  thresholds), linear and circular: Ar (Fig. 3, 0.294-0.505 a.u., 26 + 26 markers),
  Kr (Fig. 4, 0.270-0.437 a.u., 31 + 35), Xe (Fig. 5, 0.250-0.342 a.u., 18 + 23), and
  Xe's partials to the 2P3/2 and 2P1/2 cores (Fig. 6, 14, 26, 11 and 16 markers).
  Abscissa the photon energy in hartree, unshifted (the calculation's own thresholds and
  resonances, J-resolved). The paper prints no table of cross sections; each computed
  value is a marker, seeded by inspection and centred by the script on its shape's
  template in the native 600-dpi page image (ticks within 1 pixel in x, 3 in y), each
  value's pixel in its printed cell; markers merged in clusters (Kr 0.317-0.345, Xe
  0.293-0.302 a.u.) and off scale are not read. Uncertainty: the paper's 'numerically
  more accurate than 5%' with the reading (0.015e-50 Fig. 3, 0.03e-50 Fig. 4, 4 % on the
  log axes). All use = check. Not taken: Figs. 1 (He) and 2 (Ne, against n_eff), raster
  line curves; the Lu-Fano plots; Table I (model and unattributed thresholds, used in the
  checks).
- **Checked:** Table I against its image cell by cell; its splittings are the
  differences of its energies within 0.01 eV. Fig. 6's partials add up to Fig. 5's
  totals: 0.989-1.055 (linear, 7 frequencies), 0.989-1.023 (circular, 9). Fig. 5 against
  Lagutin et al.'s vector redrawing of these curves (lagutin_2017 Fig. 8, TC-880, not
  taken there): 0.84-0.99 (linear) and 0.93-1.03 (circular) at 6.80-8.10 and 8.70-9.28
  eV; the redrawing starts at 6.803 eV, Fig. 5's first frequency 0.2500 a.u. Fig. 3
  against Starace and Jiang's ESI totals (starace_1987, TC-878; 'within drawing
  accuracy', p. 3812): 0.986-1.010 (linear), 0.954-0.971 (circular) at 8.1-9.4 eV. The
  value overlays on the page images were inspected.
- **Finding:** the first computed frequency of each curve lies at or just above half the
  experimental 2P1/2 binding energy of Table I (Ar 0.2940 against 0.2929, Kr 0.2700
  against 0.2696, Xe 0.2500 against 0.2470 a.u.) and, for Ar and Kr, below half the
  Dirac-Fock 2P1/2 energy that the text names as the calculation's threshold (0.2977,
  0.2708), although the text says only final states above both thresholds were computed
  (pp. 3801, 3812). No values lie between the fine-structure thresholds: Kr's begin at
  7.347 eV (two-photon thresholds 7.000 and 7.333 eV), Xe's at 6.803 eV (6.065-6.718 eV).
- **Finding:** krypton (OEP 6 Q2) is given only as a raster figure: no table and no vector
  drawing. Its smooth part runs from 7.35 to 9.79 eV, below the first resonance (the
  calculation's between 9.95 and 10.33 eV; experimentally 10.03 eV): linear 2.03e-50
  cm4 s at 7.6 eV falling to 1.22e-50 at 9.55 eV, circular 1.57e-50 to 1.20e-50.
  Against McGuire's Kr (mcguire_1981, TC-879, circular) these are 0.22-0.39 times
  (7.9-9.8 eV). Fig. 3's Ar linear is 0.78-0.89 times McKenna and van der Hart's
  R-matrix Floquet (mckenna_2004, TC-856) at 8.0-10.0 eV.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-09).

## TC-913 fink_1989 (Fink & Zoller, Phys. Rev. A 39, 2933 (1989)): MQDT parametrisation of two-photon ionisation; hydrogen 1s cross sections, and no noble-gas values (2026-10-09)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/fink_1989.toml`, `tools/extract/fink_1989.py`.
- **Transcribed:** Table I's sigma^(2) (cm4 s) of atomic hydrogen 1s, circular
  polarisation, at nine wavelengths from 924.06 to 300 angstrom (the first just below
  the one-photon threshold, the others above it: two-photon above-threshold
  ionisation), printed '5.530[-52]' and written 5.530e-52; use = check. The wavelengths
  are 2 pi c / omega with omega in hartree for an infinite nuclear mass. Not taken: the
  amplitude parameters t^s, t^o, t_3 (no quantity), Ref. 13's comparison column, Tables
  II and III (2PI from the excited 2s and 3s states, which multiphoton_ionization_cross_
  section does not hold), Figs. 2-5 (raster: H near threshold, a hypothetical
  two-channel model).
- **Checked:** Tables I-III against their images cell by cell (all agree). Every row is
  reproduced from its printed parameters by Eqs. 2.1, 3.2 and 3.9 (Omega^2 = 2/15):
  within 2e-4, 1.2e-3 and 2.0e-3 above the one-photon threshold (Tables I, II, III) and
  0.6 % at each table's first row (nu = 8.50, below it). This paper's sigma^(2) agrees
  with Ref. 13's (Aymar and Crance; Klarsfeld and Maquet) within 0.9 %.
- **Finding:** the paper gives no values for any noble gas, in table, figure or text:
  for Kr and Xe it offers a formula (Eqs. 4.21-4.24; two channels, Eqs. 5.5-5.7) whose
  parameters (reaction matrices and smooth dipole matrices) it does not give; a cross
  section can be reproduced from such parameters, as the hydrogen tables show, but they
  would have to come from elsewhere (energy levels, one-photon data, or a fit to ab
  initio amplitudes, p. 2945).
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-09).

## TC-917 bischel_1979 (Bischel, Bokor, Kligler & Rhodes, IEEE J. Quantum Electron. QE-15, 380 (1979)): estimated Xe two-photon ionisation coefficient at 193 nm (2026-10-09)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/bischel_1979.toml`, `tools/extract/bischel_1979.py`
  (Table I, JSON cells).
- **Transcribed:** Table I's xenon row at 193 nm with excited product Xe+: alpha = 1 x
  10^-34 cm4/watt (multiphoton_ionization_cross_section, photons = 2, unit as printed,
  use = check), an estimate from second-order perturbation theory with one
  intermediate state (energy denominator 16 x 10^3 cm^-1, mu^2 = 1 debye^2) and a width
  of ~10^9 MHz, footnote (g) 'Estimated for photoionization continuum'. The definition,
  quoted: 'sigma(nu_2) = alpha I_1' (Eq. 1) and 'W_fg = alpha I^2 / hbar omega' (p. 382):
  mccown_1982's (TC-884) and hodges_1981's definition; sigma_2 = alpha hbar omega =
  1.03e-52 cm4 s (not printed). The text: autoionising resonances 'could enhance the
  value of alpha given in Table I by a factor of ~10^2' (p. 386).
- **Not taken:** the bound two-photon excitation estimates of Table I (H2, CO, N2, Kr,
  I2 at 193 nm; Xe 5p5 6p and N2O at 248 nm), the H2 measurement (~10^-32 cm4/W) and the
  N2O upper limit: linewidth-dependent peak coefficients that no quantity holds
  (two_photon_excitation_cross_section is frequency-integrated; converting would need
  the assumed line shape). Krypton (OEP 6, Q2): no two-photon ionisation value in any
  form; Table I's Kr row is a bound excitation estimate, 1 x 10^-31 cm4/watt for a 100
  cm^-1 laser.
- **Checked:** the cell against the table image; the script requires the table's
  value to equal the text's 'sigma / I ~ 10^-34 cm4/W (see Table I)' (p. 388) and
  mccown_1982's reproduction (1 x 10^-34), and footnote (a)'s 3 x 10^6 MHz to be the
  text's 100 cm^-1 (100.07). The p. 388 ion-density estimate (Xe 3 x 10^17 cm^-3, 10^9
  W/cm2, 20 ns pulse) follows from alpha as 5.8e11 cm^-3 against the printed ~3 x
  10^11 (2.9e11 for 10 ns): an order-of-magnitude estimate.
- **Finding:** mccown_1982 describes this value as an estimate 'assuming a laser
  linewidth of 100 cm-1'; Table I gives the Xe+ row the photoionisation-continuum width
  of footnote (g), ~10^9 MHz, not the 100 cm^-1 of the bound rows. geohegan_1986's
  (TC-886) '(1-2.3) x 10^-31 cm4 W-1' for Kr 6p[3/2]2 'assuming a 100-cm-1-bandwidth'
  laser: this paper's 1 x 10^-31 is the lower end; 2.3 x 10^-31 is not in it (the
  bokor_1980 record: 2.34 x 10^-31 for a 25 cm^-1 laser).
- **Doubt:** Table I prints the Kr 4p5 6p level at '103,762 cm^-1'; the text (p. 386)
  puts 6p(1 1/2)2 at 103 363 cm^-1, inside the ArF two-photon range it gives (103
  300-103 560 cm^-1): probably a misprint in the table (no value of it is taken).
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-09).

  (two_photon_excitation_cross_section, primary), adjusted so that rate equations
  reproduce the absolutely calibrated 427.4 nm fluorescence densities (Table III); the
  profile has unit area in the two-photon angular frequency (Eq. 3, Gaussian laser),
  photon statistics corrected with an assumed G^(2) = 2, linear polarisation (> 80 %).
  No uncertainty is printed for it (the measured densities carry +-50 %). The adjusted
  6p[3/2]2 photoionisation cross section at 193.41 nm, 4.39 x 10^-19 cm2
  (excited_state_photoionization_cross_section, primary; ion densities +-25 %, no
  uncertainty for sigma_pi). As checks: the single-path sigma_0^(2), 8.7 x 10^-37 cm4,
  and the quantum-defect sigma_pi, 1.696 x 10^-19 cm2. Krypton two-photon ionisation:
  none (193 nm ionisation of Kr is 2+1).
- **Checked:** on the rendered pages: g = 3.298 x 10^-14 s (printed 3.3); Delta omega_L
  = 2.014 x 10^13 s-1 is Table II's 0.40 nm at 193.41 nm (the text's '0.04 nm' is a
  slip); Delta omega_D = 1.313 x 10^10 s-1 is Kr's one-photon Doppler width at 297 K
  (half the two-photon width the text names; negligible); Eqs. (14), (15) give 8.68 x
  10^-37 cm4; alpha = sigma g G / h nu gives 5.59 and 3.47 x 10^-32 cm4/W (printed 5.6,
  3.5); Eq. (4) gives 1.6961 x 10^-19 cm2.
- **Finding:** drag_2021 (TC-891) reproduces the value correctly (5.4 x 10^-45 m4,
  angular); its 'not stated' polarisation and photon statistics are linear and G^(2) = 2
  assumed; its +-50 % is the uncertainty of the measured densities, not one printed for
  sigma_0^(2); its 193.5 nm is the laser's 193.41 nm. The quoted alphas of bokor_1980
  (2.34 x 10^-31, a 25 cm-1 laser) and geohegan_1986 (TC-886, 2 x 10^-32 cm4/W, an
  off-line average for 140 cm-1) match their originals as printed.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-09).

## TC-921 bokor_1980 (Bokor, Zavelovich & Rhodes, Phys. Rev. A 21, 1453 (1980)): Kr 6p[3/2]2 photoionisation cross section at 193 nm (2026-10-09)

- **Checked:** Eqs. (1), (5) with the table's dipoles and 29 000 cm-1 give 2.73 and 2.44

## TC-925 sundholm_1994 (Sundholm, Rizzo & Jørgensen, J. Chem. Phys. 101, 4931 (1994)): MCSCF two-photon transition moments and rate constants of argon 1Se -> 1De; their convention, and the experimental comparison (2026-10-09)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/sundholm_1994.toml` (inline text points, no
  script).
- **Transcribed:** the HF and CAS oscillator strengths of argon's 1Se -> 1Po (lowest,
  3p5 4s) transition, 0.3154 and 0.3358 (p. 4933, text; two inline datasets,
  oscillator_strength, use = check). Not taken: Table III (the element S_xy of one
  component of 3p5 4p 1De: HF 9.499 and 20.467, CAS 10.424 and 27.367 au at omega_1 =
  omega_f/2 and 0.3855 au), Table IV (K in cm4 s), Tables I-II: no quantity holds them
  (two_photon_transition_strength holds the level's delta^TP, TC-872).
- **Checked:** the convention by reproduction: every K of Table IV is Eq. (2), K = a0^4
  t0 (2 pi)^3 alpha^2 omega_1 omega_2 delta^TP, with delta^TP = (4/15) S^2 (the F = G =
  H = 2 average of the xy component alone) and omega_2 from the method's Table I energy
  (0.3701, 1.1873, 0.4261, 1.9107 x 10^-51 against 0.370, 1.19, 0.426, 1.91). The
  level's delta^TP (all five components, henriksson_2005's convention, TC-888) is (4/3)
  S^2 = 5 x (4/15) S^2. Table III's columns sum to their totals; the CAS oscillator
  strength is 2 omega mu^2 from Tables I-II (the HF one gives 0.3172, not 0.3154);
  hattig_1998b's argon SCF/MCSCF 1De S^0f and K are this paper's (TC-887); the text's
  ratios (10 %, 45 %, 2.6 times, 33 %, 7 %) and closure estimate (10.40; 14.72 against
  '14.8').
- **Finding:** Table IV quotes Moccia and Rizzo's 1De K (moccia_1984: 2.16 x 10^-51 cm4
  s, reproduced from its amplitude) as 0.216 x 10^-51, and Lebedev and Yakovleva's
  (2.88 x 10^-51 from their amplitude 14.0 by the same formula) as 0.288 x 10^-51: both
  ten times too small, and the text's 'good agreement with previously calculated rate
  constants' rests on them.
- **Finding:** the computed K are one component's; the experiment (2.05 x 10^-51 cm4 s,
  the sum over the three J = 2 levels with 1De character) is the level's. Per level the
  CAS K at 0.3855 au is 9.55 x 10^-51, a factor 4.7 above experiment, not the 'excellent
  agreement' (7 %) the paper reports (as for hattig_1998b's CCSD 1.83, TC-887).
- **Finding:** the experimental parts 1.4, 0.53 and 0.12 x 10^-51 cm4 s are McCann et
  al.'s T2 (mccann_1988, Table II: 6.2, 2.2, 0.51 x 10^-35 cm4) times t0 (Eq. 4): the
  second and third reproduce (0.532, 0.123), the first does not (1.500 against 1.4); the
  sum is 2.16, not 2.05. T2 uses G = 1/Delta, not a normalised line shape (mccann_1988).
- **Doubt:** Table II's 1Po contributions S_1Po do not follow from its mu and Table I's
  energies (implied factors 0.83-0.97); the text's '13%-16%' is 14.6-19.3 % by Tables
  II-III. 'Less than 5%' uncertainty (CAS) is the authors' judgement.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-09).

  0.006 85 au; the text prints 0.6936 +- 0.0068: the uncertainty reproduces, the value

## TC-927 moccia_1984 (Moccia & Rizzo, Mol. Phys. 51, 1095 (1984)): RPA two-photon amplitudes and rate parameters of Ne and Ar, not taken; their convention (2026-10-09)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/moccia_1984.toml` (notes only).
- **Transcribed:** nothing. The paper prints amplitudes M (Tables 2-3; LG Ne 2p5 3p 1Se
  4.514, 1De 3.836, Ar 3p5 4p 1Se 14.907, 1De 12.149 au) and rate parameters K in cm4 s
  (Table 4; Figs. 1-5, scanned images, K against omega_1), for parallel linear
  polarisation, with experimental (LS-averaged) energies for the final and first 1Po
  levels. M is an amplitude (delta^TP = |M|^2 would be a derived value), K no quantity.
- **Checked:** every EMM K of Table 4 (Ne and Ar, 1Se and 1De, LG and VG) from Table 3's
  M by Eq. (6), K = (2 pi)^3 alpha^2 omega_1^g omega_2^g |M|^2 x 1.8967e-50 cm4 s, with
  omega = half of Table 1's experimental energy (worst 0.32 %); M = M^d + M^c in every
  column; Table 2's 'This work' is Table 3 rounded (table images checked).
- **Finding (convention):** M is the zz amplitude of the final level's M = 0 component
  for parallel linear polarisation, so |M|^2 is the level's strength: for 1Se, S_zz^2 =
  delta^TP (F = G = H = 2); for 1De, (4/3) S_xy^2, henriksson_2005's per-level
  convention (TC-888), five times the one-component values of sundholm_1994 and

  prints 2.16(-51). hettema_1992 compares the Ne 1De 3.84 with its S_xy without the
  factor 2/sqrt 3.

## TC-931 chang_1982 (Chang & Kim, Phys. Rev. A 26, 2728 (1982)): photoionisation cross sections of the excited np5 mp (1S) states of Ne, Ar, Kr and Xe (2026-10-09)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/chang_1982.toml`, `tools/extract/chang_1982.py`
  (Table II, text, raster figures).
- **Transcribed:** a single-configuration calculation (hole-corrected Hartree-Fock
  effective Hamiltonian), LS-coupled J = 0 states, as
  `excited_state_photoionization_cross_section` (TC-872), all use = check except as
  noted. Table II (p. 2731), the length form (p. 2732): Ne 3p 2.0 and Xe 6p 6.9 Mb at
  308 nm, Ar 4p 4.8 and Kr 5p 4.5 Mb at 248 nm; its Duzy and Hyman column (Phys. Rev.
  A 22, 1978 (1980), not in the library) as use = reproduced. The text's Kr 6p, 7.4e-19
  cm2 at 193.5 nm (velocity), inline. Figs. 1-4 (raster scans, velocity form, against
  the photoelectron energy, log-log): Ne 3p, Ar 4p, Kr 5p, Kr 6p and Xe 6p, read by the
  script from the page images (per-side decade calibration, decades within 5 pixels,
  every minor tick within 10; the curves taken by rank where four runs are resolved),
  from 0.6-0.9 eV (Ar, Kr, Xe; below, the curves merge) or 2.6 eV (Ne; they cross near
  1 eV) to 52-60 eV, 8 % uncertainty. The photon energy is the photoelectron energy
  plus the calculation's binding energy Ry / n*^2 from Table I (a conversion the record
  states; not shifted to experimental thresholds). Tables checked against the images;
  overlays (points and the calibrated decade grid on the page images) inspected.
- **Checked:** Table II (length) against the figures (velocity) at the same
  wavelength: Ar 4p 0.97, Kr 5p 0.99 (the paper's 10 % between the forms), Xe 6p 0.89
  ('larger' for Xe); Ne 3p lies in the crossing region, not read.
- **Finding:** Fig. 3's Kr 6p curve at 193.5 nm reads 8.2e-19 cm2, 1.10 times the
  text's 7.4e-19 (both velocity); the experimental J = 0 threshold changes the reading
  by 1.8 % only. Unresolved; both kept. geohegan_1986 (TC-886) quotes 'Chang and Kim'
  as 8.0e-19 (within 2 % of the figure, not the text) and cites page 2278 for 2728.
  kroll_1990 (TC-890) quotes this paper for Xe 6p as 3.7 (248 nm) and 1.8e-18 (193 nm),
  values the paper does not print: Fig. 4 gives 3.47 and 1.74 Mb (velocity), the
  length form about 13 % more; consistent with this calculation (figure or the
  authors' tabulation). pindzola_1981 is cited with a wrong initial and page ('M. A.
  Pindzola, 23, 20').

  of Figs. 1-4; Fig. 5 (wave functions), Fig. 6 (beta, no quantity).
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-09).

## TC-932 pindzola_1981 (Pindzola, Phys. Rev. A 23, 201 (1981)): Hartree-Fock and Dirac-Fock photoionisation cross sections of Xe 6p[1/2]0, partial and total, length and velocity (2026-10-09)

## TC-933 hyman_1977 (Hyman, Appl. Phys. Lett. 31, 14 (1977)): photoionisation cross sections of the excited Ar(4s, 4p) and Kr(5s, 5p) configuration averages at 2486 A (2026-10-09)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/hyman_1977.toml`, `tools/extract/hyman_1977.py`.
- **Transcribed:** Table I (p. 15), one value each, at 'lambda = 2486 A' (KrF; air or
  vacuum not said): Ar(4s) 2.1e-20, Ar(4p) 4.3e-18, Kr(5s) 1.3e-19, Kr(5p) 4.5e-18 cm2,
  as `excited_state_photoionization_cross_section` (TC-872), all use = check. A
  central-field model (Hartree-Fock ion potential plus a polarisation potential, no
  spin-orbit) of levels averaged over J and over the two core states; the s states
  include the 3P0,2 metastables and 'the two 3P1 levels' (p. 14, as printed). The
  library's cells are an OCR of the scan ('4. 3x 10-18'), kept in `printed`; checked
  against the table image. No uncertainty stated; the s-state values are 'very
  sensitive to the details of the model' (p. 15).
- **Checked:** the text's repetitions (Ar 4p 4.3e-18, the abstract's ~4.5e-18). Figs. 2
  and 3 (raster, sigma against the excess energy epsilon) read by the script from the
  page images (per-side tick calibration, every tick within 3 pixels): Table I lies on
  the 4p and 5p curves at epsilon = 0.167 and 0.170 Ry, implying binding energies of
  2.72 (Ar 4p) and 2.68 eV (Kr 5p) (+-0.03 eV) with the paper's 1 Ry = 13.6 eV;
  overlays inspected.
- **Finding:** dakka_2018 (TC-892) quotes 3.3e-18 cm2 for Kr 2p6 at 215 nm 'Calculated
  from' this paper: Fig. 3's 5p curve 0.0573 Ry above Table I's point gives 3.39e-18
  (dakka/read 0.97), so the quotation is this configuration average carried along Fig.
  3, within the reading. chang_1982's Table II reproduces the later Duzy and Hyman
  values (5.4, 5.2 Mb at 248 nm), 26 and 16 % above this paper's.
- **Not taken:** Figs. 2-3 as data (no threshold of the averaged levels is printed, so
  no photon energy); Dunning and Stebbings's threshold bounds (Phys. Rev. A 9, 2378
  (1974), not in the library); the renormalised Ar(4s) ~1.5e-19.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-09).

## TC-935 drake_1969 (Drake, Victor & Dalgarno, Phys. Rev. 180, 25 (1969)): two-photon decay rates of the 2 1S0 and 2 3S1 levels of He-like ions; no values taken (2026-10-09)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/drake_1969.toml` (notes only, no datasets).
- **Transcribed:** nothing. The paper gives spontaneous two-photon emission rates (s^-1)
  and their photon-energy distributions, He I to Ne IX (variational, nonrelativistic,
  infinite nuclear mass); no quantity of the vocabulary (TC-872) holds a decay rate, and
  the rates are not converted into a two-photon strength or cross section. The helium
  values are recorded in the notes: 2 1S0 A = 5.13 x 10^1 s^-1, lambda_max 771 A
  (Table I, p. 29); 2 3S1 A = 4.02 x 10^-9 s^-1, lambda_max 699 and 2400 A (Table III,
  p. 30); both checked against the table images.
- **Checked:** Simpson's rule over the He columns of the distributions (Tables II, IV,
  y = 0-0.5) gives 51.15 s^-1 (Table I 51.3, -0.3 %) and 4.04 x 10^-9 s^-1 (Table III
  4.02 x 10^-9, +0.5 %): the tables give the rate per unit y counting each photon of a
  pair, the total being the integral over half the range (Eq. 2). The wavelength peaks
  from the distributions and NIST's level energies: 761 A (printed 771; the peak is
  flat to 0.1 % over that interval) and 700, 2344 A (printed 699, 2400).
- **Finding:** see bondy_2020: 51.3 s^-1 is 0.54 % above bondy_2020's infinite-mass
  51.0233 s^-1, and the other ions' rates differ from bondy_2020's by -0.39 to +0.49 %,
  more than the paper's 'converged to the number of figures quoted'.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-09).

## TC-936 bondy_2020 (Bondy, Morton & Drake, Phys. Rev. A 102, 052807 (2020)): two-photon decay rate of He 2 1S0 with finite nuclear mass; no values taken; comparison with drake_1969 (2026-10-09)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/bondy_2020.toml` (notes only, no datasets).
- **Transcribed:** nothing; no quantity holds a decay rate (TC-872). Recorded in the
  notes, for 4He 2 1S0 -> 1 1S0 (Tables II, IV, V, VI, images checked): w_inf =
  51.023 3210(5) s^-1 (nonrelativistic, infinite mass), the finite-mass correction
  -0.015 617 48, the relativistic estimate -0.08(7), total 50.93(7) s^-1 (Derevianko and
  Johnson 51.02); w/alpha^6 = 8.170 693 021 30(21) x 10^-3 au (velocity), length form
  equal to 1.2 x 10^-8; peak rate 72.562 3228 s^-1 per unit y at 120.2628 nm.
- **Checked:** w_inf/alpha^6 x 6242.763420 s^-1 reproduces Table VI's w_inf (51.023 321)
  and the finite-mass corrections of 4He and 3He (-0.015 617 5, -0.020 725 9); the peak
  wavelength is 2 / Delta.
- **Finding:** drake_1969 (same approximation) gives 51.3 s^-1 for He, 0.54 % above w_inf
  = 51.0233; its Li II to Ne IX rates differ from Table VI's w_inf by +0.49, -0.39,
  +0.48, +0.23, -0.26, -0.14, +0.23, -0.36 %, errors of a few units of the third figure
  where drake_1969 says its results converged to the figures quoted. drake_1969's He
  distribution peak, 1.45 x 10^2 s^-1, is twice this paper's 72.562 within its rounding,
  as the text says (drake_1969's table counts both photons). The paper gives no 2 3S1
  rate (drake_1969: 4.02 x 10^-9 s^-1); it quotes a triplet-to-singlet ratio of 6.2 x
  10^-11 (Derevianko and Johnson) without saying which rates it divides (drake_1969's
  ratio is 7.8 x 10^-11).
- **Doubt:** three misprints in the text, none affecting a value: 'total rate of 50.093
  s^-1' for Table VI's 50.93; Sec. V's wavelengths in 'um' are nm or angstrom
  ('601.40 um' is 601.40 A, 1e8 / 166 277.44 cm^-1); the lifetimes 5.178(45) x 10^-4 s
  and 1.9634(28) x 10^-2 s are attributed to He and 7Li+ respectively, the reverse of
  1/w (1/50.93 s^-1 = 1.9635 x 10^-2 s for He, 1/1938.8 s^-1 = 5.158 x 10^-4 s for
  7Li+); 5.178(45) is not 1/1938.8(17) (5.158(5)): unexplained.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-09).

## TC-937 payne_1981 (Payne et al., Chem. Phys. Lett. 79, 142 (1981)): photoionisation cross sections of two-photon-excited np5 n'p[1/2]0 levels of Ar, Kr, Xe (estimates) (2026-10-09)

  (cm2) quoted in the text (pp. 145-146, rendered pages read): Ar 3p5 4p[1/2]0 at 1576 A,
  ~1 x 10^-18; Kr 4p5 6p[1/2]0 at 1927.48 A, ~5 x 10^-19 (Ref. 9, Pindzola, unpublished);
  Kr 4p5 5p[1/2]0 at 3262 A, 10^-18; Xe 5p5 6p[1/2]0 at 2496 A, ~3 x 10^-18 (Ref. 9). All
  use = check; the two Ref. 9 values reproduced_from Pindzola (unpublished); no
  uncertainty stated. Wavelengths in vacuum (2 x 1e8 / 1927.48 A = 103 762.4 cm^-1
  against NIST's Kr 6p[1/2]0, 103 761.63; air would be 1926.9 A).

  3.05 x 10^-18 cm2 (DF length); the 3 x 10^-18 here is the largest form. Kr 6p against
  bokor_1980: (3.2 +- 2.0) x 10^-19 cm2, but for 6p[3/2]2 at 193.49 nm.

## TC-939 palm_1998 (Palm & Merkt, Appl. Phys. Lett. 73, 157 (1998)): resonant four-wave mixing in Ar beyond 19 eV via the 4p[5/2]2 two-photon resonance; no values taken (2026-10-09)

- **Where:** `src/optmat/data/sources/palm_1998.toml` (notes only, no datasets).
- **Transcribed:** nothing: the paper reports XUV output (photons per pulse, ~10^-6
  conversion, 0.1 cm^-1 bandwidth) and relative signals. The Ar 3p5 4p[5/2]2 resonance
  (2 nu = 105 617.3 cm^-1) is Moore's (1949), reproduced.
- **Checked:** the resonance positions named (Ar 189.3, 186.8, 184.0 nm; Kr 212.5, 202.3,
  192.7 nm) are NIST's levels as vacuum wavelengths (2/105 617.27 ... 2/103 761.63 cm^-1);
  the XUV energies 18.32, 18.76, 19.64 and 'up to 19.66' eV follow from 105 617.3
  cm^-1 and the stated second-laser wavelengths. Not reproduced: the Kr 192.7 nm
  resonance's limit '155 700 cm^-1 (19.3 eV)'; with the same 189 nm limit it would be
  156 672 cm^-1 (19.42 eV). The page prints '10-20 uJ' where the text layer has 'mJ'.
- **Finding:** compared with rupper_2004 (TC-900), the same group's later laser: there
  the J = 0 argon resonances 4p[1/2]0 and 4p'[1/2]0, which this paper expected to
  improve the conversion, give 3.3 and 6.3 times the four-wave-mixing output of the
  4p[5/2]2 resonance used here (rupper_2004 Table I, 4.0(12) and 7.5(24) against 1.2(2)),
  much less than the factor of about 100 between krypton's J = 2 and J = 0 resonances
  quoted here, and the Kr 6p[1/2]0 resonance gave 45 times the XUV signal of Ar 4p[5/2]2.
  Neither paper gives a two-photon cross section.
- **Status:** verified (2026-10-09).
